The models include radioactive energy deposition from 56Co, 57Co, and 44Ti, with explicit treatment of gamma-ray transport, positron slowing-down, and the coupling of non-thermal electrons to excitation and ionization. We incorporate time-dependent terms in the rate and energy equations, charge-exchange reactions, and a parameterized description of mixing and clumping motivated by hydrodynamic instabilities. Late-time spectra and photometry of SN 1987A (days ~300–3000) are used to calibrate the thermal and ionization histories and to test the sensitivity of key diagnostics to ejecta structure. We reproduce the observed evolution of prominent nebular lines, including [O I] λλ6300, 6364, [Ca II] λλ7291, 7324, [Fe II] near-infrared transitions, and select [Si I] and [Ni II] features, and we show that time dependence is essential to match both line ratios and absolute fluxes beyond ~500 days. Steady-state approximations systematically underpredict the strength of low-ionization lines and overestimate temperatures, demonstrating the role of recombination freeze-out and non-thermal excitation. We derive the oxygen mass by modeling the [O I] doublet fluxes and profiles, accounting for optical-depth effects, collisional de-excitation, and contamination from neighboring lines. The allowed range depends on the degree of clumping and mixing with radioactive material; within our favored models, the oxygen mass in the inner ejecta is constrained to be of order one solar mass, consistent with a ~15–20 M⊙ progenitor and nucleosynthesis expectations. Line-profile analyses further reveal the macroscopic distribution of elements, with broadened and asymmetric wings indicating extensive Rayleigh–Taylor mixing and a heterogeneous density field; these profiles provide independent constraints on the spatial co-location of oxygen with iron-group nuclei that control local heating. We discuss complementary approaches to determine the 44Ti mass that powers the luminosity at very late epochs: (1) fitting the bolometric light-curve tail with time-dependent deposition and thermalization, (2) detailed spectral synthesis of iron-group lines and continuum constrained by positron transport and trapping, and (3) comparison with hard X-ray/γ-ray limits on the 44Ti decay lines. Applying these methods to SN 1987A yields a consistent 44Ti mass of a few ×10^-4 M⊙, with uncertainties dominated by positron escape and dust reprocessing. Our results underscore that reliable inferences of elemental yields and ejecta structure require time-dependent treatments and line-profile information, and they provide robust constraints for progenitor and explosion models of SN 1987A and related events.

Using a sample of nine giant elliptical galaxies, we compare the projected radial distributions of their red (metal-rich) and blue (metal-poor) globular cluster (GC) subpopulations with the host galaxies’ stellar and X-ray surface brightness profiles. Consistent with prior work, we find that the surface density of red GCs closely follows the stellar light at all radii, reinforcing their association with the bulge/spheroid component. In contrast, the outer slope of the blue GC surface density agrees well with that of the X-ray emission, suggesting a common equilibrium within the same gravitational potential. After deprojection, the radial density of the hot, X-ray–emitting gas scales as the square root of the GC density profile, as expected if the gas and blue GCs trace the dark-matter–dominated halo in different dynamical states. Energetics further support this picture: the specific energy of blue GCs is roughly half that of the hot gas. These results strengthen the link between blue GCs and the outer halo and provide constraints on mass profiles, dynamical equilibrium, and the formation pathways of giant ellipticals.

We extend our earlier framework, in which a generalized entropy functional provides a monotonic time-direction for dynamics generated by a Markov generator, to open systems with external pumping and loss. We model populations injected from unaccounted levels, transported through the coupled manifold, and removed by decay to states outside the system, and derive the corresponding equation of motion. We show how the formalism maps onto the previous treatment and identify conditions under which a suitably defined Lyapunov functional remains monotonic despite sources and sinks. The physical implications—nonconserved normalization, steady-state flux balance, and approach to stationarity—are analyzed. Numerical simulations of a standard two-level system with pumping and relaxation illustrate the theory, revealing the transient and steady-state behavior and confirming the generalized entropy’s role as an arrow-of-time indicator. The results establish a unified description of closed and pumped-relaxing Markovian dynamics.

We conduct a detailed case study of the interstellar shell surrounding the high‐mass X‐ray binary Cygnus X‐1. The combined diagnostics place physically motivated constraints on the shock and on the ambient interstellar medium it is plowing through. Emission‐line ratios and line widths indicate a slow, radiative shock propagating at less than a few hundred km s−1 into a low‐density medium (number density ≲ 1 cm−3). The absence of thermal X‐ray emission from the shell, together with the optical line luminosities, yields a robust upper limit on the time‐averaged mechanical power required to drive the shock and inflate the bubble, of order 10^36–10^37 erg s−1. We evaluate possible origins for the shell and find a supernova remnant scenario to be disfavored by the energetics, morphology, and lack of ejecta signatures. In contrast, the black‐hole jet and/or the O‐star wind associated with Cygnus X‐1 can plausibly account for the observed properties, individually or in concert. While our analysis tightens the constraints on the shock and environment, the ultimate driver of the Cygnus X‐1 shockwave remains unsettled, motivating deeper, spatially resolved multiwavelength observations.

We investigate the entropy dynamics of piecewise affine surface homeomorphisms. Our approach constructs a jump transformation based on chosen good returns, replacing first-return schemes and obviating the need for Markov partitions. Entropy and ergodic control yield recurrence and expansivity along good returns, enabling symbolic coding and counting estimates. These results advance the understanding of piecewise affine models and their relevance to smooth surface diffeomorphisms.

This work investigates sending two correlated vector Gaussian sources over a bandwidth-matched, two-user scalar Gaussian broadcast channel, where each receiver reconstructs its designated source subject to covariance distortion constraints. We establish a lower bound on the optimal tradeoff between transmit power and the achievable pair of reconstruction distortions. The bound is obtained via a new converse technique that introduces constructed remote sources to tighten mutual-information inequalities. For the special case in which the weak receiver targets a scalar source under mean-squared error distortion, we prove that the lower bound is tight and is achieved by a class of hybrid digital–analog schemes. The results clarify power–distortion limits and guide the design of source–channel codes.

We investigate integer additive set-indexers (IASIs) on graphs, where an injective vertex labeling by finite subsets of the nonnegative integers induces an injective edge labeling via sumsets. We establish structural conditions under which the edge corona of G1 and G2 admits a weak IASI, expressed in terms of the distribution of mono-indexed (singleton-labeled) vertices and edges in the factor graphs and their interaction through the corona construction. Building on these criteria, we derive general bounds and exact values for the sparing number, defined as the minimum number of singleton set-labeled edges needed for the graph to admit an IASI, for broad families of edge coronas. In particular, we provide closed formulas or tight bounds for edge coronas involving paths, cycles, complete graphs, bipartite graphs, trees, and certain regular graphs, along with explicit labeling schemes that realize these bounds. The results unify and extend known cases, yield sharp threshold phenomena for weak IASI admissibility, and highlight how degree distributions and factor graph structure govern sparing numbers in edge corona products.

Asymmetric magnetic reconnection at the magnetopause often proceeds through the formation and rapid merging of magnetic islands, yet the associated electron dynamics remain incompletely characterized. The upper layer is an asymmetric Harris sheet of finite width, initially perturbed to promote a single reconnection site. The lower layer is a tangential discontinuity that naturally generates multiple X-points and rapidly merging islands. In both layers the magnetic field and density exhibit strong jumps while the total pressure is held constant, allowing a controlled comparison of reconnection regimes. We evaluate the parallel and perpendicular components of the electron temperature to assess energization pathways and diagnose anisotropies and non-gyrotropic behavior. The direct comparison between the two layers enables the identification of three distinct regions. First, regions of traditional asymmetric reconnection evolve without island merging and display canonical signatures of electron heating and agyrotropy localized near the primary X-line. Second, regions where reconnection occurs between two merging islands show enhanced electron energization and pronounced temperature anisotropies coincident with the coalescence front. Third, regions between two diverging islands lack typical reconnection signatures yet exhibit a characteristic flat-top electron velocity distribution. This distribution arises from the saturation of a two-stream instability driven by the interaction of electron beams emanating from the two nearest reconnection points. An agyrotropy analysis further reveals a robust double structure extending over the lower side facing the stronger magnetic field; this structure transitions to a quadrupolar morphology in the vicinity of the third-type regions. The distinguishing temperature anisotropies, non-gyrotropic patterns, flat-top distributions, and agyrotropy topology provide clear, testable indicators for the Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) mission to identify magnetopause reconnection involving multiple islands and to disentangle electron energization mechanisms during rapid island merging.

We report the first experimental determination of the third moment of voltage fluctuations in a conductor, revealing new, complementary insights into electronic transport beyond traditional noise spectra. Using non-superconducting tunnel junctions, we measure the third moment versus bias, temperature, and bandwidths up to 1 GHz. The results show strong sensitivity to the sample’s electromagnetic environment, establishing calibration strategies and quantitative benchmarks for higher-order fluctuation measurements in mesoscopic conductors.

We investigate localized modes in binary Bose–Einstein condensates loaded into one-dimensional optical lattices, modeled by coupled Gross–Pitaevskii equations. When one component dominates, we develop a systematic construction by treating the minority component as a small field bifurcating from the linear band–gap spectrum of the lattice around a pinned state of the dominant component. Numerical continuation and Bogoliubov–de Gennes analysis trace the branches and their stability, corroborated by direct simulations. Extending the approach with symmetry considerations for components of comparable size but different parities yields robust time-periodic breather modes. We chart parameter regimes of stability, identify symmetry-breaking transitions, and discuss implications for experiments and setups.

We show that the Jordan–Wigner transformation maps a one-dimensional spin system to spinless fermions; extending to a double chain of qubits with intra-chain J1 and inter-chain J2 couplings realizes a spinful 1D Fermi–Hubbard model. To build confidence in simulated observables, we propose verification protocols using measurements of local operators, including densities, spin correlations, and currents, with comparison to numerics on small instances. Our results chart a path toward emulation of strongly correlated fermions in scalable hardware.

We extend the master stability framework to delay-coupled, non-smooth dynamical systems and use it to analyze zero‐lag and cluster synchrony in networks of adaptive threshold-model neurons. We further generalize the approach to two subpopulations with nonidentical local dynamics, including bursting, and show that activity-based adaptation governs the stability of cluster states independent of connectivity details. Analytical predictions are corroborated by numerical simulations, providing a unified tool for dissecting synchrony in hybrid neuronal networks.

This paper develops a general framework for discrete observation of (marked) point processes under high-frequency sampling. The limit inherits the immigration–birth branching structure, yielding precise identification of the baseline intensity, excitation kernel, and mark law in terms of the thinning coefficients and innovation distribution of the RCINAR(∞) model. This result rigorously interprets RCINAR(∞) processes as discretely observed marked Hawkes processes in the high-frequency limit, thereby bridging discrete-time time-series analysis and continuous-time stochastic-process methodology and offering a new perspective on point-process approaches in extreme value theory. Second, we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for the stationarity of RCINAR(∞) processes, linking it to the subcriticality of the random thinning mechanism, and derive an equivalent random-coefficient autoregressive (RCAR) representation that facilitates estimation and structural interpretation. A simulation study corroborates the predicted asymptotic regime, examines finite-sample behavior, and highlights implications for inference, including estimation accuracy, model selection, and diagnostics in high-frequency extreme-value applications. Keywords: peaks over threshold, extreme value theory, marked Hawkes process, high-frequency data, RCINAR(∞) process.

We investigate the metal–insulator transition in a quantum site-percolation model on the simple cubic lattice with a binary distribution of onsite energies. Using a high-precision transfer-matrix approach, we compute the Landauer conductance for wide ranges of energy and disorder (ratio of insulating sites), perform finite-size scaling, and map the mobility edge in the disorder–energy plane. The resulting phase boundary yields an extremal critical disorder notably closer to the classical percolation threshold than previously reported. Along the entire mobility edge, the critical exponent for the localization length remains constant and matches that of the three-dimensional Anderson transition, supporting a common universality class. A possible exception arises at the band center, where either single-parameter scaling breaks down or finite-size effects dominate. This interpretation is reinforced by the pronounced disparity between arithmetic and geometric conductance averages at special energies: only the geometric mean produces a vanishing critical disorder at the band center, in agreement with theoretical predictions. These results refine the phase diagram.

We investigate a ring of FitzHugh–Nagumo excitable elements coupled in a phase-repulsive fashion and driven by a subthreshold global oscillatory signal in the presence of independent Gaussian white noises. Using numerical integration of the stochastic dynamics and complementary linear-response estimates, we quantify entrainment via phase-locking statistics, spectral amplification, cross-correlation, and a collective order parameter. Without noise, the subthreshold signal fails to entrain the ring. At intermediate noise intensities, however, the network exhibits robust 1:1 phase locking to the drive, enhanced coherence resonance, and an alternating spatial pattern imposed by repulsive coupling. The synchronization window depends nonmonotonically on noise strength, coupling, and signal frequency, with finite-size scaling demonstrating robustness across system sizes. Excessive noise disrupts coherence, while weak noise yields insufficient activation. We elucidate a mechanism in which noise-induced excitations are temporally biased by the common drive and organized by repulsive interactions. Results highlight a synergistic interplay between topology, excitability, and stochastic forcing, with implications for rhythm control in excitable media and neural circuits.

We propose a new mechanism for baryogenesis via leptogenesis in which the CP violation responsible for the lepton asymmetry is directly linked to the low-energy CP phases of the PMNS neutrino mixing matrix. The framework assumes that the full theory contains only a single CP-violating parameter, arising from the complex vacuum expectation value of a Standard Model singlet. Leptogenesis proceeds while electroweak symmetry is broken, and the dominant CP asymmetry is generated by a new loop diagram with an intermediate boson exchange that explicitly involves the PMNS matrix elements and phases. We term this setup type-II leptogenesis. We analyze the conditions under which washout remains under control and sphaleron conversion is efficient, and we provide an estimate of the maximally attainable baryon asymmetry as a function of the PMNS phases. The scenario yields testable correlations between the observed baryon asymmetry and neutrino CP measurements.

We introduce a basic definition of algebraic entropy for lattice equations, furnishing a canonical measure of the complexity of the discrete dynamics they generate. Extending the well-established notion of algebraic entropy for rational maps, we formulate entropies for multidimensional recurrences defined on lattices, in analogy to the passage from ordinary to partial differential equations. Our construction is based on the growth rate of algebraic degrees of iterates with respect to natural spaces of initial data, and accommodates distinct propagation directions. We show that vanishing entropy is a robust signature of integrability, and that nonzero entropies often take remarkable values, suggestive of algebraic integers. We describe the setting, the choice of initial staircases and patches, the associated evolutions, and the extraction of asymptotic growth from a finite number of iterates. A selection of examples, including integrable lattice equations and nonintegrable ones, illustrates the effectiveness of the entropy in detecting integrability and in quantifying global behavior efficiently. Our results formalize and confirm prior observations for maps and lattice systems, unify them in a common framework, and clarify connections between local update rules and global complexity. We outline practical procedures for entropy estimation from symbolic iterates. We conclude with conjectures and perspectives concerning universality, invariance properties, and the arithmetic nature of entropies, and discuss implications for the broader analysis of discrete dynamical systems.

We investigate the composition dependence of Yb valence and thermal expansion in the intermetallic YbGa_xGe_y. High-resolution X‐ray diffraction confirms single‐phase samples isostructural to YbGaGe over a narrow homogeneity range. Magnetic susceptibility is nearly temperature independent below room temperature and lacks a Curie tail, indicating a robust divalent Yb state throughout the studied compositions. Temperature-dependent diffraction shows that lattice parameters and unit-cell volumes decrease monotonically on cooling, demonstrating the absence of the previously reported zero thermal expansion in YbGaGe. The Yb valence does not vary measurably with composition, and no intermediate‐valence behavior is detected. These results clarify the intrinsic thermophysical properties of YbGa_xGe_y materials intermetallic.

We develop a series-based technique inspired by separation of variables to solve Cauchy problems for linear PDEs with initial data given as trigonometric, power, or exponential series. The method expands the solution in matching series and derives closed recurrences for modal coefficients, enabling treatment of many non-separable LPDEs, including classes of second-order elliptic equations and the Stokes system. Under explicit coefficient and regularity conditions, we prove convergence of the constructed series and obtain stability and uniqueness. The approach yields solutions expressed uniformly as trigonometric, power, or exponential series and recovers the classical separation method in separable cases. Furthermore, combining power/exponential series with an iterative scheme, we extend the framework to broader LPDEs and certain nonlinear PDEs, providing first solutions for several models.

We generalize the Kuramoto model by allowing oscillator natural frequencies to undergo Ornstein–Uhlenbeck dynamics, motivated by recent observations of time-varying frequencies in circadian cell populations. In the continuum limit of infinitely many oscillators, we derive the Fokker–Planck equation and perform an exact linear stability analysis of the incoherent state. We obtain an expression for the critical coupling at which incoherence loses stability, expressed in terms of the inverse relaxation rate of the frequency drift and the asymptotic frequency dispersion. In the fast-frequency limit (large relaxation rate), the threshold coincides with the noisy Kuramoto (Smoluchowski) model. As the relaxation rate decreases, the critical coupling grows slowly relative to phase-diffusive theory. An asymptotic expansion in the slow-drift limit shows that the noiseless Kuramoto model with a Gaussian frequency distribution is recovered. Varying a single parameter yields a smooth interpolation between regimes dominated by phase diffusion and frequency dispersion.

We present the first high-resolution ultraviolet spectra toward Herschel 36, a Trapezium-like system of high-mass stars embedded in the Lagoon Nebula (M8, NGC 6523). The spectra reveal extreme ro-vibrational excitation of molecular hydrogen (H2) in absorption arising from material confined to a single velocity component, or a narrow range of velocities, which we infer to lie near the stellar system and to be dominated by fluorescent pumping. The overall H2 excitation is comparable to, but apparently higher than, that observed toward HD 37903, previously the benchmark for the largest vibrationally excited H2 column densities detected in UV absorption. Remarkably, while the highly excited H2 lines are internally consistent in velocity within each epoch, they exhibit an approximately 60 km s−1 redshift over the 3.6 years separating the observations. In neither epoch does the velocity of the highly excited component match that of the bulk line-of-sight gas, which appears largely foreground to M8. Evidence from excited CH and CH+ absorption and several broad diffuse interstellar bands toward Herschel 36 supports an extreme, irradiated, and dynamic environment within ~0.1 pc of the massive young stellar system. These findings reveal the conditions in the immediate vicinity of young, high-mass stars and constrain molecular excitation and kinematics in photon-dominated regions.

We present single-site time-series photometry of the pulsating pre-white dwarf PG 0122+200 and analyze its frequency spectrum. The detected pulsations form a pattern of modes nearly equally spaced in period, and both the observed period range and mean spacing identify PG 0122+200 as an l=1 g-mode pulsator, resembling patterns seen in multi-site campaigns on PG 2131+066 and PG 1159-035. Using the measured period spacing together with the spectroscopic effective temperature, we infer a stellar mass more tightly constrained than permitted by published surface-gravity estimates; comparison with evolutionary and pulsation models yields M ≈ 0.66–0.72 M⊙. Fine structure in the power spectrum reveals rotational multiplets consistent with a rotation period of 1.6 days. Future multi-site observations, such as with the Whole Earth Telescope, should refine the spacings, resolve more components, and yield constraints on internal structure and rotation. These findings confirm PG 0122+200 as a PG 1159-type pre-white dwarf and show that single-site campaigns can yield robust asteroseismic constraints.

We evaluate the Pfaffian model for the 5/2 fractional quantum Hall state by benchmarking its quasihole sector against exact diagonalization for interactions. We analyze the low-energy spectra, overlaps of trial states, particle–hole symmetry, degeneracy splittings, and signatures of off-diagonal long-range order. Our results delineate the regime of validity and limitations of Pfaffian quasiholes and clarify the impact of perturbations. We also review alternative descriptions of the 5/2 FQHE that do not invoke Pfaffian physics, highlighting competing mechanisms, and discuss consequences for non-Abelian braiding statistics.

Decoy-state quantum key distribution (QKD) is a standard tool for long-distance quantum communications, yet its performance critically depends on how decoy-state statistics are processed under finite-key effects. We propose and analyze a practical CLT-based methodology for estimating key security parameters from decoy-state data, explicitly integrating the failure probability of statistical estimates into the overall protocol failure probability. Our approach systematically accounts for deviations between binomially distributed observables and their Gaussian approximations, providing corrected confidence intervals and conservative bounds without sacrificing tightness. We present numerical simulations across realistic operating regimes, including varying channel losses and intensities, demonstrating that the resulting parameter estimates and secure key rates closely match exact finite-size analyses while reducing computational overhead. The technique is simple to implement, compatible with existing post-processing pipelines, and suitable for industrial QKD systems requiring transparent, auditable finite-key accounting and tunable reliability guarantees today.

We present ISO SWS infrared spectroscopy of the bright reflection nebula NGC 7023 from 7.0 to 8.7 micrometers, searching for fullerene features. Expected vibrational bands of ionized C60+ occur at 7.11 and 7.51 micrometers, and neutral C60 at 7.0 and 8.45 micrometers. No significant emission is detected at these wavelengths; modeling line strengths with laboratory cross sections and the local radiation field yields stringent upper limits: C60+ at most 0.26% and C60 at most 0.27% of interstellar carbon. These constraints inform the carbon budget and processing of PAHs and fullerenes in illuminated photodissociation regions.

We report the discovery of an extremely red planetary-mass companion to the late-K dwarf 2MASS J22362452+4751425 (2M2236+4751), whose kinematics are consistent with membership in the ~120 Myr AB Doradus moving group. Multi-epoch adaptive optics imaging with NIRC2 at Keck Observatory reveals a comoving companion at a projected separation of 3.7 arcsec, corresponding to 230 ± 20 au at the kinematic distance of 63 ± 5 pc. Assuming AB Doradus age and membership, evolutionary models yield an inferred mass of 11–14 MJup for 2M2236+4751 b. Follow-up Keck/OSIRIS K-band spectroscopy shows pronounced CO absorption typical of faint, very red L dwarfs and a lack of detectable methane despite an estimated effective temperature of 900–1200 K, indicating thick photospheric clouds and potentially disequilibrium chemistry that suppresses CH4 at these temperatures. Near-infrared photometry demonstrates extreme redness, with J−K = 2.69 ± 0.12 mag. The continuum slope is redder than that of all four HR 8799 planets and closely resembles the 23 Myr isolated planetary-mass object PSO J318.5−22, implying that similarly thick cloud decks can persist in the atmospheres of giant planets well beyond 100 Myr. In near-infrared color–magnitude diagrams, 2M2236+4751 b lies at the tip of the red L-dwarf sequence and appears to delineate the “elbow” in the AB Doradus substellar isochrone, marking the transition from low-gravity L dwarfs to the cooler, young T-dwarf track. 2M2236+4751 b is the reddest known substellar companion to a star and offers a crucial benchmark for testing atmospheric models across the L/T transition at low gravity and intermediate ages. Its combination of youth, wide separation, and extreme colors provides a unique opportunity to investigate cloud evolution, chemistry, and the shared atmospheric properties of young, low-mass brown dwarfs and directly imaged extrasolar giant planets.

We investigate the extreme growth of fundamental quadratic quantities in hydrodynamic models by examining the sharpness of upper bounds for the classical and fractional enstrophy in the fractional Burgers equation. Considering subcritical, critical, and supercritical dissipation regimes, we first derive rigorous estimates for the instantaneous rates of enstrophy growth and then assess their optimality. By solving suitably constrained maximization problems with gradient-based numerical optimization, we identify families of initial data that maximize the rate of growth subject to fixed enstrophy. The resulting maximizers saturate the analytical upper bounds, up to regime-independent numerical prefactors, as the enstrophy increases, thereby establishing the sharpness of the estimates. A central outcome is that the power-law dependence of the maximal enstrophy growth rate on the fractional dissipation exponent exhibits the same global form across the subcritical, the critical, and a substantial portion of the supercritical regime. Moreover, for small values of the fractional dissipation exponent we uncover nontrivial behavior in the maximal fractional enstrophy growth, including changes in scaling and structure. We further characterize the spatial profiles of the maximizing states across regimes, elucidating the mechanisms that underpin extreme amplification. These findings refine quantitative constraints on extreme events and predictability in nonlocal dissipative dynamics.

We present low-resolution 5–12 μm spectroscopy with the Spitzer IRS of a sample of galaxies selected to span three post-starburst evolutionary stages based on optical spectral indices. The IRS spectra exhibit prominent PAH emission at 6.2, 7.7, 8.6, and 11.3 μm with minimal silicate absorption, consistent with ongoing star formation. However, the PAH inter-band ratios, particularly 11.3/6.2 and 7.7/6.2, show large variations across the sequence. These ratios correlate with both the time elapsed since the most recent starburst and indicators of active galactic nucleus (AGN) activity. We interpret the observed evolution in PAH ratios as reflecting changes in PAH ionization and size distributions driven by increasing AGN influence as systems age, highlighting a post-starburst–AGN evolutionary link.

We compare the ground-state energies of oxygen-ordered superstructures (HS) versus chain superstructures (CS), in which basal-plane oxygen atoms order into chains, across a range of oxygen compositions in YBa2Cu3Ox. The model Hamiltonian comprises three contributions: (i) the Madelung (electrostatic) energy, (ii) a term linear in the difference between Cu and O hole occupancies that controls Cu–O charge transfer, and (iii) covalency effects constrained by established one- and two-dimensional electronic-structure models. The optimum charge distribution is obtained by minimizing the total energy and depends on two parameters calibrated against known phases. On the oxygen-lean side, only CS states are energetically stable. For certain intermediate compositions, an HS featuring regularly spaced oxygen vacancies added to a reference ordered structure becomes more stable than the corresponding CS at the same stoichiometry. Our results demonstrate that detailed atomic positions and long-range Coulomb interactions are crucial in shaping the electronic structure, governing the charge-transfer mechanism, and determining the relative stability of competing phases, including the conditions for phase separation. The analysis provides a unified framework that rationalizes observed oxygen ordering phenomena in YBa2Cu3Ox and highlights the delicate balance between electrostatics and covalency that selects the superstructure. Implications for transport, superconductivity, and the emergence of mesoscale inhomogeneity are discussed. PACS: 74.72.Bk, 72.15.-v, 61.66.-f, 74.10.+v.

We develop a phenomenological framework to extract spin-dependent parton distributions from production of @xmath0 bosons at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider using non‐hermetic detectors. Because the escaping neutrino prevents full event reconstruction, we construct predictions for the distributions of charged leptons from @xmath1 decay, incorporating multiple soft‐gluon radiation through transverse‐momentum resummation of the large logarithms that dominate at small recoil. The formalism yields spin‐dependent resummed cross sections matched to fixed‐order accuracy and is compared systematically with next‐to‐leading‐order results. We demonstrate that lepton‐level single‐ and double‐spin asymmetries are perturbatively stable, insensitive to nonperturbative modeling, and robust under realistic acceptance cuts, enabling direct comparisons to experimental measurements. We also present a numerical program that implements the resummed polarized and unpolarized cross sections for @xmath2 and @xmath3 boson production, providing a tool for RHIC spin analyses.

Confusion noise is a fundamental limitation in deep mid-infrared imaging, where the point-spread function blends multiple faint sources into apparently extended objects and biases photometry and source counts. We present a practical deblending strategy that leverages higher-frequency (shorter-wavelength) observations over the same sky regions to identify distinct counterparts and partition the mid-infrared flux among them. Using IRAC images and public catalogs as positional and photometric priors, we model the 24 μm emission measured by MIPS on Spitzer and split the flux of apparently extended 24 μm sources into multiple components associated with IRAC-detected galaxies. We apply this method to the GOODS-EN1 test field, analyzing a reliable sample of 983 MIPS 24 μm sources detected above a 5-sigma threshold down to 23 μJy. We find that roughly 20% of the catalog comprises “blended” sources whose apparent extension reflects multiple contributors. After deblending, the effective confusion limit of the MIPS 24 μm survey is reduced by about 30%, and the resulting 24 μm sample is essentially unbiased down to 40 μJy. At the flux levels considered here, the careful application of the deblending procedure obviates the need for statistical completeness corrections, as demonstrated by direct comparison with the results of Chary et al. (2004), who analyzed the same data set via extensive Monte Carlo simulations. The improved photometry enables reliable source counts down to approximately 40 μJy. Extrapolating the counts to fainter fluxes suggests that the deblended 24 μm sample resolves about 62% of the cosmic infrared background down to 38 μJy. Our results underscore the power of multi-wavelength prior-based deblending for confusion-limited surveys, providing more accurate fluxes, cleaner catalogs, and robust faint-end counts, and they offer a path forward for maximizing the scientific return from current and future mid-infrared observations.

Black hole production at the Large Hadron Collider is a prediction of TeV-scale gravity models, yet the inferred fundamental Planck scale and the number of extra dimensions hinge on the accuracy of the production cross section. Using the trapped-surface approach in general relativity, calibrated to LHC kinematics and parton distributions, we compute black hole formation with and without parton electric charge. We present ranges of lower limits on the fundamental Planck scale at LHC energies as functions of the number of extra dimensions, showing that realistic charge effects can suppress the cross section by one to four orders of magnitude. This suppression substantially relaxes existing bounds and reshapes discovery prospects and search strategies in future runs.

We introduce an exponential random graph framework that generates networks with a prescribed degree distribution while allowing a tunable degree-degree correlation. Focusing on Poisson degree distributions, we analyze the nature of the percolation transition as assortativity is varied. Using analytical arguments complemented by numerical simulations, we show that negative correlation is irrelevant: disassortative networks exhibit a percolation transition in the same universality class as uncorrelated networks. In contrast, positive correlation is relevant and qualitatively changes critical behavior. Assortative networks display a nondiverging mean size of finite clusters, together with power-law scaling of both the density of the largest cluster and the cluster-size distribution in the nonpercolating phase and at criticality. These findings indicate a distinct universality class governed by assortative mixing. Our results provide a mechanism for the unusual percolation transitions reported in recent growing network models, suggesting that they are inherited from assortative degree-degree correlations rather than growth.

We propose a novel method to determine the nature of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays by exploiting the geomagnetic deviation of muons in nearly horizontal air showers. Using detailed simulations, we show that the two-dimensional muon density at ground is well captured by a simple parametrization with a few shape parameters tightly correlated with the depth of maximal muon production (Xμmax), itself closely linked to the shower maximum (Xmax) and hence to primary mass. Combining the geomagnetic distortion with standard longitudinal-profile measurements significantly improves composition sensitivity and enables constraints on hadronic interaction models. We quantify the required precision—on timing, angular resolution, and muon energy threshold—and array spacing to obtain statistically significant results, and we outline a feasible detector layout based on sparse, shielded, directional muon sensors optimized for horizontal events.

We derive the general features of baryon form factors calculated within point form kinematics using spectator currents. We show that hadronic form factors are functions of @xmath0 and, over a broad range of @xmath1, are insensitive to unitary scale transformations of the model wave functions when their spatial extent is small compared to the scale set by the constituent mass, @xmath2. The form factors remain, however, sensitive to the detailed shape of such compact wave functions. Using simple three-quark proton wave functions, we illustrate these properties and assess several ansätze. Rational and algebraic model wave functions yield a reasonable description of empirical proton form factors, whereas Gaussian wave functions fail to reproduce the observed behavior. For large @xmath1, point form kinematics with spectator currents leads to universal power-law falloff of the form factors, constraining viable wave-function shapes in relativistic quark models.

We provide a complete asymptotic characterization of the large-maturity forward implied volatility smile in the Heston model. While the leading decay follows a classical large-deviations principle, the algebraic expansion of higher-order corrections exhibits a pronounced parameter sensitivity, with distinct powers of maturity arising across regimes. As by-products, we derive new implied-volatility asymptotics for both forward-start and spot smiles, and propose extended SVI-type parameterizations consistent with the asymptotic structure. Our proofs rely on refined sharp large-deviations techniques, extending beyond standard convexity-based arguments and covering degenerate and boundary cases. The results yield transparent formulas, rigorous error controls, and practical guidance for model calibration, risk management, and extrapolation at long maturities.

We study T-duality chains of five-branes in heterotic supergravity incorporating first-order alpha′ corrections. Starting from heterotic NS5-brane solutions of the symmetric, neutral, and gauge types, we perform alpha′-corrected T-duality transformations to construct the corresponding KK5-brane and exotic 5^2_2-brane backgrounds. A central feature of these solutions is the presence of nontrivial Yang–Mills gauge fields that, after appropriate smearing necessary for T-duality, obey self-duality conditions in the three- and two-dimensional transverse spaces to the brane worldvolumes. To characterize the global properties and potential non-geometric behavior, we analyze the monodromy structures of the 5^2_2-brane solutions using the alpha′-corrected generalized metric that captures the interplay of metric, B-field, and gauge-field data within the heterotic framework. We find that the exotic 5^2_2-brane derived from the symmetric NS5-brane, which satisfies the standard embedding condition equating the gauge and spin connections, is a T-fold: it exhibits nontrivial O(d,d) monodromies that require T-duality for patching and thus displays non-geometric nature. The neutral 5^2_2-brane also shows T-fold behavior, at least to leading order in alpha′. In contrast, the 5^2_2-brane obtained from the gauge NS5-brane is not a T-fold but presents unusual spacetime structures attributable to the gauge sector and alpha′ corrections. Our results provide explicit alpha′-corrected heterotic five-brane solutions, clarify the role of gauge-field self-duality and standard embedding in non-geometric backgrounds, and refine the understanding of T-duality and monodromy in heterotic supergravity.

Warm absorbers imprint prominent soft X-ray absorption features in roughly half of Seyfert 1 galaxies and in a subset of quasars and blazars. We use thermal equilibrium (pressure–temperature) curves of photoionized gas to investigate how the shape of the ionizing continuum, the gas density, and the chemical composition govern the existence and phase structure of these absorbers. By mapping stability branches across grids of spectral slopes, ultraviolet-to-X-ray ratios, densities, and abundances, we identify the conditions under which a stable warm absorber forms either as a multiphase medium in pressure balance or with a continuous pressure gradient. We find that warm absorbers require an X-ray power-law slope steeper than a threshold; for slopes typical of Seyfert 1 galaxies, the equilibrium curve develops multiple stable branches at comparable pressure, enabling a multiphase configuration. When the ionizing continuum is sufficiently soft (UV-dominated), the thermal and ionization states of high-density absorbers become sensitive to density, departing from the commonly assumed density-insensitive regime of photoionized plasmas. Elevated metallicity enhances line cooling, broadens stability zones, and increases the likelihood of multiphase solutions. In contrast, removing iron and iron-peak elements—whose yields are associated with later stages of chemical evolution and Type Ia supernovae—suppresses key cooling features and can collapse the equilibrium into a single phase or eliminate multiphase behavior altogether. These results directly link the phase structure of warm absorbers to AGN spectral energy distributions and to the star-formation and enrichment history of their host galaxies. They further provide testable predictions for soft X-ray diagnostics (e.g., oxygen and neon lines, Fe unresolved transition arrays), for density-sensitive behavior under UV-dominated illumination, and for metallicity-dependent variability. Our framework offers a unified interpretation of warm absorber diversity in Seyfert 1s and extends to quasars and blazars where continuum shape and composition differ.

Bonding multiple frequency bands into a single logical channel can accelerate data transfer in wireless networks, yet assigning several channels to one user reduces the likelihood of finding a free logical channel for new connections, potentially lowering network-wide throughput. While this trade-off has been examined experimentally in WLANs, a rigorous analytical treatment remains limited, and is particularly needed for opportunistic spectrum access (OSA) systems where primary users exhibit dynamic duty cycles. This paper introduces an analytical framework for medium access control (MAC)-layer performance of OSA networks with channel bonding. The model captures stochastic primary-user occupancy, secondary-user contention, connection establishment and blocking, and the impact of bonding order on average channel throughput. Using the framework, we derive expressions and numerical evaluations showing that channel bonding is generally beneficial, but the magnitude of gains depends on OSA network size, traffic load, and the number of channels available for bonding. We further demonstrate that adaptive bonding—dynamically selecting the number of bonded channels in response to observed network and spectrum conditions—can realize additional performance improvements by balancing throughput per connection against admission probability. To bridge MAC and physical-layer constraints, we incorporate transmission power limits that induce sublinear throughput scaling with bonding size, quantifying the reduction relative to the ideal single virtual channel. The analysis yields design guidelines for when to enable bonding, how aggressively to bond, and how to adapt bonding strategies under varying primary-user activity and secondary-user demand and fairness considerations.

To better understand diffuse ionized gas (DIG) kinematics and halo rotation in spiral galaxies, we develop a model in which clouds are ejected from galactic disks and follow ballistic trajectories through the halo. We explore the model behavior with a comprehensive parameter-space search and analyses of individual cloud orbits, and generate synthetic velocity profiles as a function of height above the plane (z) for direct comparison to velocity centroid data obtained from long-slit spectra of the edge-on spirals NGC 891 (one slit) and NGC 5775 (two slits). In both systems, a purely ballistic framework is inadequate to reproduce all aspects of the observed DIG kinematics. For NGC 891, the measured vertical velocity gradient is shallower than predicted, suggesting additional physics such as dynamical coupling between disk and halo rotation or an outwardly directed pressure gradient acting on the extraplanar gas. In NGC 5775, the ballistic model provides a closer match to the observed trends, yet it fails to explain the approach of high-z gas velocities toward the systemic velocity; this behavior is consistent with either an inwardly directed pressure gradient or tidal influence from its companion, NGC 5774. The model robustly predicts that clouds migrate radially outward as they cycle through the halo, and order-of-magnitude estimates of associated mass and energy fluxes indicate that such circulation can redistribute material and angular momentum in a manner that significantly impacts the evolution of the interstellar medium. Our results constrain plausible launch speeds, radii, and halo scale heights, and highlight the necessity of incorporating non-ballistic forces—pressure gradients, magnetic stresses, and viscous coupling—to fully capture DIG kinematics and disk–halo interaction in spiral galaxies.

At the initial time, @xmath0 s are randomly distributed in the evolving fluid; during the subsequent expansion, free-streaming @xmath0 s are dissolved if the local temperature exceeds a threshold @xmath2. A sequential melting scenario for charmonium states (@xmath3, @xmath4, and @xmath0), characterized by melting temperatures @xmath5 and @xmath6 and a feed-down fraction @xmath7, quantitatively reproduces PHENIX measurements of the centrality dependence of @xmath0 suppression in Au+Au collisions. The model also provides a good description of the @xmath8 spectra and the nuclear modification factor. In Cu+Cu collisions, however, the centrality dependence of @xmath0 suppression is overpredicted by 20–30%, and the @xmath0 @xmath8 spectra are underpredicted by 20–30%, indicating possible system-size or initial-state effects beyond the current implementation. Extrapolating to LHC energies, the model predicts that in central Pb+Pb collisions at @xmath1=5500 GeV, @xmath0 s are suppressed by a factor of @xmath9 10, with the resulting @xmath0 @xmath8 distribution resembling that observed in Au+Au collisions at RHIC. Sensitivities to @xmath2 and feed-down inputs are discussed.

We report the observation and characterization of agglomeration of highly charged microparticles in complex plasmas formed in a capacitively coupled rf discharge. By lowering the neutral gas pressure, strong dust density waves were triggered, driving high-relative-velocity particle motion. High‐speed imaging resolved individual trajectories and demonstrated that, for a subset of collisions, relative velocities exceeded the Coulomb repulsion barrier, enabling sticking and aggregate formation. After restabilizing the cloud by increasing the pressure, we directly visualized the resulting aggregates using a long‐distance microscope and extracted size distributions and agglomeration rates. The experimentally deduced agglomeration rate agrees, within uncertainties, with theoretical estimates based on collisional kinetics and electrostatic interaction models. We further discuss candidate binding mechanisms operative for highly charged grains in plasmas, including ion‐wake–mediated attraction, charge‐fluctuation–assisted sticking, and cohesive forces. These results establish dust density wave–driven collisions as a robust pathway to aggregate formation in laboratory complex plasmas.

In recent work, simulating a classical channel exactly with the aid of quantum no-signalling correlations has been formulated via semidefinite programs, capturing the one-shot no-signalling assisted zero-error simulation cost of non-commutative bipartite graphs [Duan and Winter, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 62, 891 (2016)]. Prior to our study, it was open whether the one-shot cost is multiplicative under tensor product and whether the corresponding asymptotic cost is additive for general non-commutative graphs. We resolve these questions by deriving a general sufficient condition ensuring multiplicativity of the one-shot cost and, consequently, additivity of the asymptotic cost. Our condition applies broadly and subsumes all previously tractable families, including extremal graphs and classical–quantum graphs, thereby unifying and extending known results. Leveraging this framework, we identify and analyze a large class of cheapest-full-rank graphs, for which the asymptotic zero-error simulation cost coincides with the one-shot cost, yielding single-letter characterizations via semidefinite programming. Complementing these positive results, we prove that multiplicativity fails in general by constructing explicit qubit–qutrit non-commutative bipartite graphs that violate one-shot multiplicativity. Our findings clarify the structure of zero-error simulation under no-signalling assistance, delineate when simple composition rules hold, and provide tools for certifying optimal costs in relevant quantum information processing tasks. We discuss implications for channel simulation resource theories.

We develop a generalized transmission coefficient formula for a lead–junction–lead system that explicitly incorporates interactions between the leads. Within this unified framework, the classical Caroli formula is recovered as a special case, and a compact interface transmission expression for ballistic setups is derived. We analyze the conditions under which the generalized formula is valid, discussing assumptions such as steady-state transport, weak nonlocal coupling, and linear response. The primary focus is on phononic heat transport, while noting that the electrical counterpart follows analogously. To elucidate the formalism, we present an illustrative example that clarifies the physical meaning of the constituent quantities, including the reduced interacting matrix in different coupling scenarios. Furthermore, we obtain an explicit transmission coefficient for a general one-dimensional interface based on the interface formula, enabling practical evaluation of interfacial thermal conductance in engineered nanostructures.

The 2007–2008 credit crisis exposed weaknesses in MBS pricing, notably institutions' reliance on credit ratings despite available models. Conflicts of interest between rating agencies and issuers likely distorted risk assessment, leading to mispricing and inadequate capital. We present a transparent simulation framework for valuing and risk-managing non-agency MBS and CMOs that augments established agency-MBS cash-flow engines with borrower credit and prepayment dynamics. The model integrates Basel II credit-risk components—probability of default, loss given default, exposure at default—and portfolio correlation to generate loan-level transitions, credit enhancement usage, and tranche cash flows under macro scenarios. Calibrated to historical performance and house-price and unemployment dynamics, it produces distributions of losses, weighted-average life, option-adjusted spreads, and rating proxies, and supports stress testing. Applications to representative non-agency pools show large divergences from rating-based expectations, particularly under adverse house-price and correlation shocks; mezzanine and senior tranches exhibit fat-tailed loss and extension risk. The framework enables institutional investors to assess combined credit and prepayment risks, strengthen due diligence, and reduce reliance on conflicted ratings.

We introduce a Schur-lift basis of noncommutative symmetric functions (NSym) whose commutative image is the classical Schur basis. This basis is characterized by Pieri-type creation operators, unitriangularity with respect to the ribbon basis, and compatibility with the NSym Hopf structure. Dually, we construct a basis of quasi-symmetric functions (QSym) that expands positively in the fundamental basis and refines Schur functions via an explicit signed combinatorial decomposition. We give bijective models in terms of descent sets and standard composition tableaux, derive transition matrices to ribbon, monomial, and fundamental bases, and obtain product and coproduct formulas with combinatorial interpretations. The signed QSym expansion yields structural identities for skew Schur functions and recovers Kostka-type relations. Applications include new positivity statements, algorithms for efficient expansion, and connections to 0-Hecke representation theory. We conclude with examples, extremal cases, and conjectures on stability and unimodality of the associated coefficients.

We propose a network-based characterization of combinatorial fitness landscapes by adapting inherent networks from energy surfaces. Using the well-known family of @xmath0 landscapes, we define an inherent network whose vertices are local maxima and whose weighted edges encode transition probabilities between their basins of attraction. We exhaustively extract such networks for representative @xmath0 instances and analyze their topology, including degree distributions, path lengths, and basin size correlations. The results reveal systematic dependencies on @xmath1 and strong links to search difficulty, with harder landscapes exhibiting sparser, more heterogeneous networks and reduced basin accessibility. These insights clarify global landscape structure and offer guidance for the design of heuristic search.

One year after the launch of the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, the landscape of pulsar astrophysics has changed profoundly. Using the Large Area Telescope (LAT), the number of known gamma-ray pulsars has increased sharply, including a sizable cohort discovered directly in gamma-ray data without prior radio ephemerides. Crucially, millisecond pulsars have been confirmed as luminous gamma-ray emitters, and a population of these recycled objects is now firmly established in the LAT catalog. The remaining newly detected gamma-ray pulsars are predominantly young, identified through coordinated searches and timing campaigns with radio and X-ray observatories. The emerging picture shows that a large fraction of nearby, energetically powerful pulsars emit gamma rays, with luminosity scaling with spin-down power. Many previously unidentified EGRET sources are now recognized as pulsars, and numerous detections coincide with pulsar wind nebulae; several systems are also associated with TeV emission, linking particle acceleration across energy bands. The LAT’s sensitivity and all-sky coverage promise continued growth of the gamma-ray pulsar sample, while multi-wavelength follow-up should unveil radio or X-ray counterparts to LAT-discovered objects. Early data support outer-magnetosphere emission models with broad, fan-like beams sweeping large sky fractions, reshaping constraints on pulsar geometry, particle outflows, and magnetospheric electrodynamics. They inaugurate a new gamma-ray pulsar era.

We investigate scalar and gravitational perturbations of five-dimensional squashed Kaluza–Klein (KK) black holes, which differ qualitatively from asymptotically flat Schwarzschild black holes and from black strings even at energies below the excitation threshold of KK modes. Working in both time and frequency domains, we compute quasinormal spectra and late-time tails for generic scalar perturbations of rotating squashed KK solutions and for the zero-mode sector of gravitational perturbations in the non-rotating limit. Our time-domain evolutions exhibit exponentially damped ringdowns followed by power-law decays, with no growing modes. Frequency-domain analyses confirm the absence of unstable poles, indicating linear stability and thereby evading the Gregory–Laflamme instability that afflicts extended black objects. We further establish a clear correlation between the squashing/compactification scale and the quasinormal frequencies: increasing the size of the extra dimension lowers the oscillation frequencies and reduces damping rates, imprinting the higher-dimensional geometry on the ringdown signal across a broad parameter space. Our results highlight squashed KK black holes as stable laboratories where higher-dimensional effects can manifest in observable perturbative dynamics.

We investigate two phase-shift equivalent local nucleon–nucleon potentials, Reid93 and NijmII, previously shown by Friar et al. to yield nearly identical triton properties, within a @xmath2 no-core shell-model framework. Calculations for @xmath0 and @xmath1 employing large no-core spaces demonstrate remarkably similar binding energies, radii, and electromagnetic observables for Reid93 and NijmII. For comparison, we evaluate the widely used Hamada–Johnson hard-core and the original Reid soft-core interactions, which exhibit larger deuteron @xmath3-state percentages and correspondingly stronger tensor components. A robust correlation between tensor strength and nuclear binding energy is confirmed across interactions. Nevertheless, many nuclear-structure observables—spectra, transition strengths, and static moments—appear largely insensitive to detailed features of the NN potential, limiting their utility in discriminating among phase-shift equivalent models. These findings underscore the constrained role of two-nucleon dynamics in observables and point to the importance of three-nucleon forces and uncertainties in precision tests of NN interactions.

We investigate Aharonov–Casher oscillations of spin current in a two-dimensional ballistic ring with Rashba spin–orbit interaction under an external magnetic field. Using a semiclassical path-integral framework, we sum over multi-path trajectories and derive, for classically chaotic motion, a Fokker–Planck equation governing the stochastic evolution of spin polarization. From this kinetic description we obtain a closed analytic expression for the spin conductance of realistic rings with finite-width arms supporting many conducting channels. Multimode averaging introduces geometrical dephasing that broadens and damps the Aharonov–Casher oscillations of the spin current. A weak perpendicular magnetic field generates new nondiagonal components of the spin conductance tensor, evidencing field-induced mixing of spin projections. Consequently, the polarization of the transmitted spin current can be steered and reoriented by modest fields. Our results quantify the interplay of spin–orbit coupling, ring geometry, and magnetic control, providing design rules for tunable mesoscopic spin interferometers.

We present a statistical analysis of a complete sample of 255 northern planetary nebulae (PNe) using morphology as the principal parameter. The sample divides into round (26%), elliptical (61%), and bipolar (13%) classes. Multiple shells occur in about half of round PNe and 30% of elliptical PNe. Round PNe preferentially lie at higher Galactic latitudes and show larger scale heights (≈753 pc) than elliptical (≈308 pc) and bipolar (≈179 pc) PNe. These trends reveal morphology-dependent spatial distributions and likely reflect differences in progenitor mass ranges and stellar populations, with round PNe linked to older, lower-mass progenitors and bipolar PNe to younger, more massive progenitors concentrated near the Galactic plane.

We report combined experimental and theoretical investigations of undulation patterns in high-pressure, inclined-layer gas convection at a Prandtl number near unity. Emphasis is placed on the competition between spatiotemporal undulation chaos and stationary, ordered undulations. Experiments reveal coexistence, bistability, and state selection, with ordered undulations prevalent at higher Rayleigh numbers. The competing states are quantified using spectral pattern entropy, spatial correlation lengths, and defect statistics, providing measures of order and chaos. A weakly nonlinear stability analysis of the Oberbeck–Boussinesq equations using Galerkin expansions maps the stability region of ordered undulations as a function of wavevector and Rayleigh number. Complementary direct numerical simulations reproduce the spatiotemporal dynamics and show dependence on initial conditions, capturing both ordered undulations and undulation chaos. Across methods, thresholds, pattern wavelengths, and defect densities agree within experimental uncertainty. The results establish inclined-layer convection as a model system for order–chaos competition and highlight parameter regimes where ordered undulations suppress undulation chaos.

We present a multiple-resolution analysis of two-dimensional structures formed by randomly adsorbed, penetrable rods at coverages below the percolation threshold. In contrast to assemblies of randomly distributed isotropic objects, we show that the upper cutoff, @xmath2, is controlled not only by total coverage but also by the excluded volume averaged over the rods’ orientational distribution. Consequently, the apparent fractal dimension extracted from the intermediate scaling window is not universal: it depends explicitly on orientational anisotropy and decreases as the distribution becomes more aligned. For resolutions finer than the rod length (box sizes smaller than @xmath1), the box-counting statistics are governed by the rods’ internal structure. We illustrate two cases: (i) regular rods with one-dimensional internal geometry and (ii) rods trimmed into a Cantor-set architecture, themselves fractal. These examples establish a clear separation between two length-scale regimes: @xmath3, where the intrinsic structure of the adsorbates is probed, and @xmath4, where the spatial distribution of rods dictates the scaling; both regimes can exhibit fractal signatures but with distinct effective dimensions and crossovers. Our results provide quantitative criteria for identifying and interpreting apparent fractality in sub-percolation rod assemblies and clarify how excluded-volume and orientational effects set the observable scaling window. The models and conclusions are directly relevant to adsorption of linear molecules and fibers, liquid crystal monolayers, stress-induced fracture networks, and edge imperfections in metal catalysts. More broadly, the distinction between internal and distribution-controlled scaling extends to systems comprising a finite density of fractal-like clusters, including molecular beam epitaxy surface growth and diffusion-limited cluster–cluster aggregation.

We report the detection of a strong emission line at 6703 Angstroms in the optical spectrum of the host galaxy (r = 23.1) of the radio source RCJ0311+0507 (4C+04.11). The radio galaxy exhibits an ultrasteep spectrum with spectral index alpha = 1.31 between 365 and 4850 MHz, identified in the RATAN-600 sky-strip survey. We argue that the 6703 Angstrom feature is Ly-alpha, yielding a redshift z about 4.51. At this redshift, RCJ0311+0507 ranks among the most distant and radio-luminous galaxies known, with inferred power in the ultrahigh regime. Such extreme radio output likely requires a black hole of order 10^9 solar masses, assembled within about 1.3 Gyr of cosmic time, or originating from a massive primordial seed. The discovery supports ultrasteep-spectrum selection for locating high-redshift radio galaxies and provides constraints on early supermassive black hole growth and feedback in massive protogalaxies.

We present a multi-epoch Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) study of three EGRET-detected quasars, 0202+149, CTA 26, and 1606+106, together with additional analysis of VLBI data for 1156+295 previously reported by Piner and Kingham (1997b). Using data from the Washington VLBI correlator’s geodetic database, we produced 8 and 2 GHz images spanning 11 epochs (0202+149), 8 epochs (CTA 26), and 12 epochs (1606+106) over 1989–1996. Model fitting to the parsec-scale structures yielded proper motions and apparent velocities for identified jet components, as well as constraints on jet bending and non-radial trajectories. We find CTA 26 and 1606+106 to be superluminal, with average apparent speeds of 8.9c and 2.9c, respectively, under standard cosmological assumptions. In contrast, components in 0202+149 are stationary within our measurement uncertainties, and we classify this object as a compact double. All sources exhibit pronounced jet bending, and we detect significant non-radial motion in components of CTA 26 and 1156+295. Despite the occurrence of prominent gamma-ray flares in CTA 26, 1156+295, and 1606+106 during the monitoring interval, we do not detect new superluminal components emerging subsequently; we therefore place lower limits on any post-flare ejection epochs. We compare the misalignment angle distribution of these EGRET sources with that of the broader blazar population and find no evidence that EGRET-selected blazars preferentially occupy either the aligned or misaligned subset. Furthermore, comparisons of average apparent velocities and Doppler beaming factors between EGRET and non-EGRET blazars reveal no statistically significant differences. Within the uncertainties of our measurements, we thus find no indication that EGRET blazars are more strongly beamed than similar blazars not detected in gamma rays. These results suggest that gamma-ray detectability in blazars is not solely determined by enhanced Doppler boosting on parsec scales and may depend on additional factors such as intrinsic jet power, variability duty cycle, or high-energy emission zone conditions.

We present a comparative analysis of lithium (Li) abundances in stars hosting planets discovered via the Doppler radial-velocity method and in stars without detected planets. We assembled and homogenized Li measurements from recent studies, placing them on a consistent scale and matching comparison samples in effective temperature. Our results confirm that, near solar temperatures, planet-hosting stars exhibit systematically lower Li abundances than non-hosts. Furthermore, Li anomalies correlate with rotational velocity (v sin i) and with activity anomalies, indicating modifications of rotation and Li depletion. These patterns support scenarios in which planet formation or early disk-star interactions regulate stellar angular momentum and internal mixing, reducing surface Li in Doppler planet hosts. We encourage Li observations for stars with 5600–6200 K to further test these correlations and refine their interpretation.

We present the technical design and performance of the gamma‐ray burst (GRB) alert and response system on the Katzman Automatic Imaging Telescope (KAIT) at Lick Observatory, and demonstrate its capabilities with successful observations of the GRB 020813 optical afterglow. KAIT ingests GRB alerts robotically, interrupts programs, slews rapidly, and executes predefined imaging sequences tailored to alert type and localization accuracy. To maximize early-time coverage, a grid-imaging procedure offsets successive short exposures across the error region, increasing the probability of detection while preserving photometric fidelity. With fast telescope slew and CCD readout, KAIT typically initiates the first exposure within 60 s of alert receipt, reaching a limiting magnitude of @xmath0 in unfiltered images. We describe the automated reduction pipeline and show that unfiltered magnitudes can be transformed reliably to a standard passband with a precision of @xmath15% when the source color is known. For GRB 020813, the early optical light curve exhibits an unusually slow power-law decay, whereas subsequent temporal behavior and optical spectral index are typical of GRBs. These results validate KAIT’s rapid-response strategy and demonstrate the scientific return of efficient, robotic optical follow-up of GRB afterglows.

We investigate a model of galaxy clusters in which the hot intracluster medium (ICM) is heated by dynamical friction (DF) exerted on orbiting galaxies. We include both subsonic and supersonic galaxy motions and adopt the gravitational drag formalism for gaseous media developed by Ostriker (1999). The energy extracted from galaxy orbits is deposited either locally or redistributed with a Gaussian kernel centered on each galaxy to emulate finite-scale thermalization. Imposing hydrostatic equilibrium and strict, radius-by-radius energy balance yields either a trivial isothermal solution with T = @xmath0, independent of radius, or families of radially rising temperature profiles that exist provided @xmath1, where @xmath2 is the adiabatic index of the gas. The isothermal temperature recovers the standard scaling between ICM temperature and the galaxies’ velocity dispersion. However, the minimal temperature associated with the rising solutions is @xmath3, which exceeds values typically inferred from X-ray observations, largely independent of the assumed radial distribution of galaxy masses. We assess the impact of DF heating on thermal stability and find that heating by supersonically moving galaxies cannot suppress isobaric thermal instability, although it can extend the growth time to values comparable to cluster ages when the galaxy Mach number is less than about two. Using hydrodynamic simulations that evolve non-equilibrium cluster cores with DF-induced heating, we show that DF heating generally fails to establish long-lived, stable, quasi-steady cores, even when energy deposition is spatially broadened. Nonetheless, DF can substantially delay catastrophic cooling by lengthening the effective cooling time. We conclude that DF-induced heating alone is unlikely to resolve the cooling-flow problem, though it remains a potentially important contributor to the ICM energy budget. We briefly discuss additional ramifications of galaxy DF for cluster thermodynamics and structure.

We investigate how spectroscopic observables, particularly electromagnetic transition strengths, connect to properties of intrinsic mean‐field wave functions as nuclear deformation varies. While standard rotational formulas are reliable for strongly deformed shapes, they fail toward the spherical regime. We establish a rigorous, nonzero spherical limit that expresses transition strengths in terms of overlaps between deformed intrinsic states. Using exact angular‐momentum projection from mean‐field configurations, we benchmark the spherical and rotational limits across a broad set of nuclei and map the continuous transition between them. From these comparisons we derive a simple validity criterion for the rotational formula based on xmath0, the mean‐square fluctuation of angular momentum in the intrinsic state: large xmath0 ensures rotational behavior, small xmath0 favors the spherical limit. Finally, we propose an interpolation formula that reproduces both limits and accurately tracks projected results over the full deformation range, offering a tool for nuclear spectroscopy.

We present a three-stage framework that combines complementary N-body techniques to determine the dynamical parameters of interacting galaxies and apply it to the H I distribution of the Magellanic-type dwarf galaxy NGC 4449. In the first stage, fast restricted N-body models are employed to delineate regions of parameter space that reproduce the principal observed features of the system. These models, which treat the gas as collisionless test particles in the time-dependent gravitational field of the interacting galaxies, enable efficient exploration of key parameters such as mass ratio, orbital eccentricity and pericenter, inclination and argument of pericenter, time since closest approach, and the initial orientation and radial extent of the H I disc. In the second stage, we introduce a genetic algorithm to automate the search within this high-dimensional space and to assess the uniqueness of candidate solutions. The fitness function quantifies simultaneous agreement with multiple observational constraints, including the column density morphology (disc-like central component, asymmetric outer arm), global radial extent, projected orientation, and position–velocity structure. Tests with artificial datasets show that the genetic algorithm reliably recovers the input orbital parameters provided the data are sufficiently accurate and include all key morphological and kinematic features; conversely, omitting critical constraints leads to degeneracies and broadened confidence intervals. In the third stage, representative best-fit restricted models are confronted with fully self-consistent N-body simulations to verify the stability of the inferred scenario against model assumptions and to quantify systematic uncertainties. For NGC 4449, radio observations reveal an extended H I halo at least an order of magnitude larger than the optical diameter, with a central disc-like feature and a pronounced lopsided arm. Our simulations demonstrate that these signatures arise naturally from a recent gravitational encounter with the nearby dwarf DDO 125 on a nearly parabolic orbit, with pericentric passage occurring on the order of a few 10^8 years ago at a minimum separation of order tens of kiloparsecs. The encounter requires a dynamical mass for DDO 125 not smaller than roughly 10% of NGC 4449’s mass. Prior to the encounter, the H I was arranged in a disc of radius approximately 35–40 kpc, aligned with the central ellipsoidal H I structure; its origin may reflect an earlier interaction. The comparison with self-consistent simulations confirms the applicability of restricted models and shows that, in this case, the H I can be modeled by purely gravitational (stellar dynamical) means. This general methodology yields constrained, testable interaction histories for gas-rich dwarfs and other interacting systems.

This paper investigates multiuser diversity gains in cognitive radio systems where secondary users opportunistically access spectrum licensed to primary users only when idle. To protect primaries against interference from missed detections, we impose a minimum average throughput constraint on the primary network via transmit power control at secondary transmitters. Incorporating stochastic traffic dynamics of the primary network and imperfect sensing, we derive expressions for the average achievable capacity of the secondary network under opportunistic scheduling. Asymptotic analyses with more secondary users reveal scaling laws and regimes where diversity gains persist, saturate, or vanish. The results quantify trade-offs among sensing reliability, traffic load, and power control, guiding practical CR design.

We present a systematic analysis of hadron abundances in heavy-ion collisions from SPS to RHIC energies within the statistical–thermal model. For the first time, Pb–Pb collisions at 40 A GeV are studied. Fits to integrated multiplicities and to mid-rapidity yields consistently determine the chemical freeze-out temperature T and baryon chemical potential μB, which show only modest dependence on acceptance. In contrast, the extra strangeness suppression factor γs varies with phase-space coverage: complete strange chemical equilibrium (γs≈1) is ruled out when 4π-integrated multiplicities are used, while near-saturation can emerge in limited rapidity windows. These findings highlight sensitivity of inferred strangeness equilibration to longitudinal acceptance at SPS energies and question whether the apparent strangeness saturation observed at RHIC mid-rapidity persists in full phase space. Implications for chemical freeze-out and future measurements are discussed.

We investigate the possible quark-model assignments of the recently observed @xmath1 and @xmath2 by LHCb within a nonrelativistic quark model for bottom and bottom-strange mesons.
