While a well‐known conjecture predicts that this proportion tends to one as the radius goes to infinity, we prove a uniform positive lower bound independent of the generating set. We further obtain analogous bounds for a broad class of subgroups, highlighting genericity and stability phenomena.

We present medium-resolution spectroscopy and multicolor photometry of the optical transient PSN J09093496+3307204 (SN 2015bh) in the galaxy NGC 2770, which transitioned into a supernova. Observations conducted between February 2015 and May 2016 encompass both the pre-explosion impostor phase (2015a) and the supernova phase (2015b). In both phases, the spectra show strong Balmer emission accompanied by prominent Fe II multiplets, closely resembling the Williams Fe II type classical novae. The source lies near the edge of a dark nebula and is notably reddened; we estimate A_V = 1.14 ± 0.15 mag. Correcting for this absorption, we infer peak absolute magnitudes of M_V ≈ −15.0 mag during 2015a and M_V ≈ −18.1 mag during 2015b. The 2015b light curve exhibits a quasi-linear decline reminiscent of Type IIL supernovae. Narrow, powerful Hα emission and the photometric evolution indicate a luminous blue variable progenitor undergoing substantial mass loss prior to explosion. We evaluate several hypotheses linking LBV-related optical transients to subsequent supernovae and favor a core-collapse of an evolved massive star that interrupts an ongoing merger with a massive companion in a binary system—a failed luminous red nova. This scenario coherently accounts for the pre-SN impostor episode, Fe II-dominated spectra, IIL-like light curve, and the dusty, absorbing environment. SN 2015bh provides a compelling case connecting LBV eruptions, impostors, and terminal core collapse, underscoring the value of extended spectroscopic and photometric monitoring to trace the pathways from eruptive massive-star activity to supernovae.

Plutinos, transneptunian objects trapped in the 3:2 mean-motion resonance with Neptune, are overrepresented in flux-limited surveys due to their relative proximity at perihelion and have been extensively studied theoretically. A significant subset occupies the Kozai resonance, exhibiting coupled oscillations of eccentricity and inclination tied to libration of the argument of perihelion (@xmath0), in addition to the standard 3:2 resonant argument libration. We present a detailed forward-modeling framework for the on-sky detection biases affecting plutinos, with special emphasis on the Kozai subpopulation. Our model generates dynamically self-consistent plutino orbits, including Kozai libration, propagates them to sky coordinates and heliocentric distances, computes apparent magnitudes and rates of motion, and folds these through survey selection functions that depend on ecliptic latitude and longitude, limiting magnitude, cadence, and trailing losses. Because the 3:2 resonance phases perihelia away from Neptune’s current ecliptic longitude and Kozai libration restricts @xmath0 such that perihelia occur preferentially out of the ecliptic plane, ecliptic-focused surveys are biased against detecting Kozai plutinos. We quantify how the observed Kozai fraction @xmath1 depends sensitively on survey geometry: @xmath1 varies strongly with ecliptic latitude and exhibits additional modulation with ecliptic longitude due to resonant phasing, leading to wide survey-to-survey differences. Even an all-sky, flux-limited survey does not recover the intrinsic Kozai fraction @xmath2, because detections cluster near perihelion distances and preferred longitudes that differentially weight Kozai versus non-Kozai orbits. We provide a predictive map of the apparent on-sky Kozai fraction expected for all-sky flux-limited programs, directly applicable to the Panoramic Survey Telescope & Rapid Response System (Pan-STARRS) and the Large Synoptic Survey Telescope (LSST), which will detect large plutino samples. Comparing our bias predictions with reported @xmath1 values (8%–25%) and migration-model expectations for @xmath2 (10%–30%), we demonstrate that robust inference of @xmath2 requires forward-biasing model populations through realistic survey simulators rather than simple scalar debiasing. We further show that @xmath2 and the detailed orbital-element distributions of Kozai plutinos offer powerful diagnostics of giant planet migration. We advocate observational strategies that include significant off-ecliptic coverage and recommend that future migration simulations report the resonant Kozai content and phase distributions to enable direct, survey-aware comparisons.

We define a class of Bohmian quantum models for N entangled, noninteracting Dirac particles that achieves Lorentz invariance by supplementing the dynamics with a spacetime foliation. Extending Bohm’s original relativistic model, which uses equal-time hyperplanes in a preferred Lorentz frame, we allow general foliations and formulate foliation-dependent guidance laws for particle world lines driven by the multi-particle Dirac wave function. For each foliation we establish an equivariant probability measure on its leaves, ensuring preservation of the Born distribution and enabling statistical analysis of position correlations, analogous to equilibrium results in nonrelativistic Bohmian mechanics. We examine covariance properties, predictions, and the status of the foliation as hidden dynamical structure, and conditions for foliation independence of observable statistics.

We study superconformal defect lines in the two-dimensional tricritical Ising model. Using the folding trick, such defects are mapped to superconformal boundary conditions of the N=1 superconformal unitary minimal model with a modular invariant. We show that the complete catalog of boundary states in that model cannot be interpreted as a consistent set of superconformal defects for tricritical Ising because it does not contain the identity (“no defect”) configuration. Instead, by imposing superconformal gluing conditions and the Cardy consistency constraints, we construct a set of 18 defects, including the “no defect,” that form a closed family. These defects exhibit diverse transport properties: besides purely transmissive or purely reflective interfaces, we find mixed defects with nontrivial transmission and reflection amplitudes. We present their fusion rules, annulus spectra, and boundary entropies, and identify topological versus non-topological representatives. Our results provide a complete superconformal classification of defects in tricritical Ising and clarify the relation between boundary state data and interfaces.

We present deep Chandra observations of the kiloparsec-scale jet in the high-power quasar 3C 273, combined with radio and optical imaging to characterize the broadband emission and its spatially resolved spectra. Along the bright jet, the X-ray photon indices are significantly steeper than the radio spectral indices everywhere except the first bright knot (A). This systematic softening, together with the morphology and flux ratios, rules out a single-zone beamed inverse-Compton scattering of the cosmic microwave background as the dominant X-ray mechanism for the entire jet. In two-zone configurations, a synchrotron origin for the X-rays provides a more natural explanation than inverse-Compton models, particularly if velocity shear or small-scale turbulence sustains efficient particle acceleration. The data are consistent with near-equipartition magnetic fields, moderate bulk Lorentz factors, and continuous acceleration that offsets rapid radiative cooling of the highest-energy electrons. Knot A may reflect distinct physical conditions. Our results favor shear-accelerated, multi-component synchrotron emission in powerful quasar jets and place new constraints on their composition and energetics.

We present an analysis of 0.35–7.5 keV X-ray spectra from the central Perseus cluster obtained with the Broad Band X-Ray Telescope (BBXRT) during the Astro-1 mission, optimized for sensitivity in the 0.35–1.0 keV band crucial for diagnosing cooling-flow absorbers. Spectral fits reveal absorption in excess of the Galactic foreground and indicate an absorber that is markedly deficient in helium. The measured energy of the oxygen K-edge is consistent with neutral oxygen at the cluster redshift and is incompatible with any ionized state of oxygen. Because helium cannot be fully ionized while oxygen remains neutral, the inferred helium deficiency cannot be attributed to ionization effects. We propose that the soft X-ray absorption arises predominantly from dust grains condensed from a medium in which helium stays ionized, thereby imprinting metal edges while contributing little helium opacity. This dust-absorption scenario reproduces the observed edge energies and continuum curvature, satisfies all constraints, and implies a multiphase intracluster medium, though it poses challenges for grain formation and survival in hot cluster cores. We discuss implications for cooling-flow mass deposition and abundances.

We investigate bilayer graphene nanoribbons with zigzag edges using a tight-binding model, comparing two stacking configurations, @xmath0 and @xmath1. In @xmath0, we observe energy band splitting, whereas @xmath1 exhibits splitting along the wave-number direction. Local density of states calculations reveal that, in @xmath1, edge states preferentially avoid sites with interlayer hopping. These results clarify stacking-dependent electronic features and inform design of bilayer graphene nanostructures.

We present two-epoch polarimetric Very Long Baseline Array observations of the BL Lac object 0735+178 at 22 and 43 GHz. These highest-resolution images to date reveal a twisted parsec-scale jet exhibiting two sharp apparent bends of about 90 degrees within 2 milliarcseconds of the core. The linear polarization structure indicates that the magnetic field smoothly follows at least one bend, consistent with field ordering and suggestive of a precessing nozzle at the jet base. Proper motion measurements of compact features are insufficient to determine whether the morphology arises from ballistic knot trajectories or flow guided along a curved jet axis. We discuss implications for jet dynamics and geometry and emphasize the need for continued monitoring.

We show that for every Banach space @xmath0, the Lipschitz-free space over @xmath0, denoted @xmath1, is isomorphic to @xmath2. As applications, we develop a non-linear analogue of Pełczyński’s decomposition method for Lipschitz-free spaces and obtain identifications for broad classes of metric spaces. In particular, we prove that @xmath3 is isomorphic to the Lipschitz-free space over any compact metric space locally bi-Lipschitz embeddable into @xmath4 and containing a subset Lipschitz equivalent to the unit ball of @xmath4. We further show that @xmath5 is isomorphic to @xmath6 for all separable metric spaces @xmath7 which are absolute Lipschitz retracts and contain a subset Lipschitz equivalent to the unit ball of @xmath8. This class includes all @xmath9 spaces with @xmath10 infinite compact metric; in this setting, Dutrieux and Ferenczi had previously established that @xmath11 is isomorphic to @xmath6 by a different method. Finally, we study Lipschitz-free spaces over unions and quotients of metric spaces, extending a result of Godard and providing new tools for permanence and decomposition in the Lipschitz-free framework.

We present an analysis of the colour–magnitude and colour–velocity dispersion relations for a sample of @xmath0 brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) drawn from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), and compare them to relations for a control sample of 37,000 non-BCG early-type (E/S0) galaxies of similar luminosity. Using de Vaucouleurs structural parameters and colours measured at the half-light radius, we find that the slopes of the colour–magnitude and colour–σ relations for BCGs are significantly flatter—by factors of two or more—than those of non-BCG E/S0s at comparable luminosity (@xmath1). Moreover, the @xmath2 colours of BCGs at the half-light radius are @xmath3 magnitude redder than those of the comparison sample. To quantify radial colour structure, we employ a gradient estimator based on the ratio of de Vaucouleurs effective radii in the @xmath4 and @xmath5 passbands, @xmath6. With this measure, the mean colour gradient of BCGs is flatter by @xmath7 than in other E/S0 galaxies of similar luminosity. In the non-BCG population, colour gradients show a pronounced dependence on galaxy properties: they are strongest at intermediate luminosities (@xmath8), decline toward both lower and higher luminosities, and decrease systematically with increasing velocity dispersion (@xmath9). Gradients also increase with larger effective radii (up to 10–12 kpc), and are negatively correlated with @xmath10 (a proxy for mass density) and with stellar age. Notably, post-starburst systems at the youngest ages can exhibit substantially reduced or even positive (inverted) colour gradients. In contrast, BCGs display none of these trends: their mean colour gradient remains at a relatively low level (@xmath11 by our measure) independent of luminosity, velocity dispersion, size, density, or age. The redder half-light colours of BCGs are consistent with a combination of slightly older stellar populations and intrinsically flatter radial colour gradients. We interpret these findings within a framework in which spheroidal galaxies initially possess colour gradients that are positively correlated with luminosity and with larger radius and/or lower density. Subsequent elliptical–elliptical dry mergers progressively diminish these gradients toward a low but non-zero value, with the most massive E/S0s—and especially BCGs—experiencing the greatest cumulative reduction. These results support a formation history for BCGs dominated by dissipationless assembly and enhanced stellar population homogeneity relative to other early-type galaxies. Keywords: galaxies: elliptical and lenticular, cD; galaxies: fundamental parameters; galaxies: evolution

We investigate the essence of the exciton Mott transition in three-dimensional electron–hole systems by studying a symmetric two-band Hubbard model with onsite electron–electron (hole–hole) repulsion U and onsite electron–hole attraction U′. Within dynamical mean-field theory, which is exact in infinite dimensions, we compute the phase diagram in the U–U′ plane under the constraint that electron–hole pairs do not condense (no excitonic or superconducting order). At half-filling, two distinct insulating states emerge: a Mott–Hubbard insulator stabilized by dominant repulsion (U > U′), and a biexciton-like insulator driven by strong interband attraction (U′ > U). When U and U′ are comparable, their competition can stabilize a correlated metallic phase, yielding well-defined phase boundaries between metal and both insulating states. Away from half-filling, the conventional Mott–Hubbard transition is suppressed, yet an insulating phase composed of bound electron–hole pairs (excitonic or biexcitonic) persists up to a critical attraction or carrier density, beyond which a metallic electron–hole plasma appears. We identify this metal–insulator transition as the exciton Mott transition. The results provide a unified, non-perturbative framework for interpreting metal–insulator phenomena in electron–hole systems and clarify the roles of repulsion, attraction, and filling in controlling exciton binding and delocalization.

Understanding collective reactions to individual actions is crucial for effective information propagation on social media. We define user efficiency on Twitter as the ratio between emergent spreading—measured by audience response and retweet reach—and the activity invested by a user. We conduct a quantitative analysis of structural and dynamical patterns across multiple Twitter conversations, demonstrating universal efficiency behavior across topics and events. Our findings reveal that a small set of influential users can trigger substantial collective reactions per message, whereas the vast majority must exert far greater effort to achieve comparable impact. To explain the observed efficiency distribution, we propose a model of retweet cascades that integrates empirical tweeting activity with the followers network topology. The model reproduces cascade sizes and shows that conversational dynamics are strongly conditioned by underlying degree heterogeneity. We conclude that the emergence of highly efficient users primarily reflects network structure rather than idiosyncratic behavior. These insights clarify mechanisms of information spreading and inform practical strategies for communication and campaign design. Keywords: complex networks, social network analysis, information spreading, user behavior, Twitter.

Old, high-redshift objects provide stringent clocks on the cosmic expansion history and the onset of structure formation. We revisit the cosmological implications of the quasar APM 08279+5255 at z ≈ 3.9, whose extremely high iron abundance implies an age of 2–3 Gyr. Adopting the conservative lower limit of 2 Gyr and the Hubble constant from the HST Key Project (H0 ≈ 72 ± 8 km s−1 Mpc−1), we require the cosmic age at the quasar redshift to exceed the object’s age and thereby constrain the matter and dark energy content of the Universe. For spatially flat models with a cosmological constant, this age test demands a large vacuum energy density, yielding ΩΛ ≳ 0.78 (Ωm ≲ 0.22) across the allowed H0 range, a requirement that is only marginally consistent with joint Type Ia supernova and cosmic microwave background inferences. We extend the analysis to flat quintessence models with a constant equation-of-state parameter w, treated as a smooth dark energy component. The quasar age bound forces dark energy to be both dominant today and strongly negative in pressure, with Ωx ≳ 0.77 and w ≲ −0.6; models with less negative w fail to provide sufficient lookback time at z ≈ 4. We also estimate the earliest plausible epoch of quasar formation by including an incubation time for black hole growth and chemical enrichment. For incubation times of 0.2–1 Gyr, the formation redshift is pushed to zf ≳ 8–15, highlighting a very early assembly of massive structures. These results underscore the power of high-redshift age indicators in testing dark energy scenarios and ruling out Einstein–de Sitter–like cosmologies.

We present VLA continuum observations at 3.6 and 6 cm of the Trifid Nebula (M20), a prominent optical H II region bisected by dark lanes. The data reveal thermal free–free emission from three compact stellar sources located within a few arcseconds of the central O7 V star. Their spectra and morphologies indicate externally ionized neutral envelopes or disks, consistent with photoevaporation driven by the UV field of the central star. We also report the discovery of a barrel-shaped supernova remnant, G7.06+0.12, on the northwest rim of M20, and identify two adjacent shell-like radio features, G6.67–0.42 and G6.83–0.21, bordering W28 and M20. We discuss their radio properties and possible shock interactions, and consider associations with PSR 1801–2306 and with W28 OH (1720 MHz) masers, highlighting implications for particle acceleration and molecular shock chemistry in this complex region.

We study the spectral function of a single hole in the one-dimensional t–J model augmented by a three-site hopping term and next-nearest-neighbor frustration J2. In the strong-coupling limit t/U → 0 of the Hubbard model, we construct a complete set of eigenoperators of the Liouvillian, which yields an exact expression for the one-particle Green’s function. This formulation is valid at finite temperature and for arbitrary magnetic backgrounds. Treating weak exchange corrections via the projection method, we recover the spinon dispersion of the pure t–J model with the Heisenberg ground state and quantify deviations induced by frustration and three-site processes. For the special frustrated point J2 = J/2, where the Majumdar–Ghosh dimerized wave function is the ground state, we present a detailed analysis of the spectral function. Complementing the projection approach, we employ a variational ansatz built from the eigenoperators of the kinetic t-term. We find a spinon dispersion that is symmetric around momentum k = π/2 and observe pronounced damping of the holon branch due to enhanced spin-charge scattering. Below the continuum, a discrete bound state emerges with finite spectral weight and an exceptionally small gap to the continuum threshold. Finally, we discuss the ideal paramagnetic regime at finite temperature, where incoherent continua dominate and quasiparticle features are strongly suppressed. Our results provide a unified, temperature-dependent framework for single-hole dynamics across distinct magnetic states in frustrated one-dimensional t–J systems. PACS: 71.27.+a, 73.20.dx, 79.60.Bm

This paper investigates the performance of a parallel iterated Runge–Kutta method compared with serial fourth-order Runge–Kutta and Dormand–Prince schemes. Across diverse benchmarks, the parallel method achieves runtimes comparable to serial implementations, despite incurring substantially greater computational resource usage. To address step-size selection, we introduce a fully parallel algorithm that estimates optimal integration steps via concurrent trials, integrating adaptivity with load-balanced execution. Empirical evaluations on large-scale ODE systems demonstrate superior accuracy-throughput tradeoffs and marked speedups, with improved stability and scalability. The proposed method notably outperforms existing approaches in integrating very large systems.

We present a quantitative, room‐temperature method that uses a sensitive quantum sensor to resolve, in real time, the dynamics of magnetic materials in biological samples. Applied to American cockroaches, the approach detects sub‐micron magnetic deposits whose signals differ in living versus dead insects. Analysis of relaxation enables extraction of physical properties of the deposits and the surrounding matter despite their minute volumes, including characteristic timescales and effective viscosities. By linking dynamical magnetometry to biological context, our work bridges the gap between behavioural studies in magnetic fields and material characterisation in vivo. The data support a model in which the magnetic inclusions reside in a glassy, high‐viscosity environment, rendering simple compass‐like mechanisms too slow for normal biological function.

Engineered lattices in condensed matter, including cold atom optical lattices and photonic crystals, can exhibit properties unattainable in naturally occurring electronic crystals. Here we report a distinct form of artificial quantum matter: a multilayer heterostructure composed of alternating thin films of topological and trivial insulators. Each interface supports topologically protected electronic states; by reducing the layer thicknesses, we enable hybridization of these interface states across adjacent layers, thereby realizing an emergent one-dimensional atomic chain in which interfaces act as lattice sites and interface states serve as orbitals. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy directly visualizes the resulting superlattice band structure, revealing tunable minibands and gaps. By varying the chemical composition and thickness sequences, we control the effective hopping amplitudes between sites and drive transitions between topological and trivial phases of the superlattice. The phase evolution is consistent with a one-dimensional topological invariant closely related to the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, providing a compact characterization of the emergent bands. Our results establish topological insulator heterostructures as a versatile platform for band-structure engineering through direct control of interfacial hopping, opening avenues to designer topological phases, interface-localized transport, and quantum simulation of model Hamiltonians. This approach bridges crystalline topology and heterostructure design and enables exploration of coupled interface states beyond the limits of single-material crystals in experiment.

This work investigates the instability of a finite Fermi-liquid drop against bulk density distortions. We derive and analyze the dispersion relation, showing that the presence of a surface produces an anomalous dispersion term that markedly suppresses the growth rate of bulk instabilities. The destabilization is further mitigated by Fermi-surface distortions and finite relaxation processes, which slow the amplification of density modes. The multipolarity dependence of the instability is quantified, and illustrative calculations are presented for two representative nuclei, @xmath0 and @xmath1, highlighting finite-size and mode-structure effects across parameter regimes.

We analyze a lattice model of critical dense polymers @xmath0 on a finite cylinder. Non-contractible loops with fugacity @xmath1 generalize the solution of Pearce, Rasmussen, and Villani at @xmath2. Using Temperley–Lieb algebra and a free-fermion representation of the transfer matrix, we compute the exact finite-size free energy for arbitrary height @xmath3 and circumference @xmath4. We extract the density @xmath5 of non-contractible loops at @xmath6 and for large @xmath4, and determine scaling corrections. The results are benchmarked against an anisotropic XXZ quantum chain with twisted boundary conditions, showing complete agreement. Leveraging the quantum-chain approach, we obtain @xmath5 for any @xmath0 model and arbitrary fugacity @xmath1, expressed in terms of spanning-graph observables. We also analyze universal finite-size corrections for cylinder geometries. Keywords: dense polymers, free fermion model, spanning graphs, XXZ chain, Temperley–Lieb algebra.

We study tunneling of conduction electrons through (110)-oriented single-barrier heterostructures made of III–V semiconductors. Owing to the barrier’s reduced spatial symmetry, the tunneling current acquires a finite spin polarization. Conversely, spin-polarized carriers generate a tunneling current, revealing a spin-galvanic effect. We develop a microscopic theory based on scattering approaches, incorporating Dresselhaus spin–orbit coupling in the barrier and Rashba coupling at the interfaces. Analytical expressions for spin-resolved transmission and current are derived, including bias, energy, and crystallographic dependences. Numerical estimates for representative systems indicate sizable signals and tunability by interface asymmetry. The results suggest experimental detection and routes for spintronic device design.

Renormalisation scheme ambiguities hinder QCD predictions when relating observables. We propose a prescription that fixes ambiguities by requiring the coefficients in the perturbative relation to take their conformal-limit values, i.e. to be independent of the @xmath0-function of the renormalised coupling. Building on the Brodsky–Lepage–Mackenzie (BLM) approach, we extend automatic scale fixing from next-to-leading to next-to-next-to-leading order, uniquely determining both the renormalisation scale and @xmath1. The method reorganises series so @xmath0-dependent terms are absorbed into effective scales, yielding scheme-invariant coefficients. As an illustration, we apply it to the relation between the Bjorken sum rule and @xmath2, obtaining improved convergence and reduced scale dependence, consistent with current data. We compare with alternative scheme-fixing methods and discuss phenomenological implications.

We present a zero-temperature, phase-space description of macroscopic quantum tunneling in open systems based on the master equation for the reduced Wigner function. The model consists of a single particle trapped in a metastable cubic potential and linearly coupled to an environment that induces dissipation together with normal and anomalous diffusion. By expanding the Wigner function in the energy eigenfunctions of the isolated Hamiltonian, the master equation acquires a compact form; in this representation, WKB eigenfunctions incorporate tunneling of the uncoupled system, while environmental effects enter through drift and diffusion terms that closely parallel a Fokker-Planck operator. Decoherence emerges transparently as the rapid suppression of off-diagonal energy components. When the decoherence time is much shorter than the intrinsic tunneling time, the dynamics reduces to a Kramers-like equation in energy space that describes activation over the barrier driven by zero-point fluctuations of the quantum environment. In this regime we obtain explicit energy drift and diffusion coefficients and corresponding escape rates. The contribution of anomalous diffusion can be treated perturbatively; it renormalizes the transport coefficients and, overall, significantly inhibits tunneling by decreasing the activation current and lowering the escape probability.

Harmonic lasing offers an attractive mode of operation for X-ray free-electron laser (FEL) user facilities by enabling access to higher photon energies at a given electron beam energy, while the harmonic lasing self-seeded FEL (HLSS FEL) concept promises substantial improvements in spectral brightness. Until now, harmonic lasing has been demonstrated only in FEL oscillators at infrared and visible wavelengths, with no evidence in high-gain FELs or at short wavelengths. We report the first experimental evidence of harmonic lasing in a high-gain FEL and the first operation of an HLSS FEL at the soft X-ray FEL user facility FLASH, covering the 4.5–15 nm wavelength range. By suppressing the fundamental and enhancing gain at higher harmonics, and by seeding downstream undulator sections with harmonically generated radiation, we achieved a marked improvement in spectral properties. In the exponential gain regime, the spectral brightness exceeded that of self-amplified spontaneous emission (SASE) by a factor of six, accompanied by reduced bandwidth and enhanced longitudinal coherence. In the post-saturation regime with undulator tapering, HLSS FEL operation delivered higher pulse energy and preserved superior spectral quality relative to SASE. The demonstrated stability and reproducibility indicate compatibility with routine user operation. These results establish harmonic lasing and HLSS FEL as practical modes for X-ray FELs, expanding the accessible photon energy range and enabling higher spectral brightness for applications in high-resolution spectroscopy, resonant scattering, and coherent imaging. This advance paves the way for broader deployment of harmonic lasing strategies across existing and future X-ray FEL facilities.

Gamma-ray loud BL Lac objects exhibit spectral energy distributions (SEDs) with two broad humps, commonly attributed to synchrotron radiation by relativistic electrons and inverse-Compton upscattering (SSC). Hadronic alternatives, in which accelerated protons and their cascades produce the high-energy component, offer different multi-messenger predictions. We present a variation of the synchrotron proton blazar (SPB) model in which electrons and protons are co-accelerated in the jet, the low-energy hump arises predominantly from electron synchrotron radiation, and the high-energy hump is produced chiefly by proton synchrotron radiation accompanied by synchrotron–pair cascading. As an approximation, we adopt non-relativistic shock acceleration in the jet frame, appropriate if the bulk plasma is non-relativistic, and we discuss the potential impact of a relativistic equation of state on the inferred parameters. We consider conditions under which the maximum proton energy exceeds the threshold for pion photoproduction on the internal synchrotron photon field, and we simulate the ensuing interactions and cascades with a combined Monte Carlo/numerical approach. The treatment includes proton synchrotron losses, photopion production, muon and electron/positron synchrotron radiation, gamma–gamma absorption, and pair cascading. Applying this framework to the April 1997 flare of Markarian 501, we obtain fits to the observed high-energy gamma-ray portion of the SED without invoking extreme external photon fields. Our results indicate that cascade spectra initiated by gamma rays from neutral-pion decay and by leptons from charged-pion decay are relatively featureless and do not dominate the TeV output. Synchrotron radiation from muons can contribute, but the principal high-energy component is reproduced by proton synchrotron radiation and its associated synchrotron–pair cascade. In the preferred fit, proton synchrotron emission dominates the TeV band, while photopion processes are subdominant, implying a significantly lower neutrino flux than in proton blazar scenarios where photopion production is the primary gamma-ray source. This prediction aligns with current neutrino constraints and provides a testable discriminator among hadronic models. The model favors strong magnetic fields and efficient proton acceleration to ultra-high energies, with internal gamma–gamma absorption shaping the emergent spectrum. While the non-relativistic acceleration assumption simplifies the analysis, adopting a relativistic equation of state could alter detailed parameter estimates and merits future investigation. Overall, this SPB variant offers a viable alternative to SSC for BL Lac flares like that of Markarian 501, naturally accounting for the smooth TeV spectra and suggesting low neutrino yields, with specific multiwavelength and multi-messenger signatures that forthcoming observations can probe.

We apply quasi-elastic light scattering to quantify how the tropomyosin/troponin regulatory complex modulates the mechanical stiffness of actin filaments in semidilute solutions. To interpret the dynamics, we introduce a concentration-dependent expression for the dynamic structure factor of semiflexible polymers that explicitly incorporates hydrodynamic screening in the semidilute regime. This framework collapses the concentration dependence of the scattering data and yields a concentration-independent bending modulus. Using this analysis, we find that the bending modulus of actin increases by approximately 50% upon binding of tropomyosin and troponin at a 7:1:1 molar ratio of actin:tropomyosin:troponin. In addition, a new expression for the initial slope of the dynamic structure factor enables determination of the effective hydrodynamic diameter of the actin filament directly from the early-time decay. These results validate the central role of hydrodynamic screening in semidilute polymer solutions and support the general relevance of intrinsic semiflexibility for understanding polymer dynamics and protein-mediated mechanical regulation.

Classical search algorithms are outperformed by Grover’s quantum algorithm, which offers a quadratic speedup, and by Brüschweiler’s hybrid ensemble algorithm, which achieves exponential speedup. In this work, we experimentally realize Brüschweiler’s algorithm in a seven‐qubit NMR ensemble and introduce a simplified, more robust read‐out scheme. Tailored pulse sequences implement the oracle and iteration steps on the register and an ancilla spin. Unlike the original method, which requires quantitative measurement of the ancilla’s spin projection, our approach exploits the shape of the ancilla spectrum: the downwardness or upwardness of peaks directly encodes the bit value of the marked state. This geometric read‐out reduces calibration demands, mitigates amplitude and phase errors, and enhances resilience to decoherence and inhomogeneity. We verify correct identification of the marked item over instances and analyze signal-to-noise and error tolerance. These results demonstrate error‐robust ensemble implementations of hybrid quantum search and highlight NMR as a viable platform for quantum algorithm benchmarks. PACS numbers: 03.67.Lx, 82.56.Jn, 76.60.-k.

We examine non-minimally coupled scalar-field dark energy models and demonstrate their equivalence to interacting quintessence in the Einstein frame. For two representative potentials—nearly flat and thawing—we derive analytic expressions for the equation-of-state parameter w(Omega_phi) valid across parameter choices. Using the statefinder diagnostic, we compute and plot the evolutionary trajectories of the r,s and r,q pairs, identifying departures from LambdaCDM (r=1, s=0) and locating characteristic signatures of non-minimal coupling. We assess stability, tracker behavior, and observational viability, highlighting how statefinder paths constrain coupling strength and potential shape with current and forthcoming data.

We develop an off-shell extension of s-channel unitarity to describe deep inelastic scattering at low x and elastic vector meson production in virtual photon–proton interactions. Within this framework we derive the small-x behavior of the structure function F2(x, Q2) and the total γ* p cross section, predicting a power-like energy rise whose exponent λ(Q2) is directly related to the interaction radius of a constituent quark. The energy dependence of the total γ* p cross section is calculated, and an explicit meson-mass dependence of the exponent governing the power-law energy behavior in γ* p → V p production is obtained, providing a unified description across light and heavy vector mesons. We further analyze angular distributions at large momentum transfers, highlighting characteristic t-dependences implied by unitarity. PACS numbers: 12.40.Pp, 13.60.Hb, 13.60.Le.

We introduce MAGIC, an efficient and broadly applicable framework for covariance estimation and signal reconstruction in Gaussian random fields from noisy, contaminated, and incomplete measurements. Motivated by a long-standing challenge in cosmic microwave background (CMB) data analysis, MAGIC enables global inference of covariance structure while remaining general to spatial and temporal fields beyond the CMB domain. The method targets the full, typically non-Gaussian joint posterior of the latent signal and covariance parameters (e.g., power spectra) given observed data, thereby delivering principled uncertainty quantification and robust parameter estimation. In contrast to approaches that rely on evaluating the likelihood or its derivatives, MAGIC draws an asymptotically exact Monte Carlo sample from the posterior, avoiding costly optimization and numerical instabilities. Conceptually, MAGIC generalizes the Wiener filter: instead of requiring a fixed signal covariance, it learns signal correlations directly from the data under a specified noise model and with priors encoding knowledge about potential contaminants and systematics. This yields coherent reconstructions and covariance estimates even in the presence of masking, censoring, or nontrivial foregrounds. We present applications to CMB power spectrum estimation and signal recovery, demonstrating that MAGIC achieves speed-ups of many orders of magnitude relative to likelihood maximization techniques while increasing modeling flexibility. The method provides full posterior summaries for both signals and covariance parameters, including credible intervals and joint uncertainties, enabling rigorous propagation of errors into downstream scientific inferences. These results establish MAGIC as a scalable, accurate tool for global covariance inference and signal reconstruction in complex, real-world observational settings.

Motivated by the recent calculation of Chay and Rey, we analyze instanton-induced contributions to the lepton energy spectrum near the endpoint in inclusive heavy flavor decays. Using an ansatz inspired by studies of high-energy baryon number violating processes, we estimate the magnitude of these nonperturbative corrections. We compare their impact with that on the photon energy spectrum in radiative @xmath0 decays, testing the assumed shape-function universality. We find that instantons can violate this universality unless the spectra are smeared over a much wider energy window than previously thought. This conclusion affects the reliability of extracting @xmath1 from inclusive decays, and constrains endpoint-based precision measurements in the presence of instantons.

Protein–ligand interactions often reorganize the populations of thermally accessible conformations, allowing proteins to tune binding affinity and sensitivity through changes in their functional energy landscapes. Here, we investigate the structural origins of binding affinity and allosteric cooperativity associated with the binding of two Ca2+ ions to each domain of calmodulin (CaM) using simulations of a simple coarse-grained model. In this framework, conformational transitions between open and closed ensembles are simulated explicitly, while ligand binding and unbinding are treated implicitly within a grand canonical ensemble via a ligand chemical potential. The simulations reveal that ligand binding is cooperative because binding sites are coupled through a population shift in the dominant conformational ensemble upon ligand association. Remarkably, the classic Monod–Wyman–Changeux model, parameterized with distinct binding free energies for the open and closed ensembles, quantitatively captures the simulated binding thermodynamics and titration behavior. The results further predict domain-specific differences: the C-terminal domain of CaM exhibits higher Ca2+ affinity and stronger cooperativity than the N-terminal domain. At the structural level, the affinity of an individual binding loop depends sensitively on its compatibility with the ligand in the bound ensemble and on the conformational flexibility of the binding site in the unbound ensemble, which together set the enthalpic gains and entropic costs of binding. These findings provide a mechanistic link between ensemble redistribution and cooperative binding, offering a minimal, physically transparent description of CaM allostery and suggesting testable design principles for tuning affinity and cooperativity through targeted mutations that modulate loop compatibility and site flexibility.

We propose and analyze a minimal quantum processor built from an ensemble of electron spins coupled to a stripline cavity and an ancillary, non-destructive photon-number readout. Beyond serving as a multi-qubit quantum memory, the collective spin modes form an addressable register in which entangling operations are generated measurement-based, using cavity-mediated interactions and heralded projections. Theory and numerical modeling indicate that many logical qubits can be encoded, manipulated, and read out with high fidelity, while remaining robust to dominant errors, including inhomogeneous broadening, spin dephasing, cavity loss, and finite readout efficiency. The required quantum non-demolition detector answering “are there n photons in the cavity?” has been demonstrated experimentally, enabling near-term tests. Our results transform this architecture from storage to scalable processing and computation.

We investigate quantitative unique continuation for partial differential equations with underlying multiscale structure, motivated by applications in random Schrödinger operators and control theory. We survey recent advances and announce new results for Schrödinger and second-order elliptic operators with rough, multiscale coefficients. A key feature is scale-free quantitative estimates with explicit dependence on dimension, ellipticity, potential norms, and spectral parameters, uniform across all length scales. The principles apply to functions satisfying rigidity conditions: exact solutions or projections onto spectral subspaces. The proofs hinge on multiscale-adapted Carleman estimates and propagation-of-smallness inequalities. Consequences include Wegner-type bounds, observability and null-controllability estimates, and stability under perturbations in discrete and continuum settings.

The Gottesman–Knill theorem implies that non-Gaussian states are essential resources for nontrivial quantum computation. We present two efficient, deterministic protocols to generate target non-Gaussian states of a single-mode cavity field using a single trapped ion in a trapped-ion–cavity platform. Both schemes rely on coherent transfer of the ion’s quantized motional state to the cavity mode and are compatible with current experiments. The first protocol adapts established techniques for preparing finite motional superposition states, yielding arbitrarily accurate approximations to the desired non-Gaussian cavity states. We derive Wigner-function criteria that bound and quantify the approximation error and negativity. The second, novel protocol produces exact non-Gaussian states with a single laser pulse, simplifying control and reducing decoherence. We analyze parameter regimes and robustness, confirming near-term feasibility.

We formulate the Phase I dose-finding problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem. Using recent advances in approximate dynamic programming, we derive a feasible approximation to the Bayesian optimal design. The resulting policy is a convex combination of a treatment-oriented rule, exemplified by Babb et al.’s Escalation with Overdose Control, and a learning-oriented information-optimal rule in the spirit of Haines et al., thereby balancing patient safety and information gain. We describe implementation details, including state summarization by posterior quantities, adaptive mixing weights driven by predictive risk, and efficient value-function approximation. Through simulations across toxicity scenarios and model misspecification, the proposed design achieves strong overdose control, improved identification of the maximum tolerated dose, and a higher proportion of patients treated near the target, outperforming or matching established competitors. We also present a pragmatic two-stage variant that begins with cautious step-up/down escalation to validate the parametric model before transitioning to the model-based policy, facilitating practical routine clinical application.

This review examines how biological-scale self-organization arises in two paradigmatic active matter classes: self-propelled colloidal particles and extensile rod-like particles. We survey recent experiments and theories demonstrating macroscopic structures unattainable in equilibrium, including motility-induced phase separation, living crystals, and defect-driven active nematic turbulence. Simple physical mechanisms—autonomous propulsion, density-dependent motility, hydrodynamic and steric interactions, and internally generated extensile stresses—are outlined through minimal models, continuum descriptions, and simulations. We emphasize connections to biological systems, robust design principles, and routes to controllable transport, mixing, and pattern formation. Open challenges in quantifying fluctuations, topological dynamics, and multi-component coupling are discussed, highlighting opportunities for new materials that harness nonequilibrium energy to achieve adaptive, functional behavior and resilience.

Hybrid inorganic/organic systems (HIOSs) derive their observable properties and functions from the adsorption geometry and stability of organic molecules at inorganic surfaces. Despite notable advances in experimental metrology and first-principles electronic structure theory, comprehensive and reliable databases of structures and energetics for large adsorbates remain scarce. This review addresses that gap by assembling a benchmark database for a broad set of molecules adsorbed on metal single-crystal surfaces. The collection spans noble-gas atoms, conjugated aromatic molecules, carbon nanostructures, and heteroaromatic compounds on five different metals, with high-quality experimental adsorption heights and energies compiled under carefully controlled conditions. We use this dataset to assess current and emerging electronic structure methods, focusing on the van der Waals (vdW)-inclusive density-functional theory approach, dft+vdw@xmath0. Across 23 adsorption heights and 17 adsorption energies, dft+vdw@xmath0 yields mean absolute deviations of 0.06 Å and 0.16 eV, respectively, demonstrating accuracy and computational efficiency for HIOSs over a diverse chemical and interfacial space. The analysis highlights outstanding challenges that warrant further methodological development, including the treatment of interfacial screening and anisotropy, coverage and polymorphism effects, temperature and vibrational contributions, charge transfer and dipole formation, and the influence of defects and step edges. By providing a curated, diverse, and critically evaluated reference, this benchmark database offers a robust foundation for validating electronic structure methods, guiding improved vdW treatments, and motivating targeted experimental campaigns to refine and expand reliable adsorption data for complex organic–inorganic interfaces.

Soft X-ray spectroscopy of Seyfert 2 galaxies offers a probe of the connection between active galactic nucleus (AGN) activity and circumnuclear star formation. In Type 2 systems, nuclear continuum obscuration enables detailed study of extended emission, distinguishing warm, radiatively driven gas powered by the AGN from hot, collisionally excited plasma linked to star formation. We analyze high-resolution spectra obtained with XMM-Newton and Chandra for five Seyfert 2 galaxies. A simple biconical model of gas photoionized and photoexcited by a nuclear power-law continuum reproduces the observed soft X-ray line spectra, including He-like triplets, radiative recombination continua, and resonance-scattered features, without invoking significant thermal components. We place an upper limit of 10% on any additional hot, collisionally driven contribution to the soft X-ray emission in all targets. These constraints imply modest circumnuclear star formation and favor AGN-dominated ionization and energetics on kiloparsec scales. Our results link soft X-ray and optical narrow-line region diagnostics and provide a benchmark for future resolved observations.

Neuromorphic chips aim to instantiate the computational principles of nervous systems directly in microelectronic substrates. A central reusable cognitive primitive is attractor dynamics in recurrent networks, where point attractors encode memorized patterns and their basins of attraction confer robustness to noise and partial cues, enabling associative memory. While prior neuromorphic implementations demonstrated attractor dynamics with fixed synapses, here we address autonomous learning on chip. We configure a recurrent network of spiking neurons with local, on-chip synaptic plasticity and select network parameters using theory-driven criteria that balance excitation, inhibition, and plasticity stability. Repeated presentation of simple visual stimuli drives neural activity that, through the ensuing synaptic dynamics, shapes a connectivity structure supporting stimulus-selective point attractors. After learning, the network exhibits rapid convergence to the appropriate attractor from degraded or ambiguous inputs, indicating the emergence of sizable basins and robust recall. Learning and retrieval occur within the same ongoing dynamics, without an artificial separation of phases, supervisory signals, or off-chip updates. We quantify the stability of learned attractors, selectivity, and robustness to noise and perturbations, and show agreement with theoretical predictions for recurrent attractor networks. These results demonstrate that autonomous, low-latency, and low-power associative memory can develop directly on silicon through coupled neural and synaptic dynamics, establishing attractor-based computation as a practical and reusable primitive for neuromorphic cognition and paving the way for scalable on-chip learning in real-world sensory tasks.

We present Chandra LETG+HRC-S spectroscopy of the young white dwarf H1504+65, with an effective temperature of about 200,000 K, the hottest post-AGB object yet analyzed with detailed model atmospheres. The observations reveal the richest X-ray absorption-line spectrum ever recorded from a stellar photosphere. In this extremely hot atmosphere, the line-forming layers imprint numerous transitions in absorption that are observed in emission from cool-star coronae. Using state-of-the-art non-LTE model atmospheres tailored to H1504+65, we identify a wealth of absorption features from highly ionized oxygen, neon, and magnesium. Systematic comparison of these photospheric spectra with Chandra coronal spectra of Procyon and Alpha Centauri A and B enables identifications of coronal lines whose origins had remained unknown. Our analysis establishes H1504+65 as a laboratory for line formation, provides improved atomic line assignments for coronal diagnostics, and constrains physical conditions in extreme post-AGB photospheres, linking stellar photospheric and coronal plasmas.

Ellerman bombs (EBs) are transient reconnection-driven events in the lower solar atmosphere. Recent observations with the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS) have suggested links between EBs and IRIS bombs (IBs), implying that some EBs might reach temperatures as high as @xmath0 K. To test this, we analyze EBs observed simultaneously by the Fast Imaging Solar Spectrograph (FISS) and IRIS. The events show clear signatures of lower-atmospheric heating, including pronounced wing enhancements in H@xmath1, Ca II 8542, and Mg II triplet lines, together with localized brightenings in the 1700 and 2832 ultraviolet continuum channels and temporal evolution. The Mg II triplet intensity correlates strongly with H@xmath1 during EB occurrence, indicating that the triplet can serve as an alternative diagnostic for EB identification. In contrast, we find no co-spatial or co-temporal signals in the hotter IRIS lines C II and Si IV, arguing against temperatures sufficient to generate distinct IB-like ultraviolet signatures. Using a two-cloud radiative transfer model to fit the H@xmath1 and Ca II 8542 profiles simultaneously, we infer a temperature enhancement of about 2300 K for a strong EB. This value is among the highest reported by previous EB modeling yet remains below the threshold needed to produce IB signatures, reinforcing that EB heating is confined to the lower chromosphere and upper photosphere.

We present mid-infrared observations of the gravitationally lensing clusters A370, A2218, A1689, and CL0024+1654 obtained with the Infrared Space Observatory (ISO) using ISOCAM at 6.7 μm and 14.3 μm (hereafter 7 μm and 15 μm). We detect 178 sources, 70 of which are cluster members, enabling comparisons with field populations. For a subset, we construct spectral energy distributions (SEDs) with GRASIL and derive total infrared luminosities and star formation rates for non-stellar objects. In A2218, most cluster galaxies are best matched by quiescent elliptical models, consistent with low star formation. In CL0024+1654, galaxies in the Butcher–Oemler region of the color–magnitude diagram are preferentially fit by disk-dominated SEDs, while those on the main sequence exhibit post-starburst characteristics. We identify a significant population of luminous infrared galaxies (LIRGs) in CL0024+1654, contrasted by only a single LIRG in total across A370, A1689, and A2218. The elevated LIRG incidence in CL0024+1654 supports a link between infrared activity and recent or ongoing cluster merger processes. Comparisons with field sources and with other clusters indicate that environment strongly modulates infrared luminosity functions and star formation histories. Our findings underscore the importance of wide coverage: many dusty, star-forming cluster members likely reside in the outer regions where tidal interactions and infall are prevalent. Extending mid-infrared surveys to larger radii will be critical for capturing the full demographic of cluster star formation and for clarifying the role of dynamical state in triggering LIRG activity.

We propose a multi-Pomeron exchange potential (MPP) as a universal microscopic origin of three- and four-baryon repulsions in dense matter. The MPP strength is constrained by analyses of nucleus–nucleus elastic scattering with a G-matrix folding model based on realistic baryon–baryon interactions. Incorporating the calibrated MPP into neutron matter, we construct an equation of state that stiffens at supranuclear densities. Solving the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff equations yields neutron-star mass–radius relations with a maximum mass exceeding the ~2 solar-mass observations, while remaining consistent with experimental scattering data. Our results highlight a common repulsive mechanism that reconciles nuclear reactions with astrophysical constraints.

We numerically validate the mean-field approximation for bosonic many-body systems by tracking the time evolution of quantum states and their reduced density matrices under Schrödinger dynamics on finite-dimensional phase spaces. Using second quantization in Fock space, we compute many-body trajectories and monitor convergence toward mean-field predictions, interpreting limits via Wigner measures. Systematically varying particle number, phase-space dimension, interaction strengths, and time scales, we quantify rates of convergence and stability, identify preasymptotic regimes, and assess finite-size effects. The simulations corroborate propagation of chaos and provide practical error estimates for reduced descriptions in bosonic settings.

We report a statistical analysis of civic engagement in Brazil’s electoral processes by relating, across all municipalities, the number of party memberships and the number of candidates for mayor and councillor to the size of the electorate. Using scaling and distributional methods, we show that the dependence of engagement metrics on the number of voters is captured by sub‐linear power laws (allometric scaling) with multiplicative log‐normal fluctuations. These results parallel previously reported scaling for the number of candidates versus electorate size (EPL 96, 48001, 2011), suggesting the presence of robust, universal mechanisms governing political engagement across urban scales. A clear hierarchy emerges among the estimated exponents: the more influential the political position, the smaller the scaling exponent, indicating that engagement grows more slowly with city size for positions of greater political power. Analysis of the distributions reveals differences by position. For the most influential offices, the distributions are short‐tailed, consistent with strong constraints and limited variability. In contrast, less influential positions exhibit intermediate power‐law regimes across decades, followed by exponential‐like cutoffs, signaling greater heterogeneity tempered by finite‐size effects. We argue that both the perceived and institutional power of the position and structural limitations in the number of available seats contribute to these patterns, with seat constraints relevant for mayoral races and council chambers. Taken together, our findings point to an underrepresentation effect: as cities grow, barriers to direct participation—becoming a candidate or party member—increase disproportionately, resulting in sub‐linear scaling of engagement. These empirical regularities provide quantitative evidence for scaling laws in political behavior and have implications for designing institutions that foster broader participation in large urban settings.

Neutrinoless double beta decay of 76Ge is a sensitive probe of lepton number violation and the Majorana nature of neutrinos. The IGEX experiment operates high-purity germanium detectors enriched in 76Ge at the Canfranc Underground Laboratory (Spain) to search for this rare process, where stringent suppression of radioactive background near the Q-value is essential. We present the implementation and performance of pulse shape discrimination (PSD) techniques developed to distinguish single-site energy depositions expected from 0νββ events from multi-site interactions characteristic of gamma-ray backgrounds. Waveforms are digitized and analyzed using time-structure parameters and pattern-recognition classifiers calibrated with external gamma sources and internal peaks. The PSD selection was validated with extensive simulations and calibration data to ensure high signal acceptance and stability under underground operating conditions. Applied to a subset of the IGEX exposure, the PSD analysis rejects approximately 60% of the background in the region of interest from 2.0 to 2.5 MeV, reducing the background index to about 0.2 counts/(keV·kg·y). This reduction is achieved with minimal loss of 0νββ efficiency, thereby increasing the experiment’s discovery sensitivity and strengthening the derived lower limits on the 76Ge neutrinoless double beta decay half-life. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of PSD in enriched germanium detectors and provide guidance for background control in future large-scale 76Ge-based searches.

We present luminosity functions for star cluster populations in 20 nearby (within ~430 Mpc) star-forming galaxies constructed from Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) source lists generated by the Hubble Legacy Archive (HLA). These uniformly processed, automatically generated catalogs constitute one of the largest and most homogeneous compilations of candidate clusters currently available. We compare the HLA-derived catalogs with several recently published cluster catalogs and find comparable overall quality, though the HLA samples are generally shallower and do not reach the faintest clusters in each system. The cluster luminosity functions (LFs) are well approximated by a power law, with a mean slope near −2 in the F814W (I) band and an rms scatter of 0.18 across the sample. Fits derived from methods using both binned and unbinned (maximum-likelihood) data show good mutual consistency, although the unbinned approach tends to yield slightly more negative slopes in galaxies with steeper LFs, indicating a small systematic difference between methodologies. We identify weak but suggestive trends linking global galaxy properties to LF slope: systems with higher star formation rates (and correspondingly brighter, more numerous clusters) exhibit a slight tendency toward shallower slopes, and later Hubble types (Sd–Sm) appear to host flatter LFs than earlier types. Notably, the Antennae (NGC 4038/39), a merging system with an elevated star formation rate, shows one of the flattest LFs in the sample. Despite these trends, the overall similarity of LF slopes among diverse star-forming galaxies argues that, to first order, cluster LFs are fairly universal. At the bright end, we find evidence for a downturn affecting only about 1% of clusters, consistent with either stochastic sampling effects or subtle physical truncations. Leveraging the uniformity of our database, we recover a tight relation between the magnitude of the brightest cluster and the logarithm of the number of clusters brighter than a fixed threshold, with a small scatter of approximately 0.4–0.5 mag. Extending this analysis to a broader sample spanning dwarf galaxies to ultraluminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs), we find that the correlation between brightest cluster magnitude and the logarithm of the star formation rate holds over roughly six orders of magnitude, albeit with larger scatter, likely driven by high and spatially variable extinction in many luminous infrared galaxies. These results provide robust benchmarks for models of cluster formation and statistical sampling across diverse galactic environments.

Polarized and unpolarized neutron diffraction measurements on single crystals of the coupled spin-tetrahedra systems @xmath0 (x = Cl, Br) determine the long-range magnetic order. Incommensurate ordering with propagation vectors @xmath1 and @xmath2 appears below @xmath3 = 18 K (Cl) and @xmath3 = 11 K (Br). Symmetry analysis and refinements reveal a common canted coplanar arrangement of the four Cu@xmath4 spins per tetrahedron, rotating helically from cell to cell along the propagation vector. Refined Cu@xmath5 moments are 0.395(5)@xmath6 for Br, substantially smaller than 0.88(1)@xmath6 for Cl at 2 K, indicating stronger quantum fluctuations in the bromide. For the chloride, the structure tied to wave vector @xmath7 differs from that previously reported for @xmath8 [O. Zaharko et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. @xmath9, 217206 (2004)]. These results provide a unified microscopic model for @xmath0, constrain dominant exchange pathways, and underscore the roles of frustration and anisotropy in stabilizing canted helical order.

We present a spectroscopic study of 37 Balmer break galaxies spanning 0.045 ≤ z ≤ 0.93, selected for possessing the emission-line coverage required to place them on star-forming versus active galactic nucleus (AGN) diagnostic diagrams. The sample is, on average, somewhat less massive than comparable samples in previous works and benefits from multiwavelength photometric coverage from the ultraviolet to the mid-infrared (Spitzer/IRAC). Our primary goal is to investigate the connection between star formation and AGN activity using optical line-ratio diagnostics, the Mass–Excitation (MEx) diagram, and mid-infrared color diagnostics. Optical diagnostics classify 31 galaxies (84%) as star-forming, 2 (5%) as composites, and 3 (8%) as AGN. In contrast, the MEx diagram identifies only one AGN across the sample, highlighting classification discrepancies that likely arise from differences in mass–excitation calibration and line-ratio sensitivity. Nineteen galaxies have complete IRAC coverage; among these, three additional AGN candidates emerge from MIR colors despite lacking AGN signatures in the optical, suggesting dust-obscured nuclei or dilution by strong circumnuclear star formation. We perform spectral energy distribution fitting to derive stellar masses, dust reddening, ages, and UV-based star formation rates (SFRs). Using [O II] λλ3727, 3729 and Balmer line luminosities, we estimate SFR surface density and the stellar mass surface density growth rate per unit time, finding that both quantities increase with redshift. This behavior indicates more intense star formation and faster mass assembly at earlier epochs, consistent with cosmic downsizing. We further examine SFR and specific SFR (sSFR) as functions of stellar mass and rest-frame color. More massive galaxies exhibit higher absolute SFRs yet lower sSFRs than less massive systems, reflecting decreasing relative growth efficiencies with increasing mass. At fixed mass, higher-redshift galaxies have larger SFR and sSFR, in agreement with prior studies. In addition, bluer galaxies show systematically elevated sSFR relative to redder counterparts, and for a given color, sSFR increases with redshift. These results support a picture in which star formation intensifies and AGN activity is sometimes obscured at higher redshift, emphasizing the value of combining optical, mass–excitation, and MIR diagnostics to capture the full diversity of galaxy growth and nuclear activity.

Introducing explicit electronic polarizability into classical molecular simulations promises improved accuracy and predictive power. One practical approach employs Drude oscillators, massless auxiliary particles whose displacements mimic induced dipoles. Here, we perform extensive molecular dynamics simulations of SWM4-NDP, a Drude-based water model, across 170–340 K to evaluate its thermophysical and structural behavior over a broad temperature range. The model exhibits a density anomaly deep in the supercooled region, with the maximum near 200 K, approximately 80 K below the experimental value. At lower temperatures, we observe extremely long relaxation times and a secondary increase in density, indicative of sluggish dynamics and possible metastability. Despite these deviations in the density curve, structural metrics including hydrogen-bond coordination through the second solvation shell and tetrahedral order closely track those of TIP4P/2005, a benchmark nonpolarizable model known to reproduce bulk water properties and the temperature dependence of density. This decoupling between density anomalies and hydrogen-bond propensity is not seen in other conventional water models, suggesting a specific shortcoming of the current SWM4-NDP parametrization. Our results highlight both the appeal and limitations of simplified Drude-based polarizable water models, and underscore the need for refined parameters or functional forms to reliably capture water’s behavior beyond ambient conditions and in deeply supercooled regimes as well.

We introduce a generalized class of entangled coherent states (ECS) tailored for multi-arm optical interferometry and analyze their performance in simultaneous estimation of multiple phase shifts. Using quantum Fisher information, we derive quantum Cramér–Rao bounds for both linear and nonlinear parameterization protocols and quantify precision scaling with resources. Our results show that, in the collective estimation setting, the generalized ECS achieve tighter bounds than generalized NOON states reported in Phys. Rev. Lett. 111, 070403 (2013). Furthermore, relative to independent estimation, both linear and nonlinear protocols exhibit the same advantage as the number of parameters grows, highlighting multiplexed metrological gains.

We comment on the recent proposal by Almheiri, Marolf, Polchinski, and Sully (AMPS) that challenges black hole complementarity by positing a “firewall” that burns an infalling observer at the horizon. We analyze measurements available to an infalling observer while still outside the horizon and show that, within semiclassical accuracy, the statistical outcomes are indistinguishable between two scenarios: a vacuum state at the horizon and outgoing quanta sourced by a stretched horizon. This indistinguishability prevents a definitive inference about horizon regularity from exterior observations and compels a treatment of dynamics up to, and including, the horizon, where Planck-scale physics becomes essential. In string theory, the fuzzball structure of black hole microstates suggests there is no smooth continuation through a Planckian regime into an interior, thereby modifying the traditional complementarity narrative. While AMPS argue that near-horizon interactions obstruct complementarity, we highlight a distinct conjecture—fuzzball complementarity—where the infalling quantum is absorbed by the fuzzball surface and the ensuing collective dynamics admits an effective, complementary description for appropriate probes. We clarify the regimes in which such an effective description might approximate smooth infall, contrast it with the AMPS firewall conclusion, and discuss implications for unitarity and the information paradox. Our analysis underscores the necessity of microstate-sensitive, Planck-scale input to resolve near-horizon physics.

We investigate optimal discrimination of N mixed quantum states with a fixed rate of inconclusive outcomes (FRIR). For general ensembles in a d-dimensional Hilbert space we formulate the optimization as a semidefinite program with a single Lagrange parameter enforcing the inconclusive constraint, derive necessary and sufficient optimality conditions, and analyze the non-uniqueness of optimal measurements. Specializing to qubits, we present a constructive method, based on the Bloch-sphere geometry and complementary slackness, that yields families of optimal POVMs. We obtain closed-form solutions for several classes of ensembles, including partially symmetric qubit states, N equiprobable qubit states, and the discrimination between a pure state and a uniformly mixed state in d dimensions. Our results characterize the trade-off between success and inconclusive probabilities, identify the transition between boundary and interior optima, and delineate regions with multiple optimal measurements. In the limit of zero inconclusive rate our framework recovers minimum-error discrimination of arbitrary qubit states and provides an alternative treatment to previous approaches. We also discuss existence conditions for optimal POVMs. Numerical examples corroborate the analytical formulas.

We theoretically investigate how superlattice architectures control single-particle transport along the c axis of high-temperature superconductors by analyzing periodic stacks comprising normal metals or insulators alternating with d-wave superconducting layers (NS/IS superlattices). In the limit of a strongly anisotropic carrier mass in the metallic layers, the low-energy density of states of NS superlattices retains the characteristic bulk d-wave form; however, the principal quasiparticle coherence peak is shifted to energies substantially smaller than the superconducting gap amplitude. In contrast, for IS superlattices the coherence peak remains pinned at the d-wave gap scale. Using a microscopic scattering approach to the Bogoliubov–de Gennes problem, we further compute the nonlinear differential conductance for planar c-axis junctions. We find that the zero-bias Andreev feature is highly sensitive to the superlattice geometry: multiple Andreev reflections across the periodic superconducting layers interfere destructively, narrowing the zero-bias peak and producing a resonant-like profile. This pronounced narrowing provides a clear transport signature of superlattice-induced phase interference and offers a natural explanation for recent experimental observations of unusually sharp zero-bias Andreev peaks in c-axis tunneling through layered cuprate heterostructures at interfaces.

We calculate electric dipole (E1) excitations in a set of nuclei using a phenomenological random-phase-approximation framework and analyze the evolution of strength distributions along isotope chains of oxygen, calcium, zirconium, and tin. Increasing neutron excess generates additional E1 strength at low excitation energies. To quantify collectivity, we introduce indices based on transition amplitudes and configurations, and we examine proton and neutron transition densities to diagnose the isoscalar versus isovector character of the modes. In medium-heavy systems, the low-energy E1 response exhibits properties markedly distinct from the giant dipole resonance, including limited collectivity and surface-peaked neutron oscillations. These features support the identification of a pygmy dipole resonance as a neutron-driven excitation in neutron-rich nuclei.

The ANTARES Collaboration is constructing a deep-sea neutrino telescope in the Mediterranean Sea to open the high-energy neutrino window on the Universe. The detector will instrument a sensitive area of approximately 0.1 km2 with about 1000 optical modules (OMs) that record the Cherenkov light emitted by relativistic charged particles produced in neutrino interactions. Each OM comprises a large-area photomultiplier tube and front-end electronics integrated within a pressure-resistant glass sphere; this unit is the fundamental sensing element of the array. We report the finalized OM design following extensive research and development, guided by the constraints of the deep-sea environment and the demands of precise timing, high quantum efficiency, low noise, and long-term reliability. Key choices include the photomultiplier type and magnetic shielding, optical coupling materials and internal background mitigation, low-power high-voltage generation, waveform timing and amplitude readout, and remote control and monitoring. The mechanical housing, penetrators, and seals are engineered for resistance to high hydrostatic pressure, corrosion, and biofouling, while maintaining optical clarity and wide angular acceptance. Calibration provisions—embedded light sources, clock distribution, and acoustic positioning—ensure sub-nanosecond timing synchronization and accurate geometry knowledge. We summarize qualification tests (pressure, thermal cycling, vibration, and aging) and in-situ background characterizations due to bioluminescence and 40K decays, and present performance metrics: single-photon sensitivity, transit-time spread, dynamic range, and dark count rates. A modular architecture with wet-mateable connectors facilitates installation and replacement, and integration with the data acquisition and trigger systems supports robust operation. The readiness for mass production and deployment on moored lines is established. The ANTARES optical module design underpins the detector’s capability to perform neutrino astronomy with a deep-sea Cherenkov telescope.

We present deep 3.6 cm radio continuum observations of the H II region NGC 2024 obtained with the Very Large Array in its A configuration, achieving high angular resolution. We detect 25 compact sources within the surveyed field. Cross-matching with infrared and X-ray catalogs reveals counterparts for many objects, indicating a mixture of thermal and nonthermal emission mechanisms, including hypercompact H II regions, thermal jets, and magnetically active young stars. At least two radio sources are obscured proplyds whose cometary morphologies constrain the location of the dominant ionizing source in NGC 2024. We compare this radio cluster with others in recent star-forming regions, discussing implications for feedback and disk photoevaporation in this embedded cluster.

We study the impact of an extra @xmath0 gauge boson with flavor-changing couplings to fermion mass eigenstates on @xmath1 meson decays that are sensitive to such new-physics effects. Focusing on the case in which the flavor-changing interactions are left-chiral, we analyze current data on @xmath2, @xmath3, and @xmath4 decays and delineate the viable parameter space. We show that, within reasonable ranges of masses and couplings, the @xmath5 contribution can readily accommodate the anomaly in @xmath6, while it cannot simultaneously account for the large branching ratio of @xmath3 with the same parameter choices. The observables @xmath6 and @xmath7 emerge as the leading constraints on the additional weak phase, yielding definite correlations and testable predictions for CP asymmetries and rare decay rates overall.

We investigate superfluid pairing of massless Dirac fermions interacting via a Yukawa coupling to a massive scalar boson. In a mean-field Nambu–Gor’kov framework, we derive and solve gap equations for condensates with total spin zero. For scalar exchange, the chiral structure enforces gaps for right- and left-handed fermions that are equal in magnitude and opposite in sign, selecting a spin-singlet pseudoscalar channel. At finite boson mass, the gap spectrum for a given chirality splits into two branches associated with particle–particle and antiparticle–antiparticle condensation, which become degenerate in the limit of infinite boson mass, where the interaction reduces to a local four-fermion form. We chart how the gaps depend on coupling and boson mass and delineate regimes dominated by particle or antiparticle pairing. The condensate breaks global U(1) number symmetry, producing a gapless mode and fully gapped quasiparticles. These results isolate the impact of chirality and finite-range interactions on relativistic BCS pairing and furnish a baseline for extensions beyond mean field. We also discuss temperature and density dependences, renormalization of contact limit, and interplay between particle and antiparticle contributions.
