The three parent models (@xmath4-, @xmath5-, and @xmath6-models) are isomorphic, differing only by the neighbor shell associated with the single exchange constant @xmath13. We discuss common properties of such isomorphic cluster models and the consequences for MST spectra and perimeter-polynomial statistics, providing a unified framework for interpreting MSTs in diluted square-lattice antiferromagnets.

We propose a communication-driven mechanism for predicting triadic closure in complex networks. The approach is mathematically formulated using communicability distance functions, defined through matrix functions of the adjacency matrix, to quantify the quality of communication between node pairs. We evaluate the method on a broad collection of real-world networks and show that it predicts a large fraction of forthcoming triadic closures, substantially outperforming a random mechanism. Beyond link prediction, the communication-driven model better accounts for global and mesoscopic descriptors, including the clustering coefficient, average path length, and average communicability. The framework also reveals principled strategies for optimizing communication by targeting nodes and paths that minimize communicability distances. These findings highlight communicability as a robust driver of triangle formation and provide actionable tools for analyzing and engineering complex networks.

We present a systematic, uniform study of the X-ray emission properties of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in globular clusters using high-resolution Chandra observations cross-correlated with precise radio timing positions. This approach yields 31 secure X-ray counterparts across nine clusters, including 47 Tuc, and leverages unpublished datasets for M28, M4, and NGC 6752 to refine identifications and constraints. For all counterparts, we performed photometry, spectral extraction, and timing analyses to the extent permitted by the archival Chandra temporal resolution, and computed energy fluxes and luminosities assuming established cluster distances. For 36 additional radio MSPs with no detected X-ray source, we derived counting-rate and flux upper limits in a consistent bandpass, enabling robust population-level comparisons. The detected MSPs exhibit spectra that are well described by nonthermal power-law components (typical photon indices ~1–2) and, in several cases, soft thermal emission consistent with polar cap heating (kT ~0.1–0.3 keV), with 0.5–8 keV luminosities spanning ~10^30–10^32 erg s^-1. For PSR J1821–2452 in M28 and 47 Tuc pulsars J0024–7204D, O, and R, the X-ray and radio pulse profiles show notable phase correspondences, suggesting a common magnetospheric origin for at least part of the emission. The inferred X-ray efficiencies relative to spin-down power are in good agreement with those of Galactic field, rotation-powered pulsars, indicating that MSPs in globular clusters and in the Galactic plane share similar X-ray emission characteristics and do not display distinct, environment-driven differences.

We revisit Rømer’s 1676 demonstration of a finite speed of light and propose an analogous, direct measurement of the propagation speed of gravitational waves using stable, periodic gravitational-wave “clocks.” As Earth or a heliocentric detector orbits the Sun, the light-travel time across the orbital diameter imprints a characteristic annual modulation in the observed times of arrival of a coherent signal. For gravitational waves, this Rømer delay appears in the phase of a long-lived, nearly monochromatic source and permits an absolute measurement of the wave propagation speed without recourse to electromagnetic counterparts or assumptions about source physics. We analyze the feasibility of this measurement for foreseeable space-based and terrestrial detectors. For a LISA-like mission, Galactic close white-dwarf binaries provide abundant, stable signals in the millihertz band with high signal-to-noise ratios and year-long coherence. Using simple Fisher-information estimates that incorporate detector orbital motion, source sky localization, and phase stability, we find that a single well-measured binary can constrain the gravitational-wave speed to better than a part in 10^3 after one year of data; combining multiple binaries will improve this further. Systematic uncertainties from detector timing, spacecraft ephemerides, and intrinsic source evolution are expected to be subdominant at this level. For terrestrial detectors, rapidly rotating, non-axisymmetric neutron stars would produce continuous waves in the audio band. Although such sources may be rare and challenging to detect at required amplitudes, a detected, phase-stable signal observed coherently for a year would enable a Rømer-type measurement with precision at or better than a part in 10^6, leveraging Earth’s orbital baseline and precise timing calibration. These measurements provide a direct, model-independent probe of the propagation speed of gravitational radiation, complementing multimessenger constraints and offering a robust test of general relativity.

We report on the design basis of the TESLA linear collider employing 9-cell 1.3 GHz superconducting niobium cavities operated in pulsed mode, and on the results from the TESLA Test Facility (TTF) at DESY supporting cavity R&D toward higher accelerating gradients. Over sixty nine-cell cavities have been fabricated and tested, achieving peak gradients up to 30 MV/m; the second TTF production series reached an average gradient of 24.7 MV/m. Two cryomodules, each hosting eight resonators, are currently installed in the TTF linac and operated with 0.8 ms constant-gradient rf pulses at repetition rates up to 10 Hz. The paper addresses two central themes. First, we review fabrication routes and surface treatment protocols, mechanical processing, chemical polishing, high-pressure rinsing, and cleanliness controls, that enable high-gradient performance, and we present the latest single-cell results exceeding 40 MV/m. Second, we analyze key aspects of pulsed operation, including Lorentz-force detuning, microphonics, and rf field regulation. Strategies for detuning mitigation and field stabilization based on tuner control and combined feedback/feedforward are discussed together with experimental data from module operation. The demonstrated gradients and operational stability inform the design of next-generation superconducting linacs and have relevance to proton drivers such as the SNS linac.

We investigate nuclear attenuation of multi-hadron systems within the string model, employing an improved two-scale hadronization framework calibrated to single-hadron attenuation data. Using the established parameter set, we compute multiplicity ratios for electroproduced one-, two-, and three-hadron systems on nuclear and deuterium targets. We analyze their dependence on hadron energy fraction, virtuality, nuclear size, and hadron rank, and identify systematic differences among the channels. The model reproduces existing single-hadron trends and yields quantitative predictions for multi-hadron multiplicity ratios versus convenient kinematic variables, offering tests of space-time hadron formation and intranuclear interactions in forthcoming measurements.

Compact binary inspirals are among the most promising sources of gravitational waves for current and planned ground- and space-based laser interferometers. The strain they imprint on detectors is accurately modeled by waveforms described by a modest set of intrinsic and extrinsic parameters, making matched filtering and maximum-likelihood estimation the standard tools for detection and inference. In conventional searches, the continuous parameter space is discretized into a bank of templates chosen so that the normalized inner product (correlation) between neighboring templates is typically 0.97, a choice that limits mismatch losses for threshold-strength signals but leads to a dense covering and substantial redundancy in the matched-filter evaluations. Because the computational cost of searches is dominated by evaluating the matched filter across the bank, this redundancy constrains the parameter volume that can be surveyed in practice. We present a simple and practical interpolation strategy that exploits the strong correlation of matched-filter outputs at nearby parameter points to reduce the number of explicit template evaluations without degrading detection efficiency at a fixed false-alarm probability. Rather than evaluate the filter at every point of a densely packed grid, we evaluate it on a sparser set and interpolate the statistic across the gaps, using the smooth dependence of the filter output on the parameters. As a proof of concept, we compare the traditional dense-sampling approach with our interpolated approach along a single intrinsic parameter dimension relevant for inspiral signals. Tuning both methods to the same false-alarm probability, we find that the interpolated search achieves the same detection probability while requiring 25% fewer explicit matched-filter evaluations than a dense search with 97% template correlation. Extrapolating these savings to higher-dimensional searches suggests a roughly twofold gain in computational efficiency for the two-dimensional subspace typically used in current resource-limited analyses, and an order-of-magnitude gain for a full seven-dimensional model appropriate to eccentric binaries with spin. Because reductions in the number of matched-filter evaluations translate directly into reductions in wall-clock time and resource consumption, the proposed methodology can be traded for increased sky coverage, broader mass and spin ranges, inclusion of eccentricity, or more sophisticated noise modeling. The approach is straightforward to implement within existing pipelines and maintains the robustness and optimality characteristics of matched filtering while leveraging otherwise unused information in the smooth structure of the template manifold. We discuss considerations for non-Gaussian, non-stationary noise, multi-detector coherent combinations, and adaptive grid refinement, and outline how polynomial or spline-based interpolants can be extended across multiple intrinsic parameters to deliver scalable savings in forthcoming ground and space interferometer searches.

We present VLBI observations of GRB 030329 obtained 217 days after the 2003 March 29 burst. The new measurements of the afterglow’s angular size and centroid refine the apparent expansion rate and proper motion of this nearby GRB. We find evidence for a slowing expansion, which favors a shock propagating into a constant-density interstellar medium rather than a stratified circumstellar wind with an r^-2 density profile. Complementary late-time Arecibo spectroscopy of the redshifted H I 21-cm and OH 18-cm lines shows no absorption or emission, yielding stringent upper limits on the columns of atomic and molecular gas along the sightline. Finally, Very Large Array observations constrain the late-time radio polarization of the afterglow to be below a few percent. These results provide constraints on the circumburst environment and jet dynamics of GRB 030329.

We propose a non-perturbative method to compute derivatives of gauge couplings with respect to anisotropic lattice spacings (anisotropy coefficients), required for thermodynamic observables from lattice simulations. Our approach exploits a precise determination of the finite-temperature deconfinement transition line in the extended coupling-parameter space of anisotropic lattices, using the spectral density method. We validate the method for @xmath0 and @xmath1 gauge theories at the deconfinement point on lattices with temporal extent @xmath2=4 and 6. In both theories, the extracted anisotropy coefficients exhibit clear deviations from perturbative estimates. A longstanding issue when employing perturbative coefficients is a nonvanishing pressure gap at the deconfinement transition in @xmath1. With our non-perturbative coefficients, this problem is completely resolved: the pressure gap is consistent with zero, yielding @xmath3 and @xmath4 on @xmath2=4 and 6 lattices, respectively. Our results demonstrate the importance of non-perturbative determinations of anisotropy coefficients for reliable thermodynamics, and provide a practical, accurate framework applicable to a wide range of lattice gauge theories and anisotropy regimes. Potential extensions to improved actions and larger temporal extents are straightforward.

We investigate symmetry breaking and front dynamics in arrays of symmetric bistable Lorenz units coupled via nearest neighbors. As the coupling strength increases, fronts undergo a sequence from standing through oscillating to travelling states. Using numerical simulations and phase-space analysis, we show that, in a parameter range, this transition is organized by a gluing bifurcation in which two cycles coalesce in a planar reduction, enabling an asymptotic expression for the front velocity near depinning. When the gluing instead involves a saddle-focus equilibrium, the ensuing Shilnikov scenario induces rich dynamics, including multi-periodic oscillations, intermittency, and chaotic front propagation. We chart the bifurcation structure and identify scaling laws governing the onset of motion. Comparisons with alternative coupling schemes and with other discrete bistable media reveal the universality and limits of these mechanisms, clarifying how coupling topology shapes wave selection, pinning–depinning thresholds, and homoclinic chaos.

We present infrared (@xmath0) photometry of 52 isolated Be stars spanning spectral types O9–B9 and luminosity classes III–V. We develop a new reduction method that disentangles interstellar reddening from circumstellar continuum excess, enabling measurements of disc contributions. Applying this technique, we show that disc emission contributes at most a few tenths of a magnitude to the optical @xmath1 color. We further identify strong correlations between emission-line strengths (H@xmath2, Br@xmath3, Br11, Br18) and the circumstellar excesses, linking line formation to disc continuum. Finally, we find a significant correlation between stellar rotation and disc excess, supporting rotation-driven disc feeding.

We introduce a new class of algorithms for valence‐bond quantum Monte Carlo (VBQMC) applied to quantum spin models. VBQMC is a projective Monte Carlo method that samples operator strings, which can be organized as paths on a rooted, tree‐like structure. We reformulate VBQMC dynamics in terms of a worm that traverses this tree, modifying the associated operator string through local moves. Within this framework, we derive a set of general equations whose solutions define transition rules and acceptance criteria for broad families of worm updates, ensuring the correct stationary distribution and efficient exploration of configuration space. As concrete instances, we present two algorithms. The bouncing worm employs symmetric up‐and‐down traversals with locally constructed probabilities such that updates are always accepted, delivering low rejection overhead and robust mixing. The driven worm introduces a single control parameter that governs the maximum depth reached before a single bounce, enabling targeted sampling of longer operator strings; an analytically determined acceptance probability maintains detailed or global balance. We analyze ergodicity, computational complexity, and scaling, and provide benchmarks on bipartite Heisenberg antiferromagnets demonstrating substantial reductions in autocorrelation times and improved projector convergence compared to conventional VBQMC updates. The approach is simple to implement, uses only local tree information, and is broadly extensible to diverse spin Hamiltonians.

Using extensive density functional theory, we elucidate the adsorption mechanism of 1,4,5,8‐naphthalene tetracarboxylic dianhydride (NTCDA) on Ag(110). Calculations reveal site-selective bonding governed by electron transfer from the substrate into the molecular LUMO and electrostatic attraction between negatively charged carboxyl oxygens and positively charged silver atoms in @xmath0 atomic rows. The most stable adsorption geometry aligns the carboxyl groups with these rows, maximizing charge redistribution and stabilizing the interface, with an adsorption energy of @xmath1 eV. The work-function modification and densities of states corroborate the charge-transfer picture and weak hybridization of the aromatic core. Given the structural and electronic similarity, a comparable adsorption mechanism is predicted for perylene tetracarboxylic dianhydride (PTCDA) on Ag(110), consistent with decades of experimental observations.

SuperKEKB, the upgrade of the KEKB heavy-flavour factory at KEK, targets a design luminosity of 8 x 10^35 cm^-2 s^-1, about 40 times KEKB, necessitating comprehensive upgrades of the Belle detector. The vertex detector will comprise a four-layer silicon strip tracker surrounding a two-layer pixel detector based on DEPFET technology positioned closest to the interaction point. We outline the pixel detector requirements: minimal material budget, high granularity, low noise, radiation tolerance, and fast, low-power readout; and summarize the DEPFET principle and system design. Performance from prototypes and system tests is reported, together with the production status, integration plans, and readiness for early SuperKEKB operation.

We revisit a simplified model for PLD introduced in PRL 87, 135701 (2001), reformulating with rate equations for adatom and island populations. We analyze two variants: (i) point-like islands, yielding an exactly solvable set capturing early-time dynamics over the first few pulses but failing at longer times; and (ii) finite-size islands with size-dependent capture, integrated numerically. The latter reproduces kinetic Monte Carlo simulations across parameters and quantitatively describes the crossover from continuous flux to pulsed deposition, including pulse frequency and intensity effects. We further examine the scaling of nucleation density with pulse interval and coverage, finding systematic deviations from previously suggested logarithmic scaling. Our results clarify the regimes of validity and provide predictive tools for PLD growth control.

We report new high spatial and velocity resolution Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope observations of the nearby system HIZSS003, originally discovered in a blind H I survey of the Zone of Avoidance. Previous Very Large Array imaging, together with optical and near-infrared photometry and spectroscopy, established HIZSS003 as a low-metallicity dwarf irregular galaxy, but raised two puzzles: ongoing star formation traced by Hα emission appeared confined to a small region at the edge of the VLA H I map, and the metallicity of older red giant branch stars seemed higher than that of the ionized gas in the H II region. Our GMRT data resolve these discrepancies by revealing that HIZSS003 is in fact a close galaxy pair. The H II region coincides with the center of a much smaller companion, HIZSS003B, while the bulk of the previously mapped H I belongs to the larger primary, HIZSS003A. Although the H I emission of the two galaxies overlaps in projection, we cleanly separate their contributions in velocity space. HIZSS003B exhibits a compact H I distribution and a highly disturbed velocity field indicative of strong tidal influence or recent accretion; the disturbance precludes a reliable rotation curve, but allows an estimate of its indicative dynamical mass. In contrast, HIZSS003A shows an extended, regularly rotating H I disk, from which we derive a well-behaved rotation curve and a total dynamical mass. The spatial association of the Hα emission with HIZSS003B explains the apparent edge-confined star formation, and the metallicity offset between the RGB population and the H II gas arises naturally from comparing different galaxies within the pair. These results highlight the importance of velocity-resolved H I imaging for disentangling projection effects in the Zone of Avoidance and for interpreting star formation and chemical abundance patterns in low-mass systems.

We study radially symmetric solutions to multi-dimensional gradient systems with a coercive potential. Under generic assumptions (finitely many nondegenerate minima and proper coercivity), we consider solutions stable at infinity, meaning they tend to a homogeneous equilibrium as the radial variable tends to infinity. Our main result shows that any such solution asymptotically decomposes into a finite, ordered stack of radially symmetric bistable fronts whose radii drift to infinity; between fronts the solution is close to distinct equilibria. The dynamics near infinity are governed by an energy/Lyapunov structure, and curvature effects are controlled to recover one-dimensional–like front interaction asymptotics. The behavior thus parallels the one-dimensional theory for gradient systems on unbounded domains developed in a companion paper. We also obtain quantitative bounds on front separation and propagation and show robustness under small perturbations of the potential. Finally, we conjecture, with partial evidence, that behind the receding fronts the time derivative vanishes and the solution converges to a stationary pattern.

In searches for permanent electric dipole moments (EDMs), experiments with stored gases confront systematic shifts arising from the interplay of the motional magnetic field (E × v/c^2) and static magnetic-field gradients, commonly called the geometric-phase effect. This interaction generates a frequency shift linear in the applied electric field and can mimic an EDM signal. We develop an analytic model for the velocity–position correlation function that governs this shift, deriving closed-form expressions across ballistic, diffuse, and intermediate collision regimes. The model explicitly incorporates cell geometry, wall scattering, gas species, pressure, temperature, and magnetic-field gradient profiles, revealing scaling laws and optimal operating regimes that suppress false EDMs. We validate the analytic results against Monte Carlo simulations and provide uncertainty estimates. Finally, we propose an in situ method to measure the relevant correlation function under the exact conditions of a given experiment using controlled gradient modulation and time-resolved comagnetometer readout.

The universe became fully reionized and optically observable at redshift @xmath0, limiting direct optical probes of earlier epochs. To access the earliest stages of galaxy formation, HI 21-cm and molecular absorption must be measured against higher-redshift, radio-loud background sources. However, no suitable targets are currently known. We present a new survey designed to identify radio-loud quasars at redshift @xmath1. The program combines wide-area radio selection with multi-band photometric filtering and spectroscopic confirmation. We outline the survey strategy, sensitivity, and initial candidate yield, and describe the prospects for absorption studies that will constrain cold gas, chemistry, kinematics, and the timeline of reionization.

We investigate stochastic resonance (SR) in periodically driven noisy systems beyond the well-studied bistable double-well case. Building on recent numerical evidence that SR can manifest in sinusoidal potentials through the area of hysteresis loops, we show that this resonance is not restricted to sinusoidal landscapes. Specifically, SR emerges robustly in periodic bistable potentials, demonstrating peaking behavior in the closed hysteresis loop area, which quantifies input energy loss per cycle. We further extend the analysis to washboard potentials, where hysteresis loops typically fail to close due to the average drift of particles. By explicitly correcting for the drift term to isolate cyclic response, we recover closed hysteresis loops and observe the canonical SR peak in energy dissipation, accompanied by a corresponding peak in the signal-to-noise ratio within a limited high drive-frequency regime. The occurrence of SR across these periodic potentials is attributed to the presence of effectively two dynamical states under driving, enabling noise-assisted transitions. This mechanism persists under weak tilting of the periodic landscapes, underscoring the generality of SR in driven periodic systems.

We analyze the elastodynamic response produced by a concentrated time-harmonic point force translating at constant speed through an unbounded, homogeneous, anisotropic, two-dimensional solid. Within a coordinate frame attached to the source, we characterize plane-wave kinematics via phase, slowness, and group (ray) velocity loci, delineating admissible propagation domains for sub-, trans-, and superseismic motions. Using Fourier integral transforms and these wave-geometry properties, we derive explicit finite-interval integral representations of the full elastodynamic Green’s tensor valid for arbitrary source speeds. We isolate the dynamic (radiative) parts of the tensor and, by applying the stationary-phase method, obtain asymptotic expressions for the far-field. Formulae for the Poynting vector and energy flux are given for both co-moving and laboratory observers, enabling a separation of cylindrical wave contributions in terms of kinematics and energy transport. The analysis reveals motion-induced modifications of the radiation pattern in anisotropic media, including the reshaping and multiplication of propagation sectors, the emergence of distinct fast and slow cylindrical waves, and qualitative changes at trans- and superseismic regimes. The results provide a framework for wave prediction from moving oscillatory sources in anisotropic solids and clarify interplay between anisotropy, source speed, and energy transport in two dimensions.

We investigate the structured nature of cosmic-ray energy spectra and its implications for particle origin and propagation. Emphasis is placed on large-scale features: the nuclear knee near 3 PeV, the shallow hardening of the combined electron-plus-positron spectrum around 100 GeV, and the upturn in the positron fraction beginning near 5 GeV. We define fine structure as residual, localized departures from smooth spectral models that already include these global features. Using high-precision AMS-02 measurements of the positron fraction, we construct baseline component spectra, propagate them through Galactic transport, and perform residual analyses with flexible parametric and non-parametric fits. No statistically compelling fine structure is detected; the data are consistent with smoothly varying spectra, with any putative features constrained to the few-percent level across 5–500 GeV. These limits inform models invoking nearby sources, spectral breaks, or charge-sign dependent transport, and delineate the sensitivity required for future measurements.

We present a calculation of the radial distribution functions (RDFs) of liquid water based on classical density functional theory (DFT) combined with the reference interaction site model (RISM) for molecular liquids. To overcome the limitations of the hypernetted-chain (HNC) approximation, bridge contributions to the Helmholtz free energy functional are incorporated via a density expansion truncated at third order. A factorization approximation expresses the ternary direct correlation functions in terms of site–site pair correlations, yielding a closed, self-consistent set of integral equations for the site-resolved RDFs. Numerical solutions at ambient conditions demonstrate that inclusion of the oxygen–oxygen bridge function markedly improves structural predictions, notably correcting the height and position of the second O–O peak and enhancing medium-range order relative to HNC. The approach retains computational efficiency and stability while providing consistent descriptions of O–H and H–H correlations. Comparison with experimental scattering data and simulations shows agreement within the first and second coordination shells. The framework offers a systematic route to refine bridge function models for associating liquids.

We investigate the nature of the multi-component radio continuum and H I emission associated with the nearby galaxy group dominated by the ellipticals NGC 5898 and NGC 5903 and the dwarf lenticular ESO 514-G003. Using 150 MHz images from the second data release of the ongoing TIFR GMRT Sky Survey (TGSS; sub-arcminute resolution; typical rms ≈ 5 mJy), together with archival higher-frequency radio continuum and H I data, we characterize the morphology, spectrum, and environment of the radio emission in this compact triplet. The TGSS image unveils a large, asymmetric, low-frequency radio halo around NGC 5903 and demonstrates that ESO 514-G003 hosts the previously known bright double-lobed radio source, now detected with high fidelity at 150 MHz. In NGC 5903, the diffuse emission exhibits a very steep integrated radio spectrum and envelopes a network of filamentary structures whose projected locations track segments of the extended H I trails, where the neutral gas is kinematically disturbed and likely accreting. Spectral behavior across the filaments indicates aged synchrotron plasma with local re-acceleration and/or compression where the radio plasma interacts with the cold gas streams. A notable environmental correlation emerges: the two radio-loud members (NGC 5903 and ESO 514-G003) are also the only galaxies that are directly connected to an H I filament, whereas NGC 5898 appears radio-quiet and detached from detectable H I. This pattern is consistent with a scenario in which cold gas accretion plays a prime role in fueling and triggering powerful jet activity in early-type galaxy nuclei. Our results highlight the diagnostic power of low-frequency surveys for revealing diffuse, filamentary radio structures and for linking episodic AGN feedback to the cold-gas ecosystem in nearby galaxy groups.

We investigate quantum effects of a Dirac field in d dimensions confined to regions with nontrivial boundaries and minimally coupled to an Abelian gauge field. Using a path-integral representation with boundary projectors, we compute the Casimir energy and derive the effective action induced by boundary modes in the presence of external gauge backgrounds. A systematic large-mass expansion is implemented, yielding geometry-independent coefficients expressed as boundary integrals of local invariants, and recovering universal terms such as edge Hall-like responses and gauge-invariant counterterms. The results hold for arbitrary smooth shapes and boundary conditions within the admissible class. We compare them with those extracted from the large-mass bosonized effective theory.

Prestress significantly influences the dynamic response of thin civil structures, and thermal prestress is a key factor in ambient vibration monitoring and structural health assessment. Yet, a systematic derivation of thin-structure models that coherently incorporate generic prestress, geometric nonlinearity, moderate rotations, and viscous damping from three-dimensional continuum mechanics remains elusive. This paper presents a new modeling framework that addresses this gap by introducing: (i) a modified Hu–Washizu functional augmented with stress constraints via Lagrange multipliers, enabling a transparent and rigorous dimensional reduction; (ii) original mechanical and thermal strain and rotation measures that isolate dominant energetic contributions and support a cascade of lower-dimensional models; (iii) the concept of strain–rotation domains that clarifies the classical regimes of small perturbations and small strains with moderate rotations, and delineates the validity of linearized versus geometrically nonlinear formulations; and (iv) a pseudo-potential of dissipation with stress constraints to represent viscous damping and its coupling with prestress and geometric effects. The procedure is specialized to thin beams and yields models that capture the interaction between prestress (including thermal effects), geometric nonlinearity, and damping in a unified manner. Analytical developments are complemented by parametric studies that quantify shifts in natural frequencies, mode coupling, and damping ratios across strain–rotation domains and under varying thermal fields and prestress states. The resulting framework provides a clear pathway from 3D continuum to reliable 1D beam models for ambient vibration analysis, offering enhanced interpretability of monitoring data and improved identification of prestress and thermal states. The approach is readily adaptable to other thin structures and establishes a foundation for robust, coupled thermo-mechanical-damped modeling in civil structural dynamics.

We reanalyze the @xmath0 transition form factor @xmath1 using QCD light-cone sum rules up to twist-4 accuracy. The calculation employs the pion leading-twist distribution amplitude with two nonasymptotic terms and twist-4 distribution amplitudes inspired by the renormalon method. This framework quantifies the impact of higher conformal-spin components in the twist-4 sector on the form factor @xmath2 across momentum transfers. Theoretical predictions are compared with CELLO and CLEO measurements, yielding constraints on the shape and moments of the pion distribution amplitudes and delineating ranges for nonasymptotic coefficients.

We present new measurements of charged kaon production in inelastic proton–proton interactions at a beam momentum of 158 GeV/c recorded with the NA49 detector at the CERN SPS. The analysis is based on a high-statistics sample of 4.8 million events. Charged kaons are identified via specific energy loss in a large-acceptance time projection chamber tracking system, enabling high-purity separation over a broad momentum range. Inclusive invariant cross sections for K+ and K− are determined differentially in transverse momentum, pT, from 0 to 1.7 GeV/c and in Feynman x, xF, from 0 to 0.5. The extraction includes detailed corrections for acceptance, tracking efficiency, and residual backgrounds, as well as assessments of feed-down, momentum scale, and normalization effects. The resulting spectra provide precise constraints on the shape and normalization of kaon production at SPS energies, improving on earlier measurements through extended kinematic coverage and reduced uncertainties. Charge-dependent features are quantified through K+/K− ratios as functions of pT and xF, and integrated yields and mean transverse momenta are obtained in well-defined phase-space intervals. Using these data as a reference, we perform a new evaluation of the energy dependence of kaon production, including neutral kaons, by compiling and harmonizing world data from fixed-target experiments near threshold (∼3 GeV) up to proton–antiproton collider energies. A consistent treatment of kinematic variables and normalization allows us to trace the evolution from associated kaon production at low energies to pair production dominance at high energies, revealing a smooth increase of yields with center-of-mass energy and a gradual hardening of the transverse momentum distributions. The K+/K− ratio approaches unity at collider energies, and neutral kaon production is consistent with expectations from isospin symmetry within uncertainties. These results provide a high-precision baseline for strangeness production in elementary collisions, support quantitative comparisons with heavy-ion measurements, and offer stringent tests for QCD-inspired particle production models and event generators. The data and derived energy systematics enable improved tuning and validation across a wide energy range.

Thermal transport at short length and time scales inherently exhibits nonlocal coupling between heat flux and temperature gradients, yet this is rarely treated explicitly in constitutive modeling. Here we introduce a general formalism that characterizes delocalization effects in nondiffusive regimes via a convolution kernel κ, termed the nonlocal thermal conductivity, which fully encodes the spatiotemporal memory linking heat flux to temperature gradients. We show that, under the relaxation time approximation, the phonon Boltzmann transport equation rigorously conforms to the proposed constitutive law and yields a generic expression for κ in terms of microscopic phonon properties, including spectra, group velocities, and relaxation times or mean free path distributions. We then establish a synergy with stochastic transport frameworks, enabling compact yet accurate models with transparent parameters that capture the essential physics. In particular, an analytical solution for κ in tempered Lévy transport with fractal dimension alpha and a diffusive recovery length identifies the spatial range over which nonlocality meaningfully alters heat flow, namely at distances shorter than the diffusive recovery length before conventional diffusion is recovered. This framework not only explains quasiballistic thermal conduction in semiconductor alloys but also parallels similar anomalous transport dynamics encountered in hydrology and chemistry. We further clarify the relationship between our intrinsic nonlocal conductivity and previously introduced effective thermal conductivities inferred from transient thermal grating and time-domain thermoreflectance experiments. While effective conductivities depend on experimental geometry and probing scales, the nonlocal thermal conductivity is an intrinsic material property. Experimental analyses indicate nonlocality lengths of approximately 400 nm in silicon membranes and on the order of micrometers in InGaAs and SiGe, consistent with typical median phonon mean free paths.

We develop a star-product scheme of operator symbols built from normally ordered powers of photon creation and annihilation operators. The associated phase space is a discrete two-dimensional lattice whose nodes are indexed by pairs of nonnegative integers. We obtain closed analytical expressions for the star-product kernel on the lattice and for intertwining kernels mapping to alternative symbol calculi. Analysis of structural features of the kernel yields new finite and infinite sum identities involving factorials. The proposed scheme offers computational and conceptual advantages for describing quantum dynamics, enabling direct derivation of time-evolution equations in terms of ordered moments. Illustrative applications are provided, including examples and comparisons to phase-space formalisms.

We study the Gaussian free field on @xmath0, @xmath1, and analyze percolation of its level sets. We prove that the critical density exhibits asymptotic behavior @xmath2 as @xmath3 tends to infinity. Our approach yields the principal asymptotics of the critical level @xmath4. Moreover, we show that the parameter @xmath5 introduced by Rodriguez and Sznitman in @xcite is asymptotically equivalent to @xmath4. Our findings refine key percolation thresholds and clarify parameter equivalences.

We assess the completeness and reliability of the DENIS @xmath0 survey and the EDSGC, derived from COSMOS scans of UKST plates, through extensive cross-identifications and systematic visual inspections of conflictual classifications. Our analysis demonstrates that the DENIS galaxy extraction is over 95% complete and reliable out to @xmath1, whereas the COSMOS/EDSGC galaxy catalogue is less than 80% complete and reliable at @xmath2 and declines to below 10% completeness at @xmath3. These discrepancies trace known limitations in photographic plate material and automated star–galaxy separation at low surface brightness and high confusion. To capitalize on the homogeneous near-infrared selection of DENIS and the similar 2MASS survey, we outline spectroscopic follow-ups: (1) a 6dF robotic multi-fiber spectrograph redshift survey of approximately 120,000 galaxies at the UKST, with 300 guaranteed nights in 2001–2003; (2) a peculiar velocity survey of 12,000 early-type galaxies with 6dF; and (3) the DENIS–HI peculiar velocity survey of 5,000 inclined spirals observable from Nançay (@xmath4), which has recently begun. The DENIS–HI and 6dF peculiar velocity samples will cover contiguous regions of the southern sky and, when combined, will increase the projected and space number densities of tracers in the south by factors of about 10 and 4, respectively. These surveys will yield considerably more accurate estimates of the bulk flow, @xmath5bias, @xmath6 itself, and the primordial density fluctuation spectrum. The improved completeness and reliability of near-infrared galaxy extraction, coupled with dense spectroscopic sampling, will provide a definitive southern-hemisphere foundation for mapping cosmic flows and constraining large-scale structure, and calibrating distance indicators robustly.

In this work we investigate which resource states admit efficient classical simulation of measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC). We show that the Schmidt-rank width, recently proposed to assess universality of resource states, is also the key parameter controlling simulatability. Specifically, we relate Schmidt-rank width to optimal tree tensor network (TTN) representations and prove that MBQC on any family of states whose Schmidt-rank width grows at most logarithmically with system size can be simulated in polynomial time. For graph states with such scaling, we efficiently construct optimal TTNs, leading to descriptions and tractable update rules under adaptive measurements. We give examples and bounds, and clarify interplay between entanglement structure and computational power. Our results highlight parallels between efficient descriptions in quantum information and width measures in graph theory, bridging TTNs, rank-width, and treewidth.

We present high-resolution HST imaging of the nebula associated with the Galactic LBV candidate HD 168625, complemented by ISO mid-infrared imaging and AAT echelle spectroscopy. The nebula exhibits an overall elliptical morphology with its major axis at a position angle of approximately 120 degrees. In Hα, the apparent dimensions are 12" × 16".7, while at 4 microns they are 15".5 × 23".5. The HST Hα image resolves the nebula into a complex network of filaments and arcs with markedly varying brightness. This asymmetry is diminished in the HST continuum image, where the nebula appears more diffuse and enriched in filaments and clumps displaying cometary-tail morphologies. At 11.3 microns, the nebular emission peaks in two diametrically opposed lobes located at the nebular boundaries along the major axis. A very faint loop is also visible at optical wavelengths to the north and south of the shell. Kinematic measurements from the echelle spectra indicate an expanding ellipsoid with projected axes of 14" and 9" (0.19 pc × 0.12 pc along RA and Dec, respectively), expanding at 19 km s^-1 and possessing a dynamical age of approximately 4800 years. The spatial coincidence of the infrared lobes with the caps of the ellipsoid, together with the mid-infrared characteristics, suggests PAH emission originating where the expanding shell interacts with the current stellar wind and the outer loop. Chemical diagnostics of the loop imply largely unprocessed material, likely interstellar gas swept up by the wind. These observations support a scenario of an aspherical shell whose morphology and infrared properties are governed by wind–shell interactions and the ambient ISM. The observations provide constraints on the mass-loss history and nebular shaping.

Motivated by the ATLAS and CMS reports of an excess in diphoton events at the LHC, we analyze the production and decay of a hypothetical neutral scalar resonance S at future e+e- colliders. Assuming S accounts for the diphoton excess and couples to Standard Model gauge bosons through effective operators, we study e+e- -> S gamma and e+e- -> S Z associated production, as well as vector-boson fusion channels e+e- -> e+e- S and e+e- -> nu nu S. We compute cross sections as functions of sqrt(s), the effective couplings, and the resonance mass and width, and we evaluate signal efficiencies and dominant Standard Model backgrounds. Discovery prospects are discussed for S decays into gamma gamma, Z gamma, ZZ, and WW, emphasizing the clean diphoton final state and the use of recoil-mass techniques. We also consider invisible decays of S and assess the sensitivity of mono-photon and mono-Z signatures to invisible branching fractions, including the role of beam polarization and forward-veto capabilities. Our results indicate that e+e- facilities operating from the Higgs-factory regime to the TeV scale can either discover S or exclude the parameter space consistent with the LHC anomaly, while providing precise measurements of its couplings and CP properties if observed. We present benchmarks and analysis strategies that optimize reach across collider energies and luminosities.

We investigate inflationary scenarios with nontrivial kinetic terms and show that the tensor contribution to cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies can substantially exceed expectations from canonical single-field inflation. The resulting enhancement of the tensor-to-scalar ratio produces a larger B-mode polarization signal, improving prospects for detection in forthcoming experiments. We derive the modified consistency relations, identify the conditions for significant enhancement, and discuss observational constraints. An important implication is a higher inflationary energy scale and correspondingly higher reheating temperature than in simple models. These features suggest distinctive signatures accessible to near-term CMB polarization measurements. LMU-ASC 78/05.

We investigate M82 B, an old starburst site in the eastern disc of M82, deriving age and metallicity distributions for its star clusters using evolutionary population synthesis. Based on multi-band photometry from de Grijs et al. (2001), we compare observed colours with single-generation stellar population models to constrain cluster parameters and recent history. The results indicate rapid chemical enrichment, with metallicities reaching super-solar values around the epoch of the last close encounter with M81. The age distribution shows a peak near 1 Gyr, confirming a burst of enhanced cluster formation triggered by that interaction. We also identify a distinct subpopulation of metal-poor clusters formed at approximately the same time in the sector of M82 B closest to the galactic centre. Their low metallicities are consistent with the infall of circumgalactic gas onto M82 B during or shortly after the encounter. These findings link spatial variations in cluster properties to the dynamical evolution of M82 and demonstrate the combined roles of tidal perturbations and gas accretion in shaping starburst environments.

Cosmic shear, the statistical weak lensing signal induced by large-scale structure, is a promising cosmological probe and has motivated the design of several forthcoming wide-field surveys. We present a measurement of cosmic shear using coadded Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) imaging over 168 square degrees in the equatorial region, with @xmath0 and @xmath1, a source number density of 2.2 per arcmin@xmath2, and a median source redshift of @xmath3. The coadds were produced with a new multi-epoch combination method described in a companion paper I @xcite, designed to minimize systematic errors from coherent point-spread function (PSF) anisotropies that are otherwise prevalent in SDSS single-epoch imaging. We measure shear two-point statistics out to angular separations of 2 degrees and perform extensive systematics tests which, together with the catalogue-level validations in paper I, demonstrate that the results are dominated by statistical rather than systematic uncertainties. Adopting a baseline cosmology corresponding to WMAP7 @xcite and allowing only the amplitude of matter fluctuations, @xmath4, to vary, we find a best-fit value of @xmath5 (1@xmath6); in the absence of systematic errors this would be @xmath7 (1@xmath6). Assuming a flat @xmath8CDM model, the joint constraints with WMAP7 are @xmath9(1@xmath6)@xmath10(2@xmath6) and @xmath11(1@xmath6)@xmath12(2@xmath6), with the 2@xmath6 error ranges reduced by 14 and 17 per cent, respectively, compared to WMAP7 alone. Beyond the intrinsic cosmological value of measuring the growth of structure with weak lensing, our analysis highlights practical lessons for upcoming surveys that will combine multi-epoch data to extract precise cosmic shear signals, including strategies for PSF control, coaddition, and rigorous systematics validation. Cosmology: observations. Gravitational lensing: weak. Surveys.

This paper is part of a series investigating galaxy formation and evolution in small-scale systems of galaxies (SSSGs) in low-density environments. We present a multiwavelength study of the NGC 4756 group, dominated by the elliptical galaxy NGC 4756, combining detailed morphology, surface photometry, and spectroscopy of nine dominant members; a census of the faint galaxy population over a 34 arcmin × 34 arcmin field centered on NGC 4756; and an analysis of archival X-ray data. The core of the group, extending over roughly 300 kpc in diameter for H0 = 70 km s−1 Mpc−1, exhibits a very loose configuration with a significant fraction of early-type galaxies. We identify three new group members with previously unknown systemic velocities, including a dwarf elliptical, thereby refining the group’s membership and internal structure. A notable substructure is detected approximately 7.5 arcmin southwest of NGC 4756, comprising IC 829, MCG 2-33-35, MCG 2-33-36, and MCG 2-33-38. This quartet satisfies the Hickson criteria for a compact group, and most of its galaxies display clear signatures of tidal interaction. In contrast, the early-type galaxies in the group core show no obvious fine structure or evidence for recent mergers, with the exception of a strong dust lane in the elliptical MCG 2-33-38. Emission-line diagnostics in this galaxy reveal strong [O III], [N II], and [S II] lines together with comparatively weak but broad Hα, consistent with an intermediate Seyfert classification and indicating ongoing nuclear activity. The faint-galaxy photometry reveals an excess consistent with an associated intragroup population, though the field is heavily contaminated by the background cluster Abell 1631. Despite this contamination, the X-ray analysis suggests the presence of diffuse, extended emission attributable to a hot intragroup medium linked to the NGC 4756 system. These results portray a group in a mixed dynamical state: a loose, early-type-rich core with limited evidence for recent transformative interactions, coexisting with a compact, interaction-driven substructure. The detection of hot gas supports a gravitationally bound system in an advanced evolutionary phase, while the compact subgroup highlights ongoing dynamical processing. We discuss the implications for the assembly history of SSSGs and the role of substructure and environment in driving morphological transformation and nuclear activity in low-density group environments.

We investigate electromagnetic effects arising from the neutron’s spatial charge and magnetization distributions, encoded in the form factors @xmath1 and @xmath2 in momentum space, despite its vanishing total charge. From these distributions we construct an electromagnetic potential for the @xmath0 and evaluate its contribution to nuclear binding. Using realistic deuteron and halo wave functions, we compute first-order corrections to the binding energy @xmath3 for the deuteron and the one-neutron halo nucleus @xmath4be by folding the neutron–proton and neutron–charged-core (@xmath5be) potentials. For the deuteron, the correction amounts to @xmath6 keV and is comparable to the effect of the @xmath7-isobar admixture. For @xmath4be, whose valence neutron is weakly bound, the correction is approximately @xmath8 keV. Implications for precision structure calculations and constraints on nucleon form factors are discussed.

Detection of primordial B-mode polarization probes the tensor-to-scalar ratio r, imposing strong constraints on inflation. We present a single-field inflation framework whose potential is an infinite power series (IPS). The IPS model yields slow-roll trajectories that fit current Planck and BICEP2 measurements of the scalar spectral index, scalar amplitude, and the tensor fraction. A distinctive prediction is a positive correlation between r and the absolute magnitude of the running of the spectral index, enabling simultaneous realization of a large r and sizable running without spoiling slow roll. The model naturally produces sufficient e-folds, at least 60, addressing horizon and flatness problems. We delineate parameter ranges consistent with data and highlight testable signatures; forthcoming B-mode and large-scale structure observations can critically evaluate IPS inflation.

We investigate the discovery prospects for a new massless, neutral gauge boson—the paraphoton—at an electron–positron collider operating at center-of-mass energies of 0.5 and 1 TeV. Paraphotons arise naturally through Abelian kinetic mixing, and a realistic, model-independent lowest-order effective Lagrangian induces magnetic-type interactions with Standard Model fermions. These couplings are proportional to the fermion mass and increase with energy, while remaining very weak for ordinary matter. At the International Linear Collider, the most promising channel is paraphoton radiation off top quarks, yielding a characteristic signature of two acoplanar top-quark jets accompanied by substantial missing energy. We develop a multivariate event selection strategy that exploits jet acoplanarity, missing momentum, reconstructed top kinematics, and b-tagging to efficiently separate signal from dominant Standard Model backgrounds. Using these discriminants, we derive projected limits on the top–paraphoton coupling across the studied energies, highlighting the improvement with increasing center-of-mass energy. We also discuss kinematic observables sensitive to the spin of the invisible particle, providing arguments that support a spin-1 interpretation consistent with a paraphoton.

Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are widely hypothesized to arise from complex organic molecules, with their strengths in local galaxies correlating with neutral hydrogen column density and dust reddening. Because Ca II absorbers in quasar (QSO) spectra are posited to have high N(H I) and significant E(B−V), they represent promising sites for the detection of DIBs at cosmological distances. We present the first systematic search for DIBs in nine Ca II–selected absorbers at @xmath0. We detect the 5780 Å DIB in one line of sight at @xmath1, marking only the second QSO absorber in which a DIB has been identified. Notably, both QSO absorbers with detected DIBs exhibit weak 6284 Å absorption relative to the 5780 Å band, in contrast to the majority of local DIB sightlines where 6284 is typically stronger. This difference may indicate distinct physical conditions—such as radiation field hardness, ionization balance, metallicity, or dust shielding—in intermediate-redshift QSO absorbers compared with local galaxies. Assuming that local empirical relations between 5780 Å DIB strength and N(H I) and E(B−V) apply at these redshifts, DIB detections and limits can be used to infer gas and dust properties. For the absorber with a detected 5780 Å DIB, we derive E(B−V) = 0.23 mag and @xmath2 @xmath3 20.9, consistent with previous evidence that Ca II systems have high H I column densities and significant reddening. For the remaining eight Ca II–selected absorbers with 5780 Å non-detections, we infer upper limits of E(B−V) ≈ 0.1–0.3 mag. These results highlight Ca II absorbers as promising laboratories for probing DIB carriers and the interstellar medium at cosmological distances. Keywords: quasars: absorption lines; dust, extinction; ISM: abundances; ISM: lines and bands; ISM: molecules; line: identification

Using DFT within LDA, we simulate the electronic band structure and optical response of Ga-substituted graphene over 0–3.91 at% doping. Ga atoms are randomly placed in a 128-atom sheet, with properties averaged over five configurations. We quantify changes in electron density, refractive index, optical conductivity, and extinction coefficient versus dopant concentration. At low Ga loadings, direct substitution induces hole doping and local disorder that disrupts Dirac states; impurity scattering perturbs electron density while semimetallic behavior persists. With increasing Ga content, the system remains metallic or semimetallic and shows enhanced carrier mobility linked to Ga-derived bands that shift graphene bands and gradually dissolve the Dirac cone. Frequency-resolved optical conductivity reveals doping-dependent redistribution of spectral weight and systematic trends in refractive index and extinction coefficient consistent with greater free-carrier contributions. For context, we compare these results to a purely theoretical 100% Ga sheet, providing a conductivity benchmark and clarifying the role of carbon in sustaining transport. These calculations delineate how dilute-to-moderate Ga substitution tunes graphene’s optoelectronic properties through controlled hole doping and impurity scattering.

We analyze the asymptotic behavior of fermion scattering amplitudes in the Sudakov limit, incorporating next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic electroweak corrections. The framework is applied to high-energy fermion–antifermion production in e+e− annihilation, highlighting the impact of subleading logarithms on predictions and resummation. We present the two-loop fermionic contributions to the Abelian form factor and discuss their interplay with electroweak Sudakov effects. Numerical estimates demonstrate sizable corrections at multi-TeV scales, with implications for collider phenomenology and precision tests.

We analyze fluctuation dynamics for electrons near a positive ion and for charges confined in traps, focusing on stationary nonuniform equilibrium densities and their contrasts. Small perturbations about these states are treated via linear response from a Markov kinetic framework whose dynamical generator is exact at short times. The kinetic equation is solved using an effective mean-field single-particle description, with local density determining forces and dynamical screening embodied by a dielectric function tailored to nonuniform environments. We present expressions for the response and explore consequences for transport and relaxation. Finally, we evaluate the autocorrelation function of the total force, elucidating memory and screening effects.

We study dynamics of two-dimensional coherent structures in planetary atmospheres and oceans. Starting from the barotropic quasigeostrophic equation, we derive the Zakharov–Kuznetsov equation governing large-scale, weakly nonlinear, long-wave motions over a narrow jet-like mean flow. Using multiple-scale analysis with asymptotic matching, we capture the emergence and evolution of coherent structures from the instability of the jet. The amplitude equation admits solitary wave solutions and provides a framework for anisotropic dispersion and nonlinearity. Implications for jet-modulated mesoscale variability are discussed.

in this study, we present a comprehensive analysis of deep near-infrared (nir) imaging observations of the globular cluster m4, obtained using the hubble space telescope's wide field camera 3 (hst/wfc3). our high-precision nir photometry has produced an exceptionally detailed colour-magnitude diagram (cmd) that clearly traces the main sequence down to and beyond the theoretical hydrogen-burning limit, while also revealing the white dwarf sequence. this represents the deepest nir cmd ever constructed for a globular cluster. to enhance the reliability of our stellar classification, we incorporated archival hst optical data for proper-motion cleaning of the cmd and to distinguish between white dwarfs (wds) and brown dwarf (bd) candidates. our observations achieve remarkable detection limits of @xmath0 mag and @xmath1 mag in the nir bands, and @xmath2 mag in the optical. by comparing our observed cmds with state-of-the-art theoretical stellar models, we confirm that our nir photometry extends beyond the hydrogen-burning limit, while our optical-nir cmds reach approximately to this critical boundary. this depth differential creates a unique opportunity: nir sources fainter than the h-burning limit without optical counterparts become potential bd candidates, as the optical observations lack sufficient depth to detect these extremely faint objects. we conducted a systematic visual inspection of nir sources fainter than the h-burning limit in @xmath3 that lacked measured optical counterparts. this investigation identified five sources without optical photometry. for four of these, we detected faint optical emission and estimated upper magnitude limits. based on these constraints and comparison with theoretical models, we classify one source as likely a white dwarf, one as ambiguous (either wd or bd), and two as consistent with brown dwarfs. the fifth source, showing no detectable optical counterpart, represents our strongest bd candidate. in total, we identify four compelling brown dwarf candidates in m4, demonstrating the power of combining ultra-deep nir imaging with complementary optical data for studying the substellar population in globular clusters.

This work investigates a lattice model of critical spanning webs on a finite cylinder, extending the classical spanning tree framework. The presence of cycles introduces non-trivial topological features, placing the model within logarithmic conformal field theories with central charge $ c = 0 $. By analyzing the scaling limit of the universal partition function, we demonstrate that closed boundary conditions at both cylinder edges yield the character of symplectic fermions with periodic boundary conditions. Conversely, mixed boundary conditions (open at one edge, closed at the other) reproduce the antiperiodic character. These results establish a direct correspondence between the model’s Virasoro module structure and dense polymer systems. The study bridges free fermion methods and logarithmic CFT, offering insights into the interplay of boundary conditions and modular properties in critical two-dimensional systems. Keywords: free fermion model, logarithmic conformal field theory, spanning graphs, dense polymers, Virasoro module.

This paper investigates the structural implications of causal diamond-shaped subsets of space-time in quantum field theory (QFT), particularly their interplay with operator algebras and the Bousso covariant entropy bound. We propose that when space-time is described as a manifold with a minimal length scale, the net of causal sets to which local operator algebras are assigned should exhibit non-orthomodular lattice structures. Such a geometry arises naturally under conditions that reduce the degrees of freedom in a manner akin to holography, aligning with constraints on local algebraic properties. A concrete example of a non-orthomodular net is constructed, implementing a covariant ultraviolet cutoff. This framework clarifies the non-positive expansion condition for light-sheet selection in the Bousso entropy bound, offering a novel perspective on entropy bound formulations. By integrating algebraic QFT methods with geometric constraints, our approach bridges foundational aspects of quantum gravity and holography, suggesting a covariant refinement of entropy bounds while addressing the algebraic underpinnings of spacetime discreteness.

The Victoria-Regina isochrones for [α/Fe] = 0.0, 0.4, and a wide range in [Fe/H], alongside zero-age horizontal branch (ZAHB) models, are applied to the color-magnitude diagram (CMD) of the Carina dwarf spheroidal galaxy (dSph). Color transformations derived from globular clusters (M3 and M92) are calibrated to ensure robust fits to their CMDs under well-constrained reddening and metallicity assumptions. The adopted distance moduli for Carina and the globular clusters (GCs) are anchored to ZAHB models, which reproduce Carina’s old horizontal branch (HB) and the luminosity of its HB clump despite the galaxy’s broad metallicity spread ([Fe/H] spanning ~1.2 dex). This success hinges on [α/Fe] variation with [Fe/H], as spectroscopically observed. Ages inferred from the CMD agree with prior estimates for old (≥10 Gyr) and intermediate-age turnoff stars, as well as the 9–11 Gyr epoch of negligible star formation (SF). CMD simulations of the faintest turnoff and subgiant stars reveal a preference for prolonged SF lasting several Gyr, rather than a single burst, with a tentative trend of decreasing ages at higher [Fe/H]. Stellar models assuming spectroscopic metallicities yield satisfactory fits to Carina’s CMD features, including its thin giant branch.
