Our results reveal that linear degradation mechanisms yield formation times that scale linearly with distance from the source, whereas nonlinear degradation mechanisms exhibit quadratic scaling. These findings are attributed to the strength of the effective potential generated by degradation, with linear degradation producing a stronger potential and nonlinear degradation resulting in a weaker potential. This research provides new insights into the physical-chemical principles governing morphogen gradient formation, shedding light on the intricate processes that shape tissue and organ development in multicellular organisms. By elucidating the role of degradation in morphogen gradient formation, this study contributes to a deeper understanding of the fundamental biological processes that underlie development and patterning in complex biological systems.

We present an ongoing survey utilizing the Nanay Radio Telescope at L-band, targeting areas @xmath0 and @xmath1. This survey boasts an 18-minute integration time, 512 MHz bandwidth, and high resolutions of 64 @xmath2s and 0.5 MHz. The nominal sensitivity limit of 0.055 mJy surpasses the mid-latitude HTRU survey by a factor of two. Designed to complement large-scale surveys, this project enhances detection of transients, distant millisecond pulsars, and scintillating sources. Its prolonged integration time renders it more sensitive to faint radio sources than preceding short-integration surveys, offering new insights into the radio sky.

This article presents a unified framework for stochastic optimization algorithms, known as Information-Geometric Optimization (IGO). IGO transforms the original optimization problem into a maximization problem on the parameter space of a given family of probability distributions. The algorithm updates the parameter of the distribution along the natural gradient, with respect to the Fisher metric, to maximize an adaptive transform of the objective function. Notably, IGO encompasses several established algorithms, including PBIL, CMA-ES, and the cross-entropy method, as special instances. Theoretical justification for the IGO framework is provided, demonstrating that any step size not exceeding a certain threshold guarantees monotone improvement in the optimization process, in terms of quantile values of the objective function. Furthermore, the article extends this result to accommodate different step sizes for parameter blocks and shows that expected fitness improves over time when fitness-proportional selection is applied, yielding the RPP algorithm. This work offers a comprehensive foundation for the IGO framework, highlighting its versatility and theoretical soundness in addressing optimization problems. By unifying various stochastic algorithms under a single framework, IGO provides a powerful tool for tackling complex optimization challenges.

This article provides definitions and formulas for consistent computation of helicity amplitudes in theoretical approaches, clarifying sign determinations for transverse and longitudinal amplitudes. This work resolves existing confusions and enables direct comparison with experimentally extracted amplitudes, promoting accuracy and consistency in theoretical and experimental analyses.

We investigate the ultraspinning instability of rapidly rotating Myers-Perry black holes in higher-dimensional spacetimes, a phenomenon conjectured by Emparan and Myers. Our previous work numerically identified the onset of this axisymmetric instability in singly-spinning Myers-Perry black holes in five dimensions, marking a bifurcation point to new branches of axisymmetric solutions with pinched horizons, potentially connecting to black rings, black saturns, and other families in the phase diagram of stationary solutions. Here, we extend this analysis to demonstrate the presence of this instability in six and seven dimensions. A detailed examination of the perturbation boundary conditions reveals that they preserve the angular velocity and temperature of the original black hole, a crucial property for establishing a thermodynamic necessary condition for the existence of this instability in general rotating backgrounds. Furthermore, we prove that ultraspinning modes cannot be pure gauge modes, confirming a previous claim. Our study also uncovers new ultraspinning Gregory-Laflamme instabilities of rotating black strings and branes, which emerge precisely at the critical rotation predicted by a refined version of the Gubser-Mitra conjecture. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the complex landscape of higher-dimensional black hole solutions and their stability properties, with implications for the phase diagram of stationary solutions and the behavior of rotating black objects in diverse gravitational settings.

We demonstrate that small Okubo-Zweig-Iizuka rule violations in quark-flavor basis for @xmath0-@xmath1 mixing can significantly enhance the chiral scale associated with the @xmath2 meson. This enhancement reconciles discrepancies in @xmath3 and @xmath4 branching ratios. Alternative proposals, including flavor-singlet contributions and axial @xmath5 anomaly, are discussed. Discrimination between these proposals using @xmath6 and @xmath7 data is proposed, offering a resolution to the longstanding problem.

This article presents the motivation, design, and implementation of the Cornish Survey, a high-resolution radio continuum survey of the inner Galactic plane at 5 GHz using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA). Conducted in coordination with the northern Spitzer GLIMPSE I region, this blind survey covers a 10° × 6.5° area at arcsecond resolution, providing an unbiased dataset for studying ultra-compact H II regions, a crucial phase in massive star formation. To mitigate beam elongation effects at low declinations, a two-snapshot strategy was employed, resulting in a synthesised beam with an elongation of less than 1.5 over 75% of the survey area and less than 2 over 98%. With a sensitivity of approximately 2 mJy, the survey enables the distinction between radio-loud and quiet mid-infrared sources. The Cornish Survey has far-reaching legacy applications beyond star formation, including the study of evolved stars, active stars and binaries, and extragalactic sources. By complementing existing surveys of diffuse and non-thermal sources, as well as atomic and molecular phases, this project contributes to a comprehensive understanding of the interstellar medium in the Galaxy. The survey's findings will provide valuable insights into the formation and evolution of massive stars and the structure of the Galactic plane.

This article presents a novel beam profile measurement technique for the Antiproton Decelerator at CERN, utilizing a single Gas Electron Multiplier with a 2D readout structure. Weighing virtually nothing, this detector directly measures horizontal and vertical profiles in one plane, overcoming issues with multi-wire proportional chambers. A prototype was successfully tested in 2010, and five additional detectors have been installed in the ASACUSA and AEGIS beam lines. This paper provides a detailed description of the detector and discusses the obtained results, highlighting the advantages of this innovative approach to beam profile measurement.

This study investigates the phenomenon of traffic-driven epidemic spreading on correlated networks, a previously unaddressed problem. Contrary to expectations, our findings reveal that the epidemic threshold exhibits non-monotonic behavior, reaching a minimum at a critical value of the assortativity coefficient. To elucidate this phenomenon, we employ degree-based mean-field theory to calculate the traffic-driven epidemic threshold for correlated networks. Our theoretical framework predicts an inverse relationship between the threshold and both the packet-generation rate and the largest eigenvalue of the betweenness matrix. Numerical simulations confirm our theoretical predictions, demonstrating consistency between the two. These results offer valuable insights into the dynamics of real-world epidemic spreading driven by traffic flows, with potential implications for controlling and mitigating the spread of diseases in complex networks. Our work contributes to a deeper understanding of the interplay between traffic dynamics and epidemic spreading.

This article reexamines the @xmath0-metric, a spacetime describing two causally separated black holes accelerating in opposite directions due to conical singularities. By utilizing newly developed coordinate systems with simple metric functions, we transparently demonstrate the metric's properties. These coordinates enable the construction of Kruskal-Szekeres-type extensions and 2D conformal Penrose diagrams, which are then combined into a 3D illustration of the spacetime's global causal structure outside the horizons. We interpret the metric's parameters physically using the weak field limit and invariant quantities. Additionally, connections to other familiar coordinate systems are discussed, providing a comprehensive understanding of the @xmath0-metric and its applications in describing black hole spacetimes. Our approach offers a clearer insight into the metric's properties and its role in theoretical physics, enhancing the existing knowledge of black hole dynamics.

This study demonstrates the coherent control of plasma dynamics in a laser wakefield electron acceleration experiment. By utilizing a genetic algorithm and a deformable mirror, we optimize the wavefront of an intense laser field to achieve a final coherent state. The algorithm iteratively adjusts the laser phase front based on feedback from the electron beam signal, enabling a heuristic search for the optimal conditions. Our results show a significant improvement in both the electron beam charge and angular distribution, with enhancements of up to an order of magnitude. Notably, these improvements do not solely correlate with the quality of the focal spot, but rather with the specific laser phase front that effectively steers the plasma wave to a final state with optimal accelerating fields. This work highlights the potential of coherent control techniques in plasma-based acceleration experiments, paving the way for further advancements in this field. The findings have implications for the development of high-quality electron beams and the optimization of laser-plasma interactions.

This study addresses the fundamental problem of estimating commuting flows at various spatial scales, a crucial aspect of research in multiple fields. Current methods often rely on calibrated parameters from empirical trip data, which can be limiting when such data is unavailable. To overcome this challenge, we develop a statistical expression to estimate commuting trips using a quantitative functional form, eliminating the need for empirical calibration data. By introducing a scaling parameter to the parameter-free radiation model, we calculate commuting trip volumes at scales ranging from intra-city to national levels, utilizing only population and facility density distributions. Our model's parameter is interpretable as the influence of regional scale and facility distribution heterogeneity. We investigate the scaling limitations of this problem, determining the conditions under which our model can be applied without calibration data. Our results show that the proposed model's estimation accuracy is comparable to existing models when empirical trip data is available. The model is validated in various U.S. regions and successfully applied in three different countries, demonstrating its versatility and potential for widespread application. By providing a reliable and data-efficient method for estimating commuting flows, this study contributes to the advancement of research in transportation planning, urban development, and related fields.

This study examines the ground-state properties of strongly correlated electrons interacting with phonons using a generalized Gutzwiller wavefunction. The paramagnetic half-filled Hubbard-Holstein model is investigated, where electron-electron interactions can induce a Mott transition and electron-phonon coupling can lead to a bipolaronic transition. The proposed wavefunction's quality is assessed in describing various transitions and crossovers as a function of parameters. By retaining full variational freedom, previously inaccessible regions of the phase diagram are explored, while previous variational attempts are recovered as special cases. This approach provides a comprehensive understanding of the interplay between electronic and phononic degrees of freedom.

The observed abundance of weak gravitational lenses offers a promising avenue for constraining the equation-of-state parameter of dark energy. Dark energy's influence on the distance-redshift relation, the amplitude of the matter power spectrum, and the rate of structure growth affects the efficiency of dark-matter concentrations in producing detectable weak-lensing signals. To explore this, we solve the spherical-collapse model with dark energy, clarifying existing ambiguities and providing fitting formulas for the non-linear overdensity at virialization and the linear-theory overdensity at collapse. Our calculations reveal a high degree of degeneracy between the equation-of-state parameter and the present matter density in the predicted redshift distribution and number count of weak lenses. However, by fixing the present matter density, we find that the number count of weak lenses for a given dark energy model is significantly lower than for the standard cold dark matter (SCDM) model. To mitigate the impact of degeneracy and observational uncertainties, we propose an alternative approach: comparing the relative abundance of virialized X-ray lensing clusters with the abundance of non-virialized, X-ray underluminous, lensing halos. This method is largely insensitive to the degeneracy between the equation-of-state parameter and the present matter density, as well as uncertainties in observational noise. Our results show that, for aperture sizes of 10 arcmin, the predicted ratio of non-virialized to virialized lenses is greater than 40% and varies by 20% between different dark energy models. We conclude that, if all other weak lensing parameters are fixed, a survey must cover at least 100 square degrees to differentiate a SCDM cosmology from a dark energy model with a given equation-of-state parameter at the 3σ level. However, when accounting for uncertainties in lensing parameters, the non-virialized lens fraction provides a more robust constraint on the equation-of-state parameter, requiring 200 square degrees of sky coverage to differentiate a SCDM model from a dark energy model to 3σ. Our findings highlight the potential of weak gravitational lensing as a powerful tool for constraining dark energy models and demonstrate the importance of considering alternative approaches to mitigate the impact of degeneracy and observational uncertainties.

This article presents high-resolution observations of the massive star-forming region W75 N, obtained using 3 mm continuum and line emission, as well as near-infrared K-band and [FeII] images. The CO emission reveals a complex morphology of multiple, overlapping outflows driven by at least four late to early B-type protostars. The total flow mass of approximately 500 solar masses extends 3 parsecs from end to end, with over 10% of the molecular cloud accelerated to high velocities. The mechanical energy in the outflowing gas is roughly half the gravitational binding energy of the cloud, indicating a significant impact on the surrounding environment. The W75 N cluster members exhibit a range of evolutionary stages, from stars with no apparent circumstellar material to deeply embedded protostars powering massive outflows. Millimeter-wavelength emission highlights the locations of nine embedded protostars, with associated gas and dust masses ranging from 340 to 11 solar masses. The infrared reflection nebula and shocked emission display multiple peaks and extensions, suggesting the presence of several outflows. Notably, the [FeII] emission is only detected close to the protostars, while diffuse emission extends 0.6 parsecs beyond the CO emission boundaries. The infrared line emission morphology indicates the presence of slow, non-dissociative J-type shocks throughout the parsec-scale outflows, with fast, dissociative shocks absent in W75 N. This contrasts with low-mass outflows, where jet-driven fast shocks are common. Our findings suggest that the energetics of outflows from late to early B-type protostars in W75 N differ from their low-mass counterparts, and are not simply scaled-up versions of low-mass outflows. This study provides new insights into the complex processes governing massive star formation and the impact of outflows on the surrounding molecular cloud.

We derive the AGL equation from the dipole picture, confirming its validity in the double logarithmic approximation limit. This unitarized gluon distribution equation, originally obtained via the Glauber-Mueller approach, accurately describes small-x regime phenomena, making it a strong candidate for unitarized evolution equations in this domain, with implications for high-energy particle physics and QCD research.

This study investigates the quasiparticle spectra of Co-based Heusler compounds, Co2MnSi and Co2FeSi, using the one-shot GW approximation in an all-electron framework. The calculations reveal that many-body corrections are crucial for Co2FeSi, resulting in a pseudogap and good agreement with experimental magnetic moments. Moderate changes are observed compared to the density-functional theory starting point. The calculated photoemission and X-ray absorption spectra are in good agreement with experimental results. Comparison with the GW density of states suggests that the Kohn-Sham eigenvalue spectrum provides a reasonable approximation for the quasiparticle spectrum of these Heusler compounds, offering valuable insights into their electronic properties.

We present high-resolution VLBI imaging of SGR A* at 7mm and 3.5mm, revealing wavelength-dependent intrinsic sizes. The 3.5mm emitting region is approximately 1AU in size. Combining these measurements with the lower mass limit of SGR A* provides strong evidence for a supermassive black hole. Notably, a structural variation is detected, resulting in an intrinsically symmetrical structure that increases in size by over 25% at 7mm. These findings offer insights into the compact emission region and the nature of SGR A*, supporting its classification as a supermassive black hole at the Galactic Center.

We present the results of an ASCA (Advanced Satellite for Cosmology and Astrophysics) investigation of four prototype powerful far-infrared galaxies: Mrk 231, Mrk 273, Arp 220, and NGC 6240. The soft X-ray spectra of these galaxies exhibit thermal emission with temperatures of approximately 0.5-1 keV, likely produced by starburst activity. The soft X-ray (0.5-2 keV) luminosities range from 10^41 to 10^42 erg/s. Our analysis reveals evidence of heavily obscured active galactic nuclei (AGN) in Mrk 273 and NGC 6240, characterized by strong iron K emission line features. In NGC 6240, the hard X-ray emission (>3 keV) is likely the result of reflected light from a hidden quasar, with an intrinsic luminosity comparable to its far-infrared luminosity. While Mrk 231 exhibits 2-10 keV emission, the origin of this hard X-ray emission remains uncertain due to data quality limitations. In contrast, Arp 220 shows no evidence of an AGN in its X-ray data, despite a significant far-infrared excess. However, the soft X-ray emission from this galaxy is surprisingly weak, suggesting the possible presence of a heavily obscured, Compton-thick AGN. Our findings provide new insights into the complex interplay between starburst activity and AGN in these powerful far-infrared galaxies.

This study presents a detailed analysis of the young stellar cluster NGC 602, situated in the peripheral Wing region of the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). Utilizing deep optical imaging from the Hubble Space Telescope's Advanced Camera for Surveys, we have identified an extensive pre-main sequence (PMS) population with stellar masses ranging from 0.63-3.5 M. These low-mass PMS stars are found to have formed coevally with the central cluster approximately 4 million years ago. Furthermore, Spitzer Space Telescope images reveal a population of young stellar objects, some of which are still embedded in nebular material, indicating a more recent formation. Our findings suggest that star formation in this region initiated around 14 million years ago with the formation of the central cluster and has since propagated towards the outskirts, where star formation is currently ongoing. This research provides valuable insights into the star formation history and evolution of the SMC's Wing region, shedding light on the complex processes that shape the galaxy's peripheral areas.

This article introduces the Exponential Linear Unit (ELU), a novel activation function designed to accelerate learning in deep neural networks while achieving higher classification accuracies. ELUs build upon the strengths of existing activation functions, such as Rectified Linear Units (ReLUs), Leaky ReLUs (LReLUs), and Parametrized ReLUs (PReLUs), by alleviating the vanishing gradient problem. However, ELUs exhibit improved learning characteristics compared to these units, attributed to their ability to push mean unit activations closer to zero, similar to batch normalization, but with reduced computational complexity. This property enables faster learning by minimizing the bias shift effect and bringing the normal gradient closer to the unit natural gradient. Furthermore, ELUs demonstrate a noise-robust deactivation state, allowing them to effectively code the degree of presence of specific phenomena in the input. Experimental results show that ELUs outperform ReLUs and LReLUs on deep networks, achieving significantly better generalization performance and faster learning. Notably, ELU networks achieve state-of-the-art results on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and demonstrate accelerated learning on ImageNet, obtaining a single-crop, single-model classification error of less than 10%. Overall, the ELU activation function offers a promising approach for improving the performance and efficiency of deep neural networks.

This study investigates the non-linear stress-strain relation in crosslinked polymer networks using molecular dynamics simulations. Building on previous work highlighting the role of trapped entanglements, we present new results for stress versus strain in both dry and swollen networks. Our findings show that models limiting network strand fluctuations, such as the tube model, accurately describe stress behavior under elongation and compression. For swollen networks, the total modulus decreases with increasing strain, approaching the phantom model result only for short strand networks, providing new insights into the mechanical properties of crosslinked polymers.

This study presents self-consistent models of X-ray irradiated accretion discs in close binary systems, examining the impact of a point X-ray source on disc structure. Our results indicate that a source located in the disc plane cannot significantly alter the disc due to self-screening by the disc's outer regions. Observations of low-mass X-ray binaries suggest that the outer disc emission is dominated by reprocessed X-ray flux, implying that accretion discs in these systems must be either warped or irradiated by a source above the disc plane. We investigate the thermal-viscous stability of irradiated accretion discs, deriving stability criteria and challenging common assumptions. Notably, the critical accretion rate below which a disc is unstable is found to be uncertain due to the lack of a well-defined formula describing irradiation effects. Our findings have significant implications for understanding accretion disc dynamics and stability in close binary systems.

This study examines the influence of superconducting fluctuations on the mesoscopic persistent current in an ensemble of rings, comprising a superconducting layer in contact with a normal one, within the Cooper limit. The superconducting transition temperature is found to decay rapidly with increasing relative width of the normal layer. However, when the Thouless energy exceeds the temperature, the persistent current suppression is significantly slower. This phenomenon, akin to the effect of magnetic impurities, arises from the proximity-induced pair-weakening, contrasting with pair-breaking. Our findings provide insight into the interplay between superconducting fluctuations and the proximity effect in bilayer systems.

This article presents a two-part study on solving a large class of Lindblad master equations for non-interacting particles on multiple sites. Focusing on bosonic particles in Part I, we demonstrate a reduction method involving the diagonalization of a non-Hermitian matrix. Specifically, for boundary dissipative driving in a uniform chain, the matrix simplifies to a tridiagonal bordered Toeplitz matrix, allowing for analytical solutions of master modes and relaxation rates. When analytical solutions are unattainable, our approach still accelerates numerical evaluation. We apply this method to investigate the relaxation gap at non-equilibrium phase transitions in a boundary-driven bosonic ladder with synthetic gauge fields, and construct the non-equilibrium steady state, providing new insights into the behavior of bosonic systems under dissipative driving. Our results have implications for understanding quantum many-body systems out of equilibrium.

This paper presents a low-density parity-check (LDPC) code with a parity-based approach for distributed joint source-channel coding (DJSCC) with decoder side information. The proposed method achieves the theoretical limit and utilizes different edge degree distributions for source and parity variable nodes. Codeword-averaged density evolution (CADE) is applied to asymmetrically correlated nonuniform sources over asymmetric memoryless transmission channels. Simulation results demonstrate that splitting variable nodes improves coding efficiency and lowers the error floor, making it suitable for DJSCC applications with nonuniform sources and asymmetric channels, thus enhancing the overall performance of suboptimal codes.

This study analytically solves the zeroth-order complex dispersion relations of a cylindrical metallic nanowire using approximate methods. The solutions accurately describe sections near the surface plasmon frequency and the back bending of surface plasmon-polaritons, attributing it to metal ohmic loss. The findings validate the utility of the back bending point in measuring metallic ohmic loss, providing a novel approach for characterizing nanowire properties and understanding the role of ohmic loss in plasmonic phenomena.

This study examines the distribution of eigenvalues of the stock market correlation matrix as the time series length increases, utilizing 100 highly-capitalized American stocks. The results are compared to the Wishart random matrix ensemble, revealing a systematic excess of eigenvalues beyond the predicted borders. This suggests that the bulk of the spectrum retains correlations masked by measurement noise in shorter time series. Further analysis of the "noisy" eigensignals' return distributions, temporal correlations, and multifractal spectra supports this conclusion. The findings imply that even the bulk of the stock market correlation matrix spectrum carries meaningful correlations, contributing to a deeper understanding of portfolio theories and the interplay between noise and collective behavior in financial markets. The research has implications for the application of random matrix theory in finance, highlighting the importance of considering time series length and noise effects.

This study investigates a microtwinned single crystal of LAMNO3 using implanted muons. Two muon stopping sites are identified in the ordered phase, yielding insights into the staggered magnetization's temperature dependence. A static critical exponent is extracted and discussed. The muon spin relaxation rate exhibits critical slowing down, characterized by a critical exponent, indicating Ising-like dynamic fluctuations. Additionally, muon precession frequencies reveal the saturation of the weak ferromagnetic domain structure, attributed to the Dzialoshinski-Moriya antisymmetric exchange. These findings provide a comprehensive understanding of the material's magnetic properties and behavior near criticality.

This article explores the implications of a screened charge by a Yukawa potential on the electric field and spacetime metric. We consider a modified Yukawa-Reissner-Nordström spacetime, which asymptotically decays to a Schwarzschild spacetime. The screening effect reduces the number of singularities from two to one at a suitable distance. By analyzing the tetrad fields associated with this spacetime, we demonstrate that linear motion in proper time yields estimates for the Yukawa screening parameter related to the Schwarzschild radius, providing insights into the interplay between gravity and electromagnetism in curved spacetime. Novel implications emerge.

This article examines heterotic orbifold compactifications, which reproduce properties of the supersymmetric standard model and address high-energy physics problems, such as neutrino masses and the strong CP problem. However, these scenarios rely on stable vacuum assumptions, characterized by moduli fields. We relax this assumption, investigating moduli stabilization in realistic orbifold models. By analyzing their qualities and 4D effective action, we find nonperturbative effects lift bulk moduli directions, resulting in typically de Sitter vacua with quasi-flat directions. Although unstable, these vacua offer potential solutions to cosmological challenges, including inflation, and provide new insights into the phenomenology of heterotic orbifold compactifications, shedding light on the intricacies of high-energy physics and the search for a more complete theoretical framework.

This article employs Lie symmetry analysis to examine two significant evolution equations in financial mathematics: the two-dimensional Black-Scholes equation and the equation for the two-factor commodities problem. We investigate these equations under autonomous and non-autonomous conditions, where parameters may be unspecified functions of time. Our results show that the autonomous Black-Scholes equation exhibits maximal symmetry, enabling its reduction to the classical heat equation. In contrast, the non-autonomous Black-Scholes equation and both autonomous and non-autonomous two-factor equations display submaximal symmetry. By utilizing solution symmetries to reduce each equation to an ordinary differential equation, we find that the resulting equation possesses maximal symmetry, rendering it equivalent to the classical heat equation. This study contributes to the understanding of symmetry properties in financial mathematics, particularly in the context of option pricing and commodity models. The application of Lie point symmetries provides valuable insights into the inherent structure of these equations, facilitating their solution and analysis.

This article presents a comprehensive analysis of RXTE-PCA observations of SMC X-1, a high-mass X-ray binary pulsar, between January 1996 and December 2003. A precise timing solution is obtained from observations around August 30, 1996, yielding an eccentricity of 0.00089(6) and an orbital decay rate of -3.36(4) x 10^-6 yr^-1, consistent with previous results. The constructed 8-year pulse period history reveals long- and short-term fluctuations in the frequency derivative. Spectral analysis shows that most parameters remain stable over time, except for hydrogen column density, which increases with decreasing X-ray flux. This correlation may be attributed to enhanced soft absorption when the pulsar is partially obscured or could be an artifact of the soft excess in the energy spectrum. These findings contribute to our understanding of the accretion processes and neutron star properties in SMC X-1, providing valuable insights into the behavior of high-mass X-ray binary pulsars. The results have implications for the study of X-ray binaries, pulsars, and accretion discs, and highlight the importance of long-term monitoring of these systems.

This paper presents a comprehensive data survey of well-defined streamer wave events observed by the Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph (LASCO) on board the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO) throughout Solar Cycle 23. A total of 8 candidate events were identified and analyzed, revealing common characteristics such as high-speed and wide angular span driving Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) and interactions with the streamer structure at low altitudes. Notably, all front-side CMEs were accompanied by flares, shedding light on the excitation conditions of streamer wave events. A detailed analysis of a specific event on June 5, 2003, was conducted, yielding the heliocentric distances of wave troughs and crests, which were used to deduce wave properties such as period, wavelength, and phase speeds. The results show that the period and wavelength increase with wave propagation, while the phase speed of the preceding wave is faster than that of the trailing ones. A coronal seismological study was also performed, providing radial profiles of the Alfvén speed and magnetic field strength in the region surrounding the streamer plasma sheet. Both quantities exhibit a declining trend with time, indicative of the recovering process of the CME-disturbed corona. Furthermore, the Alfvénic critical point was found to be located at approximately 10 R⊙, where the flow speed equals the Alfvén speed, approximately 1200 km/s. These findings contribute to our understanding of the dynamics and properties of streamer wave events and the associated coronal processes.

This study presents integral field spectroscopy of 16 stars in the Braid Nebula star formation region within Cygnus OB7. Combining spectroscopic data with 2MASS near-IR photometry, we identify many objects as members of the region's pre-main sequence population. Our findings contribute to a large-scale, multi-wavelength survey aiming to characterize the young stars and star-forming activity in the Lynds 1003 molecular cloud. The results provide insights into the number, mass distribution, and evolutionary state of the young stars within this previously understudied region, shedding light on the star formation processes at play.

Title: A Detailed Study of the 5 Hz Quasi-Periodic Oscillation in the Black-Hole Candidate GRS 1739-278 Abstract: We present an in-depth analysis of the 5 Hz quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) recently discovered in the bright X-ray transient and black-hole candidate GRS 1739-278. Utilizing data from the Rossi X-Ray Timing Explorer, our study reveals a complex QPO phenomenon with distinct energy-dependent characteristics. The 5 Hz QPO, detected during the second 3.2 ksec data set, exhibits an increase in strength from 2% to 5% rms amplitude as photon energies rise from below 4 keV to above 10 keV. Notably, soft QPO photons (below 5 keV) lag hard photons (above 10 keV) by approximately 1.5 radian. Additionally, the first overtone of the QPO fundamental is detected, with its strength increasing with photon energy. Although limited statistics hinder precise lag determination for the overtone, indications suggest a similar soft-photon lag. During the QPO's absence, a broad noise component emerges below 10 keV, transforming into a near-QPO above this energy threshold with a frequency of approximately 3 Hz. The hard photons precede soft photons in this instance, suggesting a physical connection between the two features. Our findings are discussed within the framework of low-frequency QPOs in black-hole candidates, offering insights into accretion disk dynamics and the underlying physical mechanisms driving these phenomena. This study contributes to our understanding of QPO properties in black-hole systems, shedding light on the intricate relationships between accretion, disk structure, and X-ray emission.

This study investigates the nature of accretion flows in stellar-mass black holes residing in the low-hard state, with a focus on understanding jet formation and basic accretion disk physics. Through an X-ray analysis of eight black holes, we detect a thermal disk continuum with a color temperature consistent with expectations in all sources, even at low luminosities. Disk models indicate that the inner disk is not significantly truncated in six of the sources. Furthermore, iron-fluorescence line emission is observed in half of the sample, and detailed fits to the line profiles suggest that a truncated disk is unlikely. Our results show that none of the spectra exhibit strong evidence of disk truncation, defined as the non-detection of a broad iron line and an inner disk temperature much cooler than expected. These findings imply that the inner disk may evaporate at or below a certain luminosity threshold. This research provides new insights into the accretion flow dynamics in low-hard state black holes, shedding light on the interplay between the disk and jet components. By probing the radial extent of the inner disk through blackbody-like continuum emission and dynamically-broadened iron lines, we contribute to a deeper understanding of the underlying physics governing these complex systems.

The "ultraviolet upturn" (UVX) phenomenon, observed in elliptical galaxies and the bulges of spirals, is widely attributed to the presence of extremely hot horizontal branch (HB) stars and their progeny. However, the precise evolutionary pathways leading to the formation of these stars remain a topic of ongoing debate. This review highlights two crucial physical ingredients necessary for accurate quantitative models of the UV output of stellar populations: the mass loss rates of red giant branch stars and the helium enrichment law at high metallicities. Recent evidence suggests a strong enhancement of α-elements in the Galactic bulge and massive elliptical galaxies, implying a potentially higher helium abundance in these systems compared to spiral disks. This, in turn, would favor the production of hot HB stars at high metallicity in galactic spheroids. Furthermore, alternative mass loss recipes that better align with empirical data are discussed, which may promote the formation of extended HB stars at high metallicity. Additionally, new empirical evidence is presented, indicating that distinct evolutionary channels may be responsible for the production of extremely hot HB stars in field and cluster environments. By exploring these key ingredients and their implications, this review aims to shed light on the complex mechanisms underlying the UVX phenomenon and the formation of extremely hot HB stars in various astronomical contexts.

This study demonstrates the robustness of the neighbor-joining algorithm as a quartet method for constructing trees from distances. A new performance guarantee is established, encompassing Atteson's optimal radius bound. The guarantee explains the algorithm's success in cases where Atteson's criterion is not met. Additionally, a proof is provided for Atteson's conjecture on the optimal edge radius. The guarantees also apply to the fast neighbor-joining algorithm, enabling the inference of large phylogenies with theoretical backing, and supporting the use of neighbor-joining for constructing very large phylogenetic trees efficiently and accurately.

This article presents an efficient method for calculating Lyapunov exponents and eigenvectors in long-range interacting many-particle systems governed by the Vlasov equation. By expanding the distribution function using Hermite and Fourier modes with a scaling parameter, we achieve rapid convergence. This parameter is identified as the inverse system temperature, enabling accurate predictions of dynamics and linear stability in both near-equilibrium and far-from-equilibrium regimes using a limited number of expansion coefficients. The approach is demonstrated through an analysis of the Hamiltonian Mean-Field model, providing insights into the stability properties of its stationary states and showcasing the method's effectiveness in understanding complex many-particle systems.

This article introduces a class of punctured torus bundles, denoted as @xmath0, where all but finitely many Dehn fillings on @xmath2 are virtually Haken. We demonstrate that @xmath0 comprises infinitely many commensurability classes and provide evidence suggesting it encompasses representatives of most commensurability classes. An integer-valued complexity function is defined for monodromies, enabling the classification of punctured torus bundles. Utilizing computational methods, we establish that bundles with monodromy complexity of 5 or less are finitely covered by an element of @xmath0. Additionally, bundles with complexity of 12 or less are finitely covered, with a maximum of 36 exceptions. The article also presents a method for computing algebraic boundary slopes in specific finite covers, contributing to the understanding of punctured torus bundles.

The FACE (Faddeev with Core Excitation) program is a self-contained computational tool designed to solve the three-body Faddeev equations, enabling the inclusion of core excitation in one of the three bodies while keeping the other two inert. This program is particularly useful for calculating the binding energies and bound state structure compositions of light exotic nuclei treated as three-body systems, given the effective two-body interactions. The program allows for a wide range of forms for these interactions and can perform supersymmetric transformations of the potentials when two-body states need to be removed due to Pauli blocking. The FACE program is written in Fortran-90 and is designed to run on any Unix/Linux workstation or PC. It requires 9 MB of RAM memory and 12 MB of hard disk space, and can be compiled independently using the included source code for six routines from the NAG and BLAS libraries. The program calculates eigenenergies and eigenstates for the three-body problem by solving the Faddeev equations, using a hyperspherical coordinate system and expanding the three-body wavefunction in a series of Jacobi polynomials and a Laguerre basis. The program's method of solution involves calculating the three-body matrix elements and completing the full three-body Hamiltonian matrix, followed by a diagonalization process to determine the energies. The program also reconstructs the three-body wavefunction and calculates other bound state observables. The typical running time for the program is 6 seconds on a 1.7 GHz Intel P4-processor machine. The FACE program is a valuable tool for researchers studying light exotic nuclei and the three-body problem, providing a flexible and efficient way to calculate binding energies and bound state structure compositions. Its ability to include core excitation and perform supersymmetric transformations makes it a powerful tool for understanding the complex interactions between particles in these systems. With its user-friendly design and fast running time, the FACE program is an essential resource for anyone working in this field.

This article explores fully commutative involutions in Coxeter groups, characterized using Viennot's heaps. By representing heaps as Dyck-type lattice walks, we enumerate fully commutative involutions by length for all classical finite and affine Coxeter groups. For finite cases, explicit generating functions are derived with respect to the major index. Additionally, in affine type, connections are made to Fan and Green's cell structure of the corresponding Temperley-Lieb algebra, providing new insights into the properties of fully commutative involutions and their relationship to algebraic structures. Enumeration results and generating functions are presented.

We prove any admissible harmonic Ritz value set is achievable for prescribed GMRES residual norms, complementing existing results and broadening understanding of harmonic Ritz values and GMRES convergence.

This study investigates the effects of uniform acceleration on entanglement and quantum teleportation in non-orthogonal states. We demonstrate that accelerated parties exhibit enhanced entanglement and achieve higher fidelity for teleportation compared to non-accelerated parties. By analyzing the behavior of a quantum field in a Rindler wedge, we show that tracing over causally disconnected field modes deforms the effective state space of a qubit derived from scalar field modes. Using numerical calculations of the Bures angle and deriving the Bures metric for low accelerations, we illustrate the deformation of the qubit's state space. Furthermore, we calculate the scalar curvature of the effective Bures metric, revealing a loss of isotropy. Notably, our results remain relevant even in the context of large gravitational fields, despite being derived in the limit of low accelerations. These findings have significant implications for our understanding of quantum information processing in relativistic regimes.

This article examines asymptotically flat spacetimes possessing a single Killing vector field, utilizing polyhomogeneous expansions to solve the Killing equations asymptotically. By analyzing the leading terms of these expansions, the asymptotic form of the Killing vector field is determined. The potential classes of Killing fields are categorized based on their orbits on null infinity. The integrability conditions of the Killing equations impose constraints on the Weyl tensor components and shear, which are subsequently analyzed. For non-supertranslational Killing fields, it is demonstrated that the characteristics of the constraint equations coincide with the orbits of the restricted Killing field on null infinity. As a specific application, the case of boost-rotation symmetric spacetimes is investigated, where constraints on the Weyl tensor component are used to study the behavior of coefficients related to the Newman-Penrose constants. This research provides insights into the properties of asymptotically flat spacetimes with a single Killing vector field, shedding light on their geometric and physical characteristics. The findings have implications for our understanding of spacetime structure and the behavior of gravitational fields in various astrophysical contexts.

This article presents a comparative analysis of the discrepancies in simulation results between the two most widely used Monte Carlo programs, PRESHOWER and MAGICS, for the propagation of ultra-high energy cosmic ray photons in the presence of the geomagnetic field. The discovery of photons in the cosmic ray flux at the highest energies is anticipated within the next few years, according to conventional models, and reliable simulation software is essential for accurate predictions. We focus on the "preshower effect," where high-energy photons interact with the geomagnetic field, generating a cascade of particles above the atmosphere, which significantly influences air shower evolution. Our study reveals notable discrepancies between the results produced by PRESHOWER, used in CORSIKA, and MAGICS, used in AIRES, for photon energies above 10^20 eV. These findings have important implications for full Monte Carlo simulations of ultra-high energy cosmic ray photons and highlight the need for well-maintained and reliable software. By identifying and addressing these discrepancies, this research aims to improve the accuracy of preshower simulations, ultimately enhancing our understanding of extensive air showers and geomagnetic cascading. The results of this study are crucial for the interpretation of data from current and future cosmic ray detectors.

This article presents a significant development in the quasiclassical theory of nonequilibrium superconductors, specifically focusing on spin-dependent scattering near magnetic interfaces. By formulating the Riccati equations for the quasiclassical theory, we derive novel boundary conditions for the Riccati distribution functions at a spin-active interface. These boundary conditions are expressed in terms of an interface S-matrix, which encapsulates the effects of spin-filtering and spin-mixing by a ferromagnetic interface. The S-matrix provides a comprehensive description of the reflection and transmission of normal-state conduction electrons by the interface, enabling the calculation of various nonequilibrium transport properties in hybrid systems of superconducting and magnetic materials. We demonstrate the applicability of these boundary conditions by calculating the spin and charge conductance of a normal metal-ferromagnet-superconductor point contact, as well as the phase-modulated thermal conductance of a superconducting-ferromagnetic-superconducting point contact. Our results reveal a dramatic difference in the phase modulation of thermal conductance for high-transparency junctions compared to non-magnetic junctions. Furthermore, we find that low-transparency tunnel junctions with weak spin mixing exhibit an increase in thermal conductance over a broad temperature range when the superconducting phase bias is π. These findings have significant implications for the understanding and design of hybrid superconducting-magnetic devices, and highlight the importance of considering spin-dependent scattering and spin-mixing effects in the analysis of nonequilibrium transport properties.

The detection of gravitational microlensing events towards the Galactic bulge has become a prolific method for discovering exoplanetary systems. By concentrating on high-magnification events, we demonstrate that the probability of detecting Jupiter-mass planets or greater within the lensing zone (0.6-1.6 AU) approaches nearly 100%. Furthermore, the likelihood of detection remains substantial for Saturn-mass planets and significant even for planets with masses as low as 10 Earth masses. This high probability enables a definitive statement to be made about the existence of planets within the lensing zone for each system that undergoes high magnification. Although the light curve deviations caused by the source passing near the primary lens caustic may be expected to be small due to the large distance of the perturbing planet, the high magnification overcomes this effect. While high-magnification events are relatively rare, occurring in approximately 1/10th of events with peak magnifications greater than 20, they occur regularly and can be predicted in advance. This predictability allows for the detection of exoplanets using a relatively small allocation of resources over a limited period, making high-magnification events an attractive target for future exoplanetary surveys. Our findings highlight the potential of gravitational microlensing as a powerful tool for exoplanet detection and characterization.

We examine the 3D quantum many-body dynamics of a dilute Bose gas with strong confining in one direction. The corresponding BBGKY hierarchy exhibits a diverging coefficient as the confining potential strength tends to zero. However, we show that this divergence is counterbalanced by the density matrices' limiting structure, ensuring convergence of the hierarchy to a 2D cubic NLS with an exactly derived 3D to 2D coupling constant.

This article extends the structural default model to a multi-bank setting with interbank liabilities, where assets are driven by correlated Lévy processes. A novel computational method is introduced, generalizing the fractional partial differential equation approach to higher dimensions. This method achieves unconditional stability and second-order accuracy in space and time, with linear complexity for popular Lévy models. The approach is applied to compute marginal and joint survival probabilities for two and three banks with mutual liabilities. Numerical examples illustrate the impact of interbank liabilities on default probabilities, providing insights into the effects of mutual exposures on bank stability and highlighting the importance of considering correlated risk factors in default modeling.

We present the current status of leptoquark searches, utilizing next leading order theoretical predictions for pair production at hadron colliders. An optimized analysis for first generation leptoquarks yields increased sensitivity. Derived mass limits are relevant to recent high mass events at HERA, providing new insights into leptoquark physics and its potential implications for beyond Standard Model theories, with significant improvements over earlier searches.

This article presents a novel synaptic weight update rule for learning precise spike train transformations in multilayer feedforward networks of spiking neurons. Our framework generalizes error backpropagation to the deterministic spiking neuron setting, relying solely on spike timing and avoiding concepts related to spike rates or probabilistic spiking models. The derivation is based on two key innovations: an error functional that compares output and desired spike trains through their impact on a virtual postsynaptic neuron, and a virtual assignment of weights to spikes rather than synapses, enabling perturbation analysis of individual spike times and synaptic weights. This yields gradients of the error functional, which are used in a gradient descent mechanism to update weights. Simulation experiments demonstrate the efficacy of our learning framework, highlighting its ability to learn complex spike train transformations. Notably, the experiments also reveal asymmetries between synapses on excitatory and inhibitory neurons, underscoring the importance of considering neuronal type in synaptic plasticity. Overall, our work provides a foundation for learning precise spike timing in multilayer spiking neural networks, with implications for understanding neural computation and developing more efficient neural network models. The proposed framework has potential applications in neuromorphic computing and artificial intelligence.

This study investigates the excited states of 4He using four-body calculations with explicitly correlated Gaussian bases. The results demonstrate a reasonable reproduction of all levels below 26MeV using realistic potentials. A detailed analysis reveals the mechanism by which the 0+ state becomes a resonance, while similar states in other spin-isospin channels do not exhibit resonance behavior. The crucial role of the tensor force is highlighted, particularly in relation to the level spacing between the two 2+ states. Calculations of spectroscopic amplitudes and transition strengths indicate that the 0+ state and negative-parity states have distinct cluster configurations, suggesting an interpretation as inversion doublet partners. These findings provide new insights into the structure and properties of 4He excited states. The results have significant implications for our understanding of nuclear cluster configurations and resonance phenomena.

This article delves into the challenges of implementing reliable and efficient geometric algorithms, which are hindered by the conflict between the need for precise arithmetic and the demand for computational speed. Controlled perturbation algorithms offer a solution by combining the efficiency of floating-point arithmetic with a reliability mechanism. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis tool box for controlled perturbation algorithms, comprising independent components that facilitate the derivation of crucial bounds. Three distinct approaches for bound derivation are introduced, enabling flexibility in the analysis. Furthermore, the concept of controlled perturbation is expanded to incorporate rational function-based predicates, in addition to polynomial-based predicates, and object-preserving perturbations are introduced. The tool box is designed to accurately reflect the behavior of the algorithm without simplifying assumptions, providing a robust framework for performance analysis. By addressing numerical robustness problems and providing a reliable geometric computing framework, this research contributes to the development of efficient and trustworthy geometric algorithms, ultimately enhancing the accuracy and speed of floating-point computations in various applications. The presented tool box has significant implications for the field, enabling the creation of more robust and efficient geometric algorithms.

This study investigates the impact of electromagnetically generated vortex flow on parametrically amplified surface waves. The vortex flow creates nonlinear interactions with standing waves, altering the bifurcation diagram and power spectrum density. Results show the parametric instability threshold increases with vortex flow intensity, shedding light on complex wave dynamics and nonlinear interactions in fluid systems.

This study investigates the formation of the thick disk in the Milky Way galaxy by analyzing the elemental abundances of metal-poor stars. Using data from the RAVE spectroscopic survey, we selected a sample of 243 metal-poor stars, including 212 red giant branch and 31 red clump/horizontal branch stars. We measured the abundances of four alpha-elements (Mg, Si, Ca, Ti) and iron, and found that the [alpha/Fe] ratios are enhanced, indicating enrichment by core-collapse supernovae. The uniformity of these ratios suggests efficient mixing in the interstellar medium prior to star formation. The similarity between the abundance patterns of the thick disk and the halo implies a shared initial mass function for massive stars. Our results suggest that the formation of the thick disk was not significantly influenced by the direct accretion of stars from dwarf galaxies, contradicting some theories of thick disk formation. Instead, our findings support a scenario in which the thick disk formed through a rapid star formation process, with good mixing of elements in the interstellar medium. These conclusions have important implications for our understanding of the formation and evolution of the Milky Way galaxy.

We calculate the electromagnetic form factors of a bound proton using the chiral quark-soliton model. Embedding the proton in nuclear matter yields significant modifications to the form factors. Valence quark effects are mitigated by sea quarks, resulting in a 20% decrease in the isoscalar electric to isovector magnetic form factor ratio at nuclear density. The magnetic moment shows no strong enhancement, providing insight into the proton's behavior in nuclear environments.

We define twist-2 operator matrix elements for non-singlet parton densities within the Schrödinger Functional scheme. A lattice one-loop calculation establishes the relation to other schemes, identifying lattice artefacts. This sets the basis for a numerical evaluation of parton density running, enabling non-perturbative studies of their behavior.

This study examines the emergence of strange baryons during the dynamical collapse of a non-rotating massive star into a black hole, utilizing neutrino-radiation hydrodynamical simulations within the framework of general relativity. By tracking the formation and collapse of a nascent proto-neutron star from a 40M⊙ star, we employ a novel hyperonic equation of state (EOS) table. Our findings indicate that hyperons are absent at core bounce but rapidly populate approximately 0.5-0.7 seconds post-bounce, triggering a re-collapse into a black hole. Initially, hyperons appear off-center due to high temperatures, eventually dominating at the core as central density increases. Notably, neutrino emission from the accreting proto-neutron star with a hyperonic EOS ceases significantly earlier than with a nucleonic EOS, while average energies and luminosities remain comparable. These distinctive neutrino signal characteristics may serve as a probe for the emergence of new degrees of freedom within the collapse forming a black hole, offering insights into the underlying physics of such catastrophic events.

This study utilizes data from the H.E.S.S. array of Cherenkov telescopes, collected between 2004 and 2007, to survey the inner galactic plane at photon energies above 100 GeV. The accumulated 400 hours of data cover a region of -30 to +60 degrees in galactic longitude and -3 to +3 degrees in galactic latitude. Assuming weakly interacting massive particles comprise dark matter, we calculated the H.E.S.S. sensitivity map for dark matter annihilations. Our analysis derives the first experimental constraints on the mini-spikes scenario, where gamma-ray signals arise from dark matter annihilation around intermediate-mass black holes. The results exclude this scenario at a 90% confidence level for dark matter particles with a velocity-weighted annihilation cross section above a certain threshold and mass between 800 GeV and 10 TeV, providing new insights into dark matter properties.

This paper presents a unifying variational approach to prove fundamental information theoretic inequalities. Using calculus of variations, we reinterpret and prove key results, including entropy maximization and Fisher information minimization. Applications and extensions of these findings are discussed, offering new insights into information theory and its connections to variational methods, with implications for entropy, noise, and inequality analysis.

This article presents a derivation of extremal black hole solutions in various four-dimensional models, which can be reduced to 3D gravity coupled to a sigma model with a symmetric target space via Kaluza-Klein reduction. We establish a correspondence between these solutions and specific nilpotent generators of the isometry group. Notably, an exact solution is provided for a non-BPS black hole with generic charges and asymptotic moduli in N=2 supergravity coupled to one vector multiplet. Additionally, our technique enables the generation of multi-centered solutions. A key finding is that non-supersymmetric solutions lack the complex moduli space of bound configurations characteristic of supersymmetric cases, offering new insights into black hole physics.

This study examines the implications of perturbing symmetric four and three zero neutrino Yukawa textures with the most general lowest-order symmetry breaking terms, within the Type-I seesaw framework. Assuming real and diagonal charged lepton and heavy neutrino mass matrices, we demonstrate that small symmetry breaking parameters can accommodate current best-fit ranges of neutrino mass squared differences and mixing angles. Notably, an inverted mass ordering for all light neutrinos allows for a value of θ13 within the observed range. Our analysis provides insight into the viability of four and three zero textures in the context of broken μ-τ symmetry, shedding light on neutrino mass generation mechanisms.

This study employs the perturbative QCD factorization approach to calculate branching ratios and direct CP-violating asymmetries for @xmath0 and @xmath1 decays. The results suggest that the 2-quark model for the light scalar meson @xmath2 cannot be excluded by current experimental limits. Notably, the @xmath3 decay exhibits the largest branching ratio, @xmath4, but the smallest direct CP asymmetry, @xmath5. Although significant direct CP asymmetries, approximately @xmath7, are found for @xmath6 decays, their small branching ratios, around @xmath8, render them challenging to measure experimentally, highlighting the need for further investigation.

Title: Unveiling the Mysteries of GRB 120326A: An Unusual Gamma-Ray Burst with Prolonged Plateau and Late Re-brightening Abstract: GRB 120326A is a peculiar gamma-ray burst (GRB) characterized by an unusually long plateau phase and a late re-brightening in both X-ray and optical bands. The synchronized behavior of the optical and X-ray light curves suggests a common origin, sparking intrigue among astronomers. Our analysis delves into the energy injection model, exploring both wind and interstellar medium (ISM) environments for GRB afterglows. We investigate the impact of injection parameters, including starting and ending times, stellar wind density, and injection luminosity, on the afterglow light curves. The results reveal that the wind model is heavily influenced by these parameters, exhibiting a distinctive "bump" at late times. Notably, the duration of energy injection directly affects the prominence of the re-brightening, while the peak time is determined by the stellar wind density. By applying the late continuous injection model, we successfully fit the observational data of GRB 120326A, requiring an injection time scale exceeding 10,000 seconds. This, in turn, implies that the central engine activity must persist for over 10,000 seconds, providing valuable constraints on GRB central engines. Our findings support the notion of a newly formed millisecond pulsar with a strong magnetic field as the central engine. Furthermore, the circumburst environment of GRB 120326A is likely dominated by a stellar wind, shedding light on the progenitor properties of this enigmatic event. This study contributes to our understanding of GRB physics, highlighting the complexities of central engine activity and the significance of the surrounding environment in shaping the observed phenomenology.

This study presents a quantum mechanical analysis of the pendular cavity using the positive-P representation, revealing the significant impact of the moving mirror's quantum state on the system's dynamics. Contrary to previous proposals, our findings indicate that the oscillating mirror exhibits perpetual motion, lacks a stationary steady-state, and displays substantial uncertainties in position and momentum. These uncertainties typically surpass the mean values, rendering linearised fluctuation analyses ineffective in predicting highly quantum states. Furthermore, our results show that the achievable measurement accuracy is severely compromised by thermal noise, exceeding the standard quantum limit even at extremely low temperatures. This research highlights the limitations of previous approaches and underscores the need for a more nuanced understanding of the interplay between quantum mechanics and macroscopic objects in the pendular cavity system. Our findings have significant implications for the development of quantum-limited measurement techniques and the creation of entangled states.

This study explores the application of Faraday tomography in probing the distribution of magnetic fields along the line of sight (LOS), with a focus on overcoming the challenges posed by turbulent magnetic field components. By analyzing the Faraday spectrum along multiple lines of sight (LOS) within a small, uniform region of the sky, we demonstrate a method to interpret the Faraday depth and physical depth relationship. Using face-on spiral galaxies as a model, we simulate the turbulent magnetic field as a random field with a single coherence length and calculate the Faraday spectrum and its shape-characterizing parameters, such as moments of the spectrum. Our results show that when multiple LOS cover a region of sufficient size, the Faraday spectrum becomes smooth and its parameters are well-defined. We express these parameters in terms of the regular and turbulent components of the LOS magnetic field and the coherence length, using a Gaussian function representation of the Faraday spectrum. Additionally, we investigate the effects of power-law spectra on the turbulent magnetic field and its revelation in the Faraday spectrum. While our work requires further refinement to account for observational effects and more realistic models, it provides a promising approach to extracting magnetic field information using Faraday tomography, paving the way for a deeper understanding of the magnetic field distribution in the universe.

This study addresses the significant uncertainty in determining microlensing parameters caused by source star image blending in dense star fields, such as the Galactic Bulge and Magellanic Clouds. Current experiments attempt to correct for blending effects by introducing a residual flux parameter, but this approach is hindered by large uncertainties due to parameter degeneracies. To mitigate this issue, we propose utilizing the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) to resolve blended source star images. By combining HST's high resolving power with color information from ground-based observations, we can uniquely identify the lensed source star, thereby reducing uncertainty in derived time scales. This approach has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy of microlensing parameter determination, enabling more precise analyses of lensing events in dense star fields. The use of HST offers a promising solution to the blending problem, enhancing our understanding of microlensing phenomena.

Title: Abelian Powers and Repetitions in Sturmian Words: Maximum Exponents and Critical Exponents Abstract: This article improves upon the result of Richomme, Saari, and Zamboni (2011) by investigating the maximum exponents of abelian powers and abelian repetitions in Sturmian words. We derive a formula for calculating the maximum exponent of an abelian power with a given abelian period starting at any position in a Sturmian word of rotation angle α. By considering all possible abelian periods, we recover the result of Richomme, Saari, and Zamboni. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of the abelian critical exponent of a Sturmian word, denoted as γ(α), which represents the supremum of the maximum exponents of abelian powers and abelian repetitions. We demonstrate that γ(α) equals the Lagrange constant of the number α, providing a formula for its computation in terms of the partial quotients of the continued fraction expansion of α. Using this formula, we establish that γ(α) is finite if and only if α has bounded partial quotients. Additionally, we investigate the properties of the infinite Fibonacci word and derive formulas for the longest prefix that is an abelian repetition of a given period and the minimum abelian period of any factor. Our results contribute to a deeper understanding of the combinatorial properties of Sturmian words and their connections to number theory. The findings of this article have implications for the study of abelian powers and repetitions in other types of words and sequences, and highlight the importance of the abelian critical exponent as a fundamental parameter in the analysis of Sturmian words.

This review examines the intricate relationship between binary companions and activity in OB stars, with a focus on the Be phenomenon. We explore the binary channel for Be star formation and discuss its contribution to the overall Be star population. Evidence suggests that certain environments favor the appearance of Be stars, potentially linked to initial conditions such as chemical composition or rotational velocities. By investigating these connections, we shed light on the fundamental role of multiplicity in shaping Be star activity and the potential implications for our understanding of these complex systems. Key findings and ongoing discussions are presented.

This article revisits the seminal work of Sick and collaborators on electron scattering from 3He and 4He, which reported a depression in the central point nucleon density 20 years ago. Using wave functions from few-body calculations with realistic potentials, we achieve good fits to the helium charge distributions by assuming an expansion of the proton charge size towards the nucleus center. Our results are discussed in relation to 6-quark chromo-dielectric model calculations. Notably, the expansion exceeds predictions from mean field bag calculations and our own calculations using the independent pair approximation. This study contributes to the ongoing search for evidence of quark substructure, with potential implications for our understanding of nuclear physics. The findings have significant implications for the field, shedding new light on the properties of helium nuclei and the behavior of protons within them.

This study investigates the role of triplet states in photorelaxation dynamics using mixed quantum-classical dynamics simulations with the SHARC method. Ultrafast intersystem crossing processes, driven by spin-orbit coupling, occur on a timescale below 100 fs, competing with internal conversion. Comparing singlet-triplet dynamics to singlet-only dynamics reveals distinct differences in state populations. However, vibrational motion in the triplet manifold closely resembles that in the singlet manifold, suggesting that triplet state contributions may be challenging to detect in various experiments. These findings highlight the importance of considering triplet states in photorelaxation dynamics simulations to accurately capture the underlying mechanisms.

This article explores the potential of hybrid imaging techniques that combine the high contrast of electrical or optical properties with the high resolution of ultrasound. The mathematical framework for these modalities involves reconstructing a diffusion coefficient from knowledge of a solution to an elliptic equation. This inverse problem can be recast as a nonlinear equation, specifically a p-Laplacian, which is a variational elliptic nonlinear equation. However, the limiting case of p=1 has a convex but not strictly convex functional, while the case of p=∞ admits a non-convex variational formulation. To address this challenge, we augment the p-Laplacian equation with full Cauchy data at the domain's boundary, resulting in a formally overdetermined nonlinear hyperbolic equation. Our paper presents existence, uniqueness, and stability results for the Cauchy problem of the p-Laplacian. We show that the diffusion coefficient can be stably reconstructed on a subset of the domain, described as the domain of influence of the space-like part of the boundary for an appropriate Lorentzian metric. Additionally, we analyze global reconstructions for specific geometries and explore the construction of complex geometric optics solutions, providing new insights into the development of hybrid imaging techniques. Our results contribute to the advancement of ultrasound modulation of electrical or optical properties, enabling the creation of high-contrast, high-resolution imaging modalities.

We present a detailed calculation of the leading order perturbative QCD and power corrections to the hadronic invariant mass and hadron energy spectra in the decay of a heavy meson within the Standard Model framework. Utilizing the Heavy Quark Expansion Technique (HQET) and a perturbative QCD-improved Fermi Motion (FM) model, which incorporates meson wave-function effects, we find that the corrections to the hadron energy spectrum are relatively small across a significant portion of the spectrum in both methods. However, the HQET expansion fails to converge near the lower kinematic endpoint and at the threshold due to limitations in the expansion. The hadronic invariant mass spectrum, calculable only within a limited range using HQET, exhibits a similar behavior. We also compute the first two hadronic moments, analyzing their sensitivity to HQET and FM model parameters and finding a remarkable agreement between the two methods for equivalent parameter values. Furthermore, we derive constraints on HQET parameters based on assumed values of the first moment and discuss how forthcoming B-factory data could be used to measure short-distance contributions and constrain these parameters. Additionally, we investigate the impact of experimental cuts on branching ratios, hadron spectra, and hadronic invariant mass moments using the FM model, providing insights relevant to recent searches for specific decays. Our work contributes to a deeper understanding of heavy meson decays and the development of more precise models for hadronic spectra and invariant mass distributions.

This study presents evidence for the recent evolution of relaxation processes in galaxy clusters, utilizing extensive optical and X-ray cluster samples. Cluster relaxation is assessed through ellipticity, intracluster medium temperature, and X-ray luminosity. Our analysis reveals significant variations in these indicators with redshift, supporting the notion that clusters have ceased major mergers and accretion, consistent with a low-density universe. Instead, they are undergoing gravitational relaxation, characterized by reduced flattening, intracluster medium temperature, and X-ray luminosity. These findings corroborate recent claims by Melott, Chambers, and Miller, providing new insights into the evolution of galaxy clusters.

This paper investigates short homologically and homotopically independent loops based at the same point on Riemannian surfaces and metric graphs. We establish that every closed Riemannian surface of genus 0 and area 1 contains at least 2 homotopically independent loops of length at most 3, where 4 is a universal constant. This result improves upon Gromov's theorem and refines Sabourau's proof on the separating systole. Additionally, we show that every connected metric graph of first Betti number 9 and length 9 contains at least 10 homologically independent loops based at the same point and of length at most 11. This extends the bound on the homological systole to at least 12 homologically independent loops. We also provide examples of graphs where this result is optimal, demonstrating the sharpness of our bounds. Our work contributes to the understanding of geometric and topological properties of Riemannian surfaces and metric graphs, with implications for various fields, including geometry, topology, and graph theory. Overall, our findings offer new insights into the structure and properties of these mathematical objects.

This paper introduces a novel search-driven framework for acquiring documents for scientific portals, leveraging publicly available research paper titles and author names as queries to a web search engine. Our approach utilizes accurate classification modules to identify research papers and sources from search results. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the performance of individual classifiers and the overall framework's effectiveness. Notably, our fully automated framework yielded approximately 10 million research documents using around 1 million queries. These results suggest that web search can serve as a viable alternative to traditional crawl-based methods for acquiring documents and seed URLs for future crawls. By harnessing the power of web search, our framework offers a promising solution for efficiently populating open-access digital libraries, ultimately enhancing the discovery and accessibility of scientific knowledge. Our findings have significant implications for the development of scientific portals and digital libraries.

The formation and evolution of elliptical galaxies (EGs) remains an unresolved question, with recent observations indicating that these galaxies are more complex than previously thought. This study examines a sample of 487 elliptical galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey to investigate star-forming activity in local EGs.
